# Network Operations Help Desk Concept of Operations

This memorandum details the concept of operations for the new 24/7 Network Operations Help Desk at 26 NOS. The mission of this initiative is to provide round-the-clock support for network operations, ensuring continuous operational capabilities and rapid incident response. The help desk will serve as a critical point of contact to streamline support, enhance communication, and minimize downtime across our networks.

Manning for the Help Desk team will be carefully structured to ensure full coverage during all operational hours. The initial roster includes key personnel who will be responsible for shifts and escalation procedures. The team members are:

> SSgt John A. Smith\
> Sgt Lisa B. Taylor\
> Tech Sgt Michael C. Johnson\
> MSgt Robert D. Lee

Operational hours for the Help Desk will be 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, including holidays, to meet the support needs of our users. This ensures help is always available regardless of time zone or day, facilitating rapid response times and ongoing support.

Escalation procedures are established to ensure complex issues are promptly addressed. Incidents that cannot be resolved at the initial point of contact will be escalated to designated senior personnel, including higher-level network engineers or the on-duty network operations manager, to expedite resolution.

A formal review and feedback process will be instituted to evaluate the effectiveness of the Help Desk operations and identify areas for improvement. All stakeholders are encouraged to submit comments by 15 March 2026, which will be incorporated into the final operational plan, ensuring alignment with mission objectives and user needs.

The 26th Network Operations Squadron (26 NOS) is implementing a new 24/7 Network Operations Help Desk to enhance mission support and ensure continuous operational readiness for the 67th Cyber Wing. This help desk will serve as the first point of contact for all network operation-related issues, providing timely response and resolution to minimize system downtime and impact on mission-critical functions. This initiative supports the Wings commitment to maintaining superior network operations and cybersecurity defense capabilities around the clock.

Manning for the help desk will include a dedicated team of four qualified personnel who will staff all shifts to guarantee uninterrupted coverage. The primary roster for initial operations is as follows:

> SSgt EMILY J. RIVERA, NCOIC, Help Desk  \
> A1C JAMES T. NGUYEN, Cyber Operator  \
> SrA MARIA L. SANDERS, Cyber Operator  \
> SrA TREVOR P. JACOBS, Cyber Operator

The help desk will operate 24 hours per day, 7 days a week, ensuring continuous monitoring and swift issue response. Shift schedules are designed to provide seamless handovers and maintain situational awareness among the help desk operators. Service hours will cover all standard and non-standard duty periods to support network operations without interruption.

Issue escalation procedures have been established to manage incidents that exceed the help desks resolution capability. Initial troubleshoots will be conducted by help desk personnel, escalating unresolved or critical issues promptly to the 26 NOS Network Operations Center and supporting cybersecurity teams. Clear escalation protocols will ensure rapid decision-making and resource allocation to restore network functionality efficiently.

All units and stakeholders are requested to review this concept of operations and provide comments or recommendations by 15 March 2026. Feedback should be sent directly to the 26 NOS/CC office to incorporate necessary adjustments prior to full implementation. This collaborative approach will ensure the help desk fully meets the operational needs of the 67th Cyber Wing and its mission partners.

This memorandum publishes the Concept of Operations (CONOPS) for a new 24/7 Network Operations Help Desk (NOHD) to be established by 26th Network Operations Squadron (26 NOS) in support of 67th Wing network availability, cybersecurity response, and end-user support. The NOHD mission is to provide continuous centralized triage, first-level troubleshooting, incident intake, and escalation for network and cyber-related issues across 67 CW, reducing mean time to acknowledge and supporting wing mission assurance.

The NOHD manning model will be a blend of 26 NOS civilian and military personnel staffed in three shifts to ensure around-the-clock coverage. Core responsibilities include incident intake and categorization, remote remediation where possible, coordination with on-call system owners, and documentation of tickets in the service management system. Key staffing positions and initial roster are:

> SSgt MARIA L. TORRES, USAF\
> A1C JOHN P. REYES, USAF\
> CIV JANE K. DOE, DAF\
> CIV MARK T. OLSON, DAF

Shift coverage hours are: primary shift 0600–1800, secondary shift 1800–0000, and night shift 0000–0600, with overlap windows for shift turnover and peak-hours surge capacity. The help desk telephone and chat channels will be staffed 24/7; an automated ticket intake process will record after-hours reports and assign priority codes for next-shift handling when immediate response is not required.

Escalation procedures will follow a tiered approach to ensure timely resolution and appropriate engagement of subject-matter experts. The escalation ladder is:

- Tier 1: NOHD technician — initial triage, basic remediation, and ticketing.

- Tier 2: On-call 26 NOS systems administrators/network engineers — complex troubleshooting and remote fixes.

- Tier 3: 67 CW/A3 and external vendor support — major incidents, outages, or hardware replacements.

Within each tier, actions are prioritized as follows:

a. Priority 1 — mission-critical outage or compromise: immediate notification to 67 CW/A3 and mobilization of Tier 2/3 resources. b. Priority 2 — degraded mission capability or significant security concern: NOHD escalation to on-call SMEs within 30 minutes. c. Priority 3 — routine user-impacting issues: documented and scheduled for remediation during normal maintenance windows unless otherwise directed.

Operational metrics will measure time-to-acknowledge, time-to-resolution, ticket backlog, and customer satisfaction. NOHD leadership will produce a weekly report for 67 CW/A3 that highlights trends, recurring faults, and recommended mitigations. Training, knowledge-base updates, and exercises will be scheduled quarterly to maintain proficiency across shifts and ensure consistent execution of standard operating procedures.

Point of contact for this CONOPS is the undersigned at 26 NOS/CC. Request comments, recommended edits, and concurrence be provided no later than 15 March 2026; please route responses to 26 NOS/CC and copy 67 CW/A3. This CONOPS is effective on publication and will be reviewed after 90 days for adjustments based on operational feedback.

The NOHD manning model will be a blend of 26 NOS civilian and military personnel staffed in three shifts to ensure around-the-clock coverage. Core responsibilities include incident intake and categorization, remote remediation where possible, coordination with on-call system owners, and documentation of tickets in the service management system. Key staffing positions and initial roster are:

> SSgt MARIA L. TORRES, USAF\
> A1C JOHN P. REYES, USAF\
> CIV JANE K. DOE, DAF\
> CIV MARK T. OLSON, DAF

Shift coverage hours are: primary shift 0600–1800, secondary shift 1800–0000, and night shift 0000–0600, with overlap windows for shift turnover and peak-hours surge capacity. The help desk telephone and chat channels will be staffed 24/7; an automated ticket intake process will record after-hours reports and assign priority codes for next-shift handling when immediate response is not required.

Escalation procedures will follow a tiered approach to ensure timely resolution and appropriate engagement of subject-matter experts. The escalation ladder is:

- Tier 1: NOHD technician — initial triage, basic remediation, and ticketing.

- Tier 2: On-call 26 NOS systems administrators/network engineers — complex troubleshooting and remote fixes.

- Tier 3: 67 CW/A3 and external vendor support — major incidents, outages, or hardware replacements.

Within each tier, actions are prioritized as follows:

a. Priority 1 — mission-critical outage or compromise: immediate notification to 67 CW/A3 and mobilization of Tier 2/3 resources. b. Priority 2 — degraded mission capability or significant security concern: NOHD escalation to on-call SMEs within 30 minutes. c. Priority 3 — routine user-impacting issues: documented and scheduled for remediation during normal maintenance windows unless otherwise directed.

Operational metrics will measure time-to-acknowledge, time-to-resolution, ticket backlog, and customer satisfaction. NOHD leadership will produce a weekly report for 67 CW/A3 that highlights trends, recurring faults, and recommended mitigations. Training, knowledge-base updates, and exercises will be scheduled quarterly to maintain proficiency across shifts and ensure consistent execution of standard operating procedures.

Point of contact for this CONOPS is the undersigned at 26 NOS/CC. Request comments, recommended edits, and concurrence be provided no later than 15 March 2026; please route responses to 26 NOS/CC and copy 67 CW/A3. This CONOPS is effective on publication and will be reviewed after 90 days for adjustments based on operational feedback.

The intent of this memorandum is to establish standardized packaging requirements for retrograde cargo moving through Air Force channels. These standards apply to retrograde shipments tendered for return, repair disposition, or restock processing.

Effective immediately, organizations must use approved packaging configurations that protect materiel from damage during handling, transport, and storage. Ensure outer packaging is capable of supporting the maximum anticipated load, complies with labeling requirements, and includes any required protective materials for the specific cargo type.

Units and logistics activities must coordinate any exceptions, operational waivers, or questions regarding packaging selection through their supporting logistics channels. Requests for changes to these standards should include failure data, current packaging configuration, and the proposed mitigation to ensure timely resolution.

Effective immediately, the 355th Operations Group will conduct a stand-down to reset operational risk management (ORM) practices across the group. The stand-down will provide commanders, supervisors, and Airmen time to review current ORM expectations, identify recurring risk-management gaps, and reinforce deliberate risk assessment before mission execution.

The 355 OG/CC will coordinate the stand-down schedule and ensure each unit completes a focused ORM reset appropriate to its mission. Training and mission-essential activities may continue when required, provided risks are assessed and accepted at the appropriate level.

Return a summary of completed actions, identified systemic concerns, and recommended follow-up measures to the 355 FW/CC through the 355 OG/CC no later than 2026-08-21. This reset is intended to strengthen our operational discipline and preserve the safety and readiness of the wing.

This memorandum announces mandatory packaging standards for retrograde cargo processed within HQ AFMC/A4-managed facilities. All organizational elements under ALMAJCOM/A4 shall comply with the packaging, labeling, and documentation requirements detailed below to ensure safe, accountable, and transportable retrograde shipments.

Packaging must protect items from damage during handling and transport, prevent contamination, and meet surface and air shipment constraints. Use certified packing materials, internal cushioning appropriate to the item's fragility, and outer containers rated for the cargo weight and mode of transport. Affix durable labels showing origin, destination, handling instructions, and any applicable hazard or CUI markings.

Compliance will be enforced by periodic inspections and during retrograde processing. Report deviations, damaged shipments, or questions to the HQ AFMC/A4 Logistics office via established channels. These standards are effective immediately and remain in force until superseded.

This memorandum announces a unit-wide stand-down to reset Operational Risk Management (ORM) processes. All personnel will participate in required ORM training and unit-level reviews to reinforce risk identification, mitigation, and reporting procedures.

1. Purpose. Reset ORM practices across the wing to reduce risk exposure and ensure consistent application of ORM principles.

2. Scope. Applies to all 355th Wing and subordinate units.

3. Actions.

- Unit commanders will schedule and conduct ORM training and risk assessments for their personnel within seven duty days of this memorandum.

- Supervisors will document completed training and any identified hazards, submit risk mitigation plans to their group safety offices, and track corrective actions to closure.

- Safety offices will provide ORM resources, assist units with assessments, and report aggregated risk trends to the wing safety office.

4. Effective Date. This stand-down is effective immediately and will be completed as directed above.

5. Point of Contact. 355 FW/SE, (comm) or (dsn), for questions regarding implementation.

This memorandum provides planning guidance for Checkered Flag 26.  All planning should prioritize force protection, sortie generation, and realistic threat replication to maximize training value.  Coordinate with tenant wings, range control, and the 12 AF/A3 scheduling cell to align airspace and maintenance support; identify critical resource shortfalls to your staff no later than 45 days before exercise start.

Unit leads will ensure compliance with applicable directives and training objectives, submit risk assessments, and confirm personnel readiness timelines.  Point of contact for operational planning questions is 12 AF/A3 (DSN or commercial number as appropriate); submit draft plans and timelines per the schedule provided via the A3 planning folder.

This memorandum directs actions to implement a Channel Mission Diversion in the event of tasked mission redirection. The intent is to ensure continuity of operations, preserve operational tempo, and maintain clear coordination across directorates and key stakeholders.

Inspector General teams will provide relevant, unclassified observations to the inspected organization and appropriate Air Force stakeholders when sharing supports timely awareness, trend analysis, or corrective action.

$kind: main
# U.S. Air Force and Space Force Official Memorandum
# Organization or office symbol, rendered in uppercase. To address a specific person, add their rank and name in parentheses: 'ORG/SYMBOL (LT COL JANE DOE)'. For a long list, enter 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' and name the recipients in the Distribution field.
memo_for:
  - 4 AF/CC
# The office symbol alone when every recipient is on this installation. The full mailing address as well when any recipient is elsewhere, so they can write back. Leave blank for a Memorandum for Record, which prints no FROM line.
memo_from: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
# Keep it brief. Capitalize the first letter of each word except articles, prepositions, and conjunctions. Put any suspense date in parentheses. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. Subject of the Memorandum
subject: UEI Observation Sharing
# YYYY-MM-DD, printed in the format the Memo Style field selects. Leave blank to use today's date.
date: 2026-04-11
# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.
authority_line: FOR 4 AF/CC
# Line 1: Name in UPPERCASE as signed, grade, and service. Line 2: Duty title.
signature_block:
  - GINA T. MARSH, Col, USAF
  - Inspector General
# Letterhead lines, top to bottom, all rendered in uppercase. The first is the department title, set larger than the rest. Change that line only for a Joint Command or a DoW agency. The lines below it are your unit's full organization name.
# e.g. [DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE, "HEADQUARTERS [UNIT NAME]"]
letterhead_title:
  - DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE
# Department of War (DoW) or Department of Defense (DoD) seal, shown at the top left of the letterhead. Leave blank for no seal.
letterhead_seal: dow # enum<dow | dod>
# Bold-caps line below the seal. Nothing prints when it is blank, or when there is no seal.
letterhead_seal_subtitle: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Organizational motto, centered in the footer of every page. Supports Markdown emphasis: *italics*, **bold**.
tag_line: "" # richtext(inline)<markdown>
# Classification marking, banner-printed at the top and bottom of every page. Leave blank for no banner, which is what an unclassified document normally carries. Mark per DAFI 16-1404, DoDM 5200.48 for CUI, and applicable DoD guidance.
# when CUI: controlled_by, poc, category, limited_dissemination
classification:
  value: ""
# Suffix appended to the banner after a double slash, rendered in uppercase: 'NF' prints as CUI//NF. Leave blank for no suffix.
dissemination: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Cite each reference by organization, type, date, and title. Two or more print as a References block lettered (a), (b), (c); a single one prints in parentheses after the subject, per AFH 33-337. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. ["AFMAN 33-326, 25 November 2011, *Preparing Official Communications*", "AFI 33-360, *Publications and Forms Management*"]
references:
  - islands: []
    lines:
      - containers: []
        kind: para
    marks:
      - end: 48
        start: 27
        type: emph
    text: AFI 90-201, 12 April 2022, The Inspection System
# Offices or people receiving a courtesy copy, one per line.
# e.g. ["Rank and Name, ORG/SYMBOL"]
cc: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
# Every recipient, listed here when 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' stands in the Memo For field.
distribution: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
# Attachments in the order the memo mentions them. Describe each briefly; do not write 'as stated' or abbreviate. A lone attachment prints unnumbered, two or more are numbered. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. ["Attachment description, YYYY MMM DD"]
attachments: [] # array<richtext(inline)<markdown>>

This memorandum announces procedures for sharing Unit Effectiveness Inspection (UEI) observations between 4 AF staff and subordinate units to enhance transparency and accelerate corrective actions. Observations that affect multiple units or reveal systemic issues should be reported through established IG channels and documented per AFI 90-201, 12 April 2022, *The Inspection System*. Ensure submissions are factual, include necessary context, and exclude classified or Controlled Unclassified Information unless properly authorized.

Units are expected to acknowledge receipt of shared observations within five duty days and to provide a corrective action plan or an interim response when immediate correction is not feasible. The 4 AF Inspector General's office will act as the focal point for cross-unit coordination, tracking actions to closure and offering assistance to units requiring additional support.

The 5th Civil Engineer Squadron is prepared to execute snow removal operations across Minot Air Force Base during the 2025–2026 winter season. Our priority is to preserve safe access for emergency response, mission-essential operations, medical care, housing, and primary traffic routes while maintaining airfield and installation requirements.

Snow removal operations will be conducted using established priority routes and available personnel and equipment. During and immediately following significant snowfall, mission partners should expect temporary delays, restricted parking, and intermittent road closures as crews clear and treat priority surfaces. Unit commanders are requested to reinforce safe-driving practices, ensure personnel comply with temporary traffic controls, and report hazardous conditions through established base channels.

Please support the 5th Civil Engineer Squadron by identifying mission-essential areas that require immediate access during severe weather and by coordinating special snow-removal requirements with the squadron before the next significant storm. The 5th Civil Engineer Squadron will provide updates on major route restrictions and recovery timelines through installation command-and-control channels.

1. Purpose. This memorandum directs snow removal and ice mitigation actions for Minot Air Force Base during periods of snow accumulation or freeze-thaw conditions.

2. Tasking. a. 5th Civil Engineer Squadron (5 CES) will plan and execute snow removal to maintain safe installation mobility for mission-essential vehicles, pedestrian access, and emergency response. b. 5 CES will prioritize routes as follows: (1) fire and emergency access routes, (2) routes supporting essential mission operations, (3) main gate and inbound/outbound circulation, and (4) remaining internal roadways. c. 5 CES will apply anti-icing and de-icing materials in accordance with established local guidance and will adjust application rates based on pavement condition and weather forecasts.

3. Unit coordination. a. Organization commanders will ensure designated points of contact (POCs) coordinate with 5 CES for blockage reporting, facility access concerns, and time-sensitive mission requirements. b. Units will remove or relocate vehicles, equipment, and stored items from road shoulders and sidewalks as directed by 5 CES to prevent interference with clearing operations.

4. Public safety. a. All personnel will exercise caution when moving on cleared or partially cleared surfaces and will obey posted warning signage. b. Pedestrian access will be cleared to the extent feasible; however, additional caution is required during active operations and in areas with drifting snow.

5. Reporting. a. When conditions require immediate attention, units will notify 5 CES via the established snow/ice reporting channel. b. Following significant events, 5 CES will provide a summary of completed actions and remaining risk areas to affected stakeholders.

This memorandum outlines snow removal responsibilities, priorities, and reporting procedures for Minot Air Force Base to ensure safe and continuous operations during winter weather.

1. Responsibilities.

a. 5 CES/CC is responsible for planning, coordinating, and executing snow and ice control for airfield and base infrastructure. This includes plowing, deicing, snow hauling, and application of abrasives and deicers as required to maintain safe conditions.

b. 5 BW/CC will provide command-level prioritization of assets and, when requested, additional resources or authorities to support emergency snow removal operations.

c. All unit commanders will:

- Ensure assigned vehicle and pedestrian routes (including parking lots and walkways) are cleared per locally published priorities.

- Maintain accountability for personnel and equipment tasked to support snow operations.

- Report significant impacts to mission assurance or damage resulting from snow/ice control activities immediately to 5 CES/CC.

2. Priorities.

a. Airfield movement areas (runways, taxiways, aprons) and lifesaving access routes to medical and emergency services are the highest priority.

b. Mission-essential facilities, primary roadways, and building access for mission personnel are secondary priorities.

c. All other areas, including non-mission parking and non-essential walkways, will be cleared as resources permit.

3. Coordination and Notification.

a. 5 CES will monitor weather forecasts and initiate pre-storm preparations per the base Snow and Ice Control Plan. When conditions are forecast to meet or exceed locally established thresholds, 5 CES will notify 5 BW/CC, the Installation Command Post, and affected units.

b. The Installation Command Post will serve as the central point for reporting storm impacts, requests for assistance, and coordination with off-base authorities.

c. Units requiring emergency support will submit requests through the Command Post. For immediate life-safety or flight safety hazards, units will call the Command Post directly.

4. Equipment and Materials.

a. 5 CES will maintain a prioritized list of available snow removal equipment, drivers, and stock levels of deicing materials. Units with organic equipment that can assist should coordinate availability with 5 CES.

b. Requests for additional resources (mutual aid, contracted support) will be routed through 5 BW/CC for approval.

5. Reporting and After-Action.

a. 5 CES will provide 5 BW/CC with daily status reports during prolonged events, to include cleared areas, outstanding priorities, equipment status, and material consumption.

b. Following significant snow events, 5 CES will conduct an after-action review to identify lessons learned and recommend improvements to procedures, staffing, or equipment.

6. Point of Contact.

The primary point of contact for snow removal operations is:

5 CES/CC Comm: (701) XXX-XXXX Email: 5ces.commander@us.af.mil

7. Implementation.

This memorandum is effective immediately. Units will review and, as necessary, update their local procedures to align with the priorities and reporting requirements outlined above.

FIRST M. LAST, Maj, USAF\
FOR THE COMMANDER

MAJ COLIN P. HAYES, Commander Commander, 5 Civil Engineer Squadron

Per direction from 49 MXG leadership, we will implement an immediate, temporary pause to ISO maintenance activities effective upon receipt of this memorandum. All ISO maintenance tasks will be suspended until further notice to allow for a deliberate review of current processes, safety checks, and parts accountability. Unit maintenance supervisors will secure in-progress work, account for assigned parts and tools, and post status to the maintenance tracking system by the end of duty today.

During the pause, 49 MXG will conduct a focused inspection and risk assessment to identify any systemic issues and to develop corrective actions. Supervisors will prepare a written brief of findings and proposed mitigations for 49 WG/CC within 72 hours. Mission-essential maintenance authorized by my office may continue on a case-by-case basis when preapproved in writing by the maintenance group commander.

This memorandum informs 436 AW/CC of a delay in the C-5 isochronal inspection. The delay is the result of scheduling constraints with maintenance facilities and recent supply-chain adjustments that limited access to required test equipment. The delay will necessitate a revised inspection window and may impact the aircraft's availability for planned missions while maintenance teams realign resources to complete the inspection expeditiously.

Impact to readiness and proposed mitigation: we will re-sequence tasks to maximize aircraft availability, coordinate a revised inspection window with Flight Scheduling and the Maintenance Group, and implement temporary interim safety checks to ensure continued airworthiness. A revised schedule will be provided to the command as soon as the updated isochronal plan is finalized.

This memorandum provides an overview of the planned beddown actions and support requirements for Red Flag-Alaska. The 354 OG has coordinated with range control, logistics, fuel, munitions, and airfield operations to ensure aircraft, personnel, and equipment are staged and sustainment is in place to meet exercise timelines. Key considerations include airspace scheduling, munitions handling procedures, transient alert support, and liaison with host-range authorities to maintain safety and mission effectiveness.

The 354 OG requests concurrence and awareness by 354 FW leadership of the proposed beddown sequencing and resource allocations to minimize impacts on local operations and maximize sortie generation. Point of contact for this action is COL YUSUF I. HADDAD, Commander, 354 OG, or their designated representative.

His unwavering accountability, technical acumen, and willingness to assume additional duties under challenging conditions directly enhanced the squadron’s ability to execute high-risk sorties with minimal incident while mentoring junior officers and airmen toward operational independence.

Finally, Capt Mendez embodied the ethos of service before self through a relentless commitment to moral courage and professional development. He led by example in dynamic environments, guided peers through complex ethical decision-making, and institutionalized processes that ensured rapid adaptation to evolving threats. His sustained performance under stress and his quiet, effective leadership undergird unit morale, mission resilience, and the advancement of the Air Force’s core values.

Sijan Award in recognition of an unwavering commitment to professionalism, mission excellence, and the enduring care for people that defines exceptional Airmen. Capt Mendez consistently demonstrates maturity beyond his rank, pairing disciplined execution with the empathy necessary to elevate a team under pressure.

Throughout his tenure, Capt Mendez has been a steady force in translating operational needs into measurable training outcomes, while simultaneously strengthening the unit’s cohesion and resiliency. He has led and improved processes that enhanced readiness and accelerated problem resolution, ensuring that critical standards were understood, practiced, and sustained. Just as importantly, his leadership has remained grounded in mentorship—he listens first, coaches deliberately, and advocates for the removal of barriers so others can succeed. In demanding moments, he remains calm, precise, and accountable, setting conditions for safe, effective execution.

Capt Mendez’s performance reflects the Lance P. Sijan standard of balanced excellence—technical credibility, ethical conduct, and genuine concern for the Airmen he serves alongside. His initiative and follow-through have improved both unit capability and individual confidence, and his example has strengthened a culture where disciplined professionalism is expected and excellence is achieved together. The enclosed AF Form 1206, dated 2026 Jan 30, documents the basis for this nomination.

FOR THE COMMANDER,

COL JOANNA P. REED, Col, USAF Commander, 355th Fighter Wing

He set the standard for disciplined execution in the air and on the ground, repeatedly accepting the hardest tasks, solving problems before they became failures, and elevating the performance of every team around him through clarity of purpose and uncompromising professionalism.

His influence extended well beyond the cockpit: he mentored junior aviators, strengthened crew coordination, and served as a stabilizing force during high-tempo periods when time, equipment, and personnel were all in short supply. What most sets Capt Mendez apart is not merely the quantity of his accomplishments, but the character with which he achieved them. He consistently acted with selflessness, humility, and a deep sense of responsibility for the mission and the people entrusted to him, reflecting the very qualities embodied by Capt Lance P. Sijan. His record reveals a leader who never sought recognition, yet repeatedly earned the confidence of peers, supervisors, and subordinates through performance that was both operationally decisive and morally grounded. I strongly recommend Capt Mendez for this award and ask for your favorable consideration of his nomination.

Capt Luis Mendez distinguished himself through sustained, mission-focused leadership while directing his team through a demanding cycle of operational commitments, competing priorities, and constrained resources. He transformed fragmented requirements into a disciplined execution plan, synchronized operators and support agencies, and personally closed the gaps that threatened schedule and readiness. His judgment kept critical work moving without sacrificing standards, while his deliberate communication gave commanders timely, accurate insight into risk, progress, and resource decisions. The resulting performance strengthened unit responsiveness and demonstrated the calm, accountable leadership expected of an Air Force officer.

Captain Mendez also delivered effects well beyond the boundaries of his assigned duties. He identified recurring process failures, built practical solutions with the affected organizations, and converted those solutions into repeatable procedures that improved reliability and reduced avoidable workload. Rather than accepting inherited limitations, he coached teammates through the change, developed emerging leaders, and established a culture in which people raised problems early and solved them together. His initiative produced measurable improvements in mission execution while preserving trust across the diverse personnel and partner organizations required to accomplish the wing's objectives.

Most importantly, Capt Mendez's accomplishments reflect the character and selfless service central to the Lance P. Sijan Award. He consistently placed mission and people ahead of personal recognition, remained accessible when his team faced difficult decisions, and acted with courage when the right course required candor or additional effort. His example inspired peers and subordinates to assume greater responsibility, strengthened the wing's combat-ready culture, and left the organization more capable than he found it. I strongly endorse Capt Mendez for selection as the 355th Fighter Wing's nominee for the Lance P. Sijan Award; his sustained achievement, leadership, and devotion to duty merit recognition at the next level.

2. Eligibility. Parental leave is available to eligible Service members in accordance with governing Department of the Air Force policy and applicable statutory authorities. This memorandum provides implementation guidance for parental leave across the Air Force. It establishes common expectations for administering leave, supporting eligible members, and applying the policy consistently within each major command.

Commanders will ensure eligible military members receive parental leave in accordance with current Department of Defense and Department of the Air Force policy. Eligibility includes members who give birth, adopt a child, or have a child placed with them for adoption or long-term foster care, as applicable under governing policy. Major commands will ensure subordinate organizations apply the authorized leave entitlement consistently and without unnecessary delay.

Members requesting parental leave will submit the required documentation through their servicing military personnel flight or designated commander-approved process. Documentation must establish the qualifying event and, when applicable, the date of birth, placement, or adoption. Organizations will protect personally identifiable information, maintain records in accordance with applicable requirements, and promptly update leave records after approval.

Questions regarding eligibility, documentation, or implementation should be directed to the servicing military personnel flight or command human resources office. Major command points of contact will coordinate unresolved policy questions with HQ USAF/A1 through established personnel policy channels. Commands will distribute this guidance to subordinate units and supervisors responsible for approving parental leave.

Paragraph 1 — Situation: In response to the imminent threat and widespread devastation from a major hurricane affecting coastal and inland communities, the 23d Wing/CC requests immediate force generation capabilities from ACC/A3 to enable rapid airlift, MEDEVAC, and robust communications support. Time-sensitive relief requires pre-positioned assets, streamlined tasking through joint airlift channels, and integration with local and federal emergency management structures to deliver life-sustaining assistance.

Paragraph 2 — Mission: Generate and marshal immediate force generation assets and aircrew readiness to execute hurricane relief operations. Provide logistics, medical evacuation, and communications support to affected areas, ensuring rapid response within the suspense window and seamless coordination with interagency partners and disaster response cells.

Paragraph 3 — Specified Tasks:

- Airlift

  - Pre-plan and task select transport assets to move relief personnel, equipment, and supplies into/within affected regions on a priority basis.

  - Establish in-theater airlift staging with clear cabotage and weather mitigations; execute dynamic rerouting as weather and security conditions require.

- Medevac (MEDEVAC)

  - Ensure medically equipped aircraft and trained crews are positioned to evacuate critically injured/ill from incident areas to definitive care.

  - Coordinate with local hospitals and regional medical C2 for patient tracking, inbound flow, and clinical handover.

- Comms

  - Deploy or re-task comms assets to restore commander/situation awareness and interagency coordination; ensure redundant voice/data paths for command and control across affected zones.

No classification. No indorsement.

> 2026-04-22, 1840L, south traffic pattern near the alert apron\
> 2026-05-03, 0638L, eastern departure corridor off Runway 32

date: "2026-01-31"
# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Colleagues consistently recognize his strategic insight and genuine mentorship, fostering team cohesion and elevating unit performance.

The selection of Capt Mendez for the Lance P. Sijan Leadership Award acknowledges his enduring impact, exemplary integrity, and selfless service. It is with confidence and pride that this nomination is forwarded for esteemed consideration.

This memorandum documents the 4th Fighter Wing's recent bird aircraft strike hazard activity and identifies corrective actions to reduce the risk of additional strikes. Safety personnel reviewed the reported events, associated airfield conditions, and operational patterns.

The reviewed strike events occurred at the following times and locations:

> 2026-05-06, 0815L — Runway 16 approach end\
> 2026-05-07, 1420L — Taxiway Bravo near the perimeter road\
> 2026-05-08, 1745L — Runway 34 departure end

The pattern indicates recurring bird activity near aircraft movement areas during periods of increased flight operations. All units should continue prompt reporting of strikes, near misses, and significant bird concentrations through established channels.

I recommend the following mitigations:

- Increase active bird dispersal coverage during identified high-activity periods.

  - Position qualified personnel near the runway approach and departure ends before the first scheduled sortie.

  - Record dispersal actions and observed flock movement in the daily airfield wildlife log.

- Reduce attractants and improve habitat management around the airfield.

  - Coordinate removal of standing water, food sources, and other conditions that attract birds.

  - Inspect the perimeter and movement areas weekly and track corrective actions to closure.

The 4 FW/SE will monitor implementation and provide a follow-up assessment after 30 days. Questions or additional observations should be directed to the 4 FW Safety Office.

This memorandum documents a Bird Aircraft Strike Hazard (BASH) after action and provides recommendations to mitigate near-term recurrence.

On 2026-05-08 three bird strikes occurred during flight operations. Details follow.

> 0715 Z — Approach, Runway 27\
> Aircraft contacted a flock on final approach; minor airframe damage, no injuries.\\
>
> 1030 Z — Departure, Runway 09\
> Bird ingestion during initial climb; engine inspection required, flight delayed.\\
>
> 1435 Z — Taxiway B near Taxiway C intersection\
> Strike to left wing leading edge during taxi; superficial damage only.

Summary of actions taken:

- Crews inspected affected aircraft and completed required maintenance and reports.

- Airfield operations increased wildlife patrols for the remainder of the sorties.

Recommended mitigations:

- Enhance airfield wildlife control measures

  - Increase scheduled wildlife patrols to cover peak movement periods (0600–0900 and 1400–1600).

  - Deploy additional pyrotechnic and auditory deterrents along identified hotspots.

- Improve flight and ground procedural mitigations

  - Adjust launch and recovery windows when feasible to avoid identified high-risk periods.

  - Require aircrew briefings emphasizing visual scan techniques on approach, climb, and taxi to reduce strike risk.

Point of contact for this memorandum is the 4 FW Safety Office at 4fw.safety@example.mil or DSN 312-555-1234.

Respectfully,

LT COL PRISCILLA N. ORTIZ, USAF Chief of Safety

# Organization or office symbol, rendered in uppercase. To address a specific person, add their rank and name in parentheses: 'ORG/SYMBOL (LT COL JANE DOE)'. For a long list, enter 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' and name the recipients in the Distribution field.
memo_for:

memo_from: []

# e.g. Subject of the Memorandum
subject: Immediate Force Generation for Hurricane Relief
# YYYY-MM-DD, printed in the format the Memo Style field selects. Leave blank to use today's date.
date: 2026-09-02
# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.
# e.g. FOR THE COMMANDER
authority_line: ""
# Line 1: Name in UPPERCASE as signed, grade, and service. Line 2: Duty title.
signature_block:
  - GRAVES, Maj Gen, USAF

# Department of War (DoW) or Department of Defense (DoD) seal, shown at the top left of the letterhead. Leave blank for no seal.

letterhead_seal_subtitle: ""
# Organizational motto, centered in the footer of every page. Supports Markdown emphasis: *italics*, **bold**.
tag_line: ""

date: "2026-04-15" # date<YYYY-MM-DD>
# Line telling the receiver the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. This legal review memorandum addresses the proposed Off-Limits Order currently under consideration. After thorough examination of the relevant policies and legal frameworks, we provide the following analysis and recommendations.

The legal basis for the order is supported by the following authorities:

- (a) AFI 31-115, *Law Enforcement Operations*, which governs the establishment and enforcement of off-limits areas to ensure the safety and security of Air Force personnel and resources.

- (b) Applicable federal and military regulations that authorize installation commanders to impose restrictions for force protection and morale.

- (c) Jurisprudence affirming the commander's authority to regulate conduct on military installations to maintain good order and discipline.

This review endorses the proposed Off-Limits Order as compliant with applicable law and policy, provided it is implemented with clear communication to all affected parties and consistent enforcement.

Per your request, the legal office has reviewed the proposed off-limits order and the supporting memorandum prepared by Security Forces. The draft order, as written, identifies specific locations and articulates a clear nexus to unit safety and good order and discipline. On its face the proposed restrictions are within the commander’s authority to protect the health, safety, and welfare of the force, provided the factual basis supporting each listed location is documented and reasonably related to the stated purpose.

Legal support for issuing an off-limits order in this instance includes the following bases:

- The commander’s inherent authority to take measures necessary to preserve good order and discipline and protect mission readiness.

  - This authority permits reasonable, narrowly tailored restrictions when supported by articulable facts showing a genuine threat to the force.

- Regulatory authorization under AFI 31-115, *Law Enforcement Operations*.

  - AFI 31-115 discusses force protection and collaboration with installation commanders and Security Forces in establishing conditions that may warrant access restrictions.

- Civilian law and constitutional considerations permitting restrictions on access when they are content-neutral, time/place/manner regulations that are reasonably tailored to serve a significant government interest and leave open ample alternative channels for lawful conduct.

  - Ensure any order is drafted to avoid vague or overbroad language that could unnecessarily restrict protected activity or exceed the commander’s authority.

If you concur, the legal office can prepare a finalized order that incorporates the recommended factual findings, clarifies the temporal and spatial scope of each restriction, and includes notice and appeal information for affected personnel.

To: 25 AF/A2 From: 9 IS/CC

Subject: CTI Handling for Partner Air Forces

This memorandum provides guidance on the handling, dissemination, and safeguarding of Counter-Intelligence information (CTI) related to partner Air Forces. All CTI material associated with partner nations should be treated with heightened sensitivity and restricted to personnel with an operational need-to-know. Operators and intelligence personnel must ensure that CTI is accessed only by cleared individuals and that dissemination to partner forces complies with applicable DoD and Air Force policies, including NOFORN restrictions when applicable. A formal, risk-based approach should be used to determine which elements of CTI can be shared and under what circumstances, with proper documentation and oversight.

This guidance emphasizes the importance of maintaining situational awareness of partner capabilities, vulnerabilities, and intent, while preventing unintended exposure of sensitive CTI sources and methods. Partners should be engaged through authorized channels, and all exchanges should be logged and audited to maintain accountability and compliance with security requirements.

# U.S. Air Force and Space Force Official Memorandum
# Organization or office symbol, rendered in uppercase. To address a specific person, add their rank and name in parentheses: 'ORG/SYMBOL (LT COL JANE DOE)'. For a long list, enter 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' and name the recipients in the Distribution field.

# e.g. [ORG/SYMBOL, Organization Name, 123 Street Ave, City ST 12345-6789]
memo_from: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
# Keep it brief. Capitalize the first letter of each word except articles, prepositions, and conjunctions. Put any suspense date in parentheses. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. Subject of the Memorandum
subject: Below-the-Zone Promotion Board Timeline
# YYYY-MM-DD, printed in the format the Memo Style field selects. Leave blank to use today's date.
date: "2026-09-18" # date<YYYY-MM-DD>
# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.
authority_line: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Line 1: Name in UPPERCASE as signed, grade, and service. Line 2: Duty title.
signature_block:
  - Col MICHELLE A. DORN
  - Commander
# Letterhead lines, top to bottom, all rendered in uppercase. The first is the department title, set larger than the rest. Change that line only for a Joint Command or a DoW agency. The lines below it are your unit's full organization name.
letterhead_title:
  - DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE
# Department of War (DoW) or Department of Defense (DoD) seal, shown at the top left of the letterhead. Leave blank for no seal.
letterhead_seal: dow # enum<dow | dod>
# Bold-caps line below the seal. Nothing prints when it is blank, or when there is no seal.
letterhead_seal_subtitle: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Organizational motto, centered in the footer of every page. Supports Markdown emphasis: *italics*, **bold**.
tag_line: "" # richtext(inline)<markdown>
# Classification marking, banner-printed at the top and bottom of every page. Leave blank for no banner, which is what an unclassified document normally carries. Mark per DAFI 16-1404, DoDM 5200.48 for CUI, and applicable DoD guidance.

  - Timeline: Revised SOPs issued (45 days); liaison assigned immediately.

Decision 3: Enhance leader development and cross-functional training opportunities.

- Action: Establish a quarterly leader-development seminar and a rotating cross-functional shadow program.

  - Owner: 18 WG/CC (oversight) and Force Development cell (execution)

  - Timeline: Seminar calendar published (60 days); shadow program pilot (90 days).

The 366th Fighter Wing Safety Office conducted operational risk management spot checks across selected wing activities. The checks assessed whether personnel were applying ORM processes during planning and execution, documenting identified hazards, and implementing appropriate controls. Overall, personnel demonstrated a sound understanding of ORM requirements, and most observed activities reflected effective risk-based decision-making.

Several opportunities for improvement were identified, primarily involving incomplete documentation of control measures and inconsistent communication of residual risk. The Safety Office will continue follow-up checks to measure progress and provide assistance as needed.

# U.S. Air Force and Space Force Official Memorandum
# Organization or office symbol, rendered in uppercase. To address a specific person, add their rank and name in parentheses: 'ORG/SYMBOL (LT COL JANE DOE)'. For a long list, enter 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' and name the recipients in the Distribution field.

  - PACAF/A3
# The office symbol alone when every recipient is on this installation. The full mailing address as well when any recipient is elsewhere, so they can write back. Leave blank for a Memorandum for Record, which prints no FROM line.
memo_from: []
# Keep it brief. Capitalize the first letter of each word except articles, prepositions, and conjunctions. Put any suspense date in parentheses. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. Subject of the Memorandum
subject: Ulchi Freedom Shield 26 Air Tasking
# YYYY-MM-DD, printed in the format the Memo Style field selects. Leave blank to use today's date.
date: "2026-08-17"
# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.
authority_line: ""

signature_block:
  - FIRST M. LAST, Maj, USAF
  - Director of Operations

# Bold-caps line below the seal. Nothing prints when it is blank, or when there is no seal.
letterhead_seal_subtitle: ""
# Organizational motto, centered in the footer of every page. Supports Markdown emphasis: *italics*, **bold**.
tag_line: "Prepare to Win"

dissemination: ""

references: []

cc: []
# Every recipient, listed here when 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' stands in the Memo For field.

distribution: []
# Attachments in the order the memo mentions them. Describe each briefly; do not write 'as stated' or abbreviate. A lone attachment prints unnumbered, two or more are numbered. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.

attachments: []

memo_style: usaf
# Body text size in points; decimals allowed, such as 11.5. AFH 33-337 §5 specifies 12.
font_size: 12
# Write body prose here.

The purpose of this memorandum is to provide details regarding the upcoming Ulchi Freedom Shield 26 Air Tasking. This operation is a key component of our ongoing joint and combined readiness exercises, aimed at enhancing interoperability and strategic capability among allied forces. The attached schedule outlines the key activities, resource allocations, and command responsibilities.

This document also emphasizes the importance of synchronized planning and execution to ensure mission success. All involved units are directed to review the attached operational guidelines and confirm their availability and preparedness. Coordination with the PACAF/A3 and other relevant agencies must be maintained throughout the planning and execution phases to ensure a seamless operation.

Please address any questions regarding this memorandum directly to the undersigned or the PACAF/A3 staff. Your cooperation and attention to detail are vital for the success of Ulchi Freedom Shield 26. Thank you for your commitment to our collective readiness and strategic objectives.

This memorandum announces the refreshed Close Air Support (CAS) doctrine, intended to ensure U.S. Air Force and Space Force components train to consistent standards, employ CAS effectively across the joint fight, and reduce ambiguity during execution. The refresh incorporates lessons learned from recent exercises and operations, with emphasis on targeting discipline, mission planning rigor, and timely coordination across the Air Operations Center, Air Support Operations Center, and supported joint force elements.

The doctrine refresh clarifies roles and responsibilities, strengthens guidance on request-to-strike timelines, and aligns CAS procedures with current joint and service mission planning processes. It standardizes terminology, expands best practices for dynamic target development and deconfliction, and reinforces procedures for establishing and maintaining positive control of airpower throughout the CAS cycle.

All MAJCOMs will implement the refreshed doctrine in training programs, evaluation events, and unit readiness processes within applicable timelines. Commanders will ensure CAS aircrew and supporting personnel complete doctrine familiarization and applicable local follow-on training, and will provide feedback to AF/A3 on operational issues, questions, and improvement opportunities so subsequent updates can remain tightly aligned to operational realities.

AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. authority_line: ""
# Line 1: Name in UPPERCASE as signed, grade, and service. Line 2: Duty title.

  - Col ANDRE T. BOYD
  - Administrator
# Letterhead lines, top to bottom, all rendered in uppercase. Change that line only for a Joint Command or a DoW agency. The lines below it are your unit's full organization name.

\[BEGIN MEMORANDUM\]

THIS MEMORANDUM DIRECTS A 48-HOUR SAFETY DOWN-DAY FOR ALL FLIGHT OPERATIONS AND ASSOCIATED TRAINING ACTIVITIES WITHIN THE 14TH FIGHTER WING FOLLOWING A CLASS C MISHAP THAT OCCURRED ON BASE PROPERTY. THE DOWN-DAY WILL COMMENCE AT 0600 LOCAL ON 2026-09-03 AND WILL REMAIN IN EFFECT UNTIL 0600 LOCAL ON 2026-09-05, UNLESS EXTENDED OR MODIFIED IN WRITING BY THE COMMANDER.

DURING THE DOWN-DAY, ALL FLIGHT OPERATIONS AND MISSION-CRITICAL TRAINING ARE SUSPENDED. SQA/CIP REVIEWS WILL BE CONDUCTED AS REQUIRED, AND ALL PERSONNEL WILL COMPLETE A SAFETY STAND-DOWN BRIEFING PRIOR TO RESUMPTION OF OPERATIONS. UNIT LEVEL LEADERS ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR ENSURING ALL ACCESS TO MISSION-CRITICAL AREAS IS CONTROLLED AND THAT RISK MITIGATION PRACTICES ARE REVIEWED AND ADHERED TO UPON RETURN TO OPERATIONS.

THIS DOWN-DAY DOES NOT IMPLY CULPABILITY; RATHER, IT ENABLES A THOROUGH SAFETY REVIEW, IDENTIFICATION OF POTENTIAL PROCESS OR EQUIPMENT DEFICIENCIES, AND IMPLEMENTATION OF RECOMMENDED CORRECTIVE ACTIONS TO MAINTAIN ACCIDENT-FREE OPERATIONS. ADDITIONAL INSTRUCTIONS WILL BE PROVIDED AS SAFETY REVIEWS ARE COMPLETED.

POINTS OF CONTACT: SQA OFFICER, SAFETY OFFICE, AND OPs GROUP COMMAND POST.

FOR THE COMMANDER

COLONEL ALEX R. SMITH, USAF COMMANDER, 14TH FIGHTER WING

- Conduct immediate safety briefings for all aircrew, maintainers, and support personnel to review the mishap summary, human factors considerations, and interim controls.

- Implement a unit-level risk assessment for all remaining sorties/tasks scheduled immediately after stand-down, ensuring required configuration, weapon system, and equipment checks are performed prior to returning to flight.

- Ensure all aircraft and associated support equipment are inspected for applicable findings and deferred deficiencies are documented in the appropriate records.

4. The focus for the stand-down will be learning, disciplined risk management, and verification of controls—not resuming routine operations by default.

5. Provide the Wing Commander a consolidated summary no later than 2026-09-06 1200L. The summary will include stand-down attendance, completed briefings, interim corrective actions initiated, and any issues requiring Wing-level decision or additional resources.

6. Compliance with this directive is mandatory. If an exception is required, coordinate through the Operations Group Commander and Wing Safety for approval prior to execution.

Effective upon receipt, conduct a 48-hour safety down day for all flying and flying-related operations assigned to the 366th Operations Group. This direction follows the Class C mishap that occurred on 16 April 2026 and remains in effect from 0001 hours local time on 18 April through 2359 hours local time on 19 April 2026.

During the safety down day, suspend all sorties, simulator events that reproduce the mishap sequence, and nonessential maintenance or ground activities involving the affected weapon system. Continue only those activities required to protect personnel and equipment, preserve evidence, maintain essential alert or defense commitments, and support mishap response. Coordinate any exception with the 366th Fighter Wing Safety Office before execution.

Use this period to complete a command-directed safety review. At a minimum, review the mishap sequence and known hazards; verify applicable technical orders, checklists, and local operating procedures; conduct focused inspections of affected aircraft, equipment, and support areas; and identify immediate corrective actions. Ensure supervisors obtain inputs from aircrew, maintainers, and other personnel who perform the affected tasks.

Provide the completed review and a written recommendation to resume normal operations to 366 FW/CC, through 366 FW/SE, not later than 1600 hours local time on 20 April 2026. The recommendation will identify any unresolved hazards, risk controls, owners, and projected completion dates. Do not resume suspended operations until I approve the recommendation or issue further direction.

Ensure this memorandum is briefed to all affected personnel and that attendance and completed review actions are documented. Direct questions through the 366th Fighter Wing Safety Office.

final_markdown:
~~~
$quill: usaf_memo@0.3.0 # keep verbatim
$kind: main
memo_for:
  - 19 AW/CC
memo_from:
  - 19 AW/A3
# Keep it brief. Capitalize the first letter of each word except articles, prepositions, and conjunctions. Put any suspense date in parentheses. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. Subject of the Memorandum
subject: Christmas Extravaganza Parking # richtext(inline)<markdown>
# YYYY-MM-DD, printed in the format the Memo Style field selects. Leave blank to use today's date.
date: 2026-12-15 # date<YYYY-MM-DD>
# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.
authority_line: FOR THE COMMANDER # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Line 1: Name in UPPERCASE as signed, grade, and service. Line 2: Duty title.
signature_block: !must_fill # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
  - MAJ OLIVIA C. NASH, USAF
  - Director of Operations
# Letterhead lines, top to bottom, all rendered in uppercase. The first is the department title, set larger than the rest. Change that line only for a Joint Command or a DoW agency. The lines below it are your unit's full organization name.
# e.g. [DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE, "HEADQUARTERS [UNIT NAME]"]
letterhead_title:
  - DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE
# Department of War (DoW) or Department of Defense (DoD) seal, shown at the top left of the letterhead. Leave blank for no seal.
letterhead_seal: dod # enum<dow | dod>
# Bold-caps line below the seal. Nothing prints when it is blank, or when there is no seal.
letterhead_seal_subtitle: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Organizational motto, centered in the footer of every page. Supports Markdown emphasis: *italics*, **bold**.
tag_line: "" # richtext(inline)<markdown>
# Classification marking, banner-printed at the top and bottom of every page. Leave blank for no banner, which is what an unclassified document normally carries. Mark per DAFI 16-1404, DoDM 5200.48 for CUI, and applicable DoD guidance.
# when CUI: controlled_by, poc, category, limited_dissemination
classification:
  value: UNCLASSIFIED
# Suffix appended to the banner after a double slash, rendered in uppercase: 'NF' prints as CUI//NF. Leave blank for no suffix.
dissemination: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Cite each reference by organization, type, date, and title. Two or more print as a References block lettered (a), (b), (c); a single one prints in parentheses after the subject, per AFH 33-337. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
references: [] # array<richtext(inline)<markdown>>
# Offices or people receiving a courtesy copy, one per line.
# e.g. ["Rank and Name, ORG/SYMBOL"]
cc: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
# Every recipient, listed here when 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' stands in the Memo For field.
# e.g. [ORG1/SYMBOL, ORG2/SYMBOL]
distribution: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
# Attachments in the order the memo mentions them. Describe each briefly; do not write 'as stated' or abbreviate. A lone attachment prints unnumbered, two or more are numbered. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
attachments: [] # array<richtext(inline)<markdown>>
# USAF memorandum or DAF headquarters memorandum, per AFH 33-337. DAF dates as 'September 15, 2026' rather than '15 September 2026', and leaves top-level paragraphs unnumbered with a first-line indent.
memo_style: usaf # enum<usaf | daf>
# Body text size in points; decimals allowed, such as 11.5. AFH 33-337 §5 specifies 12.
font_size: 12 # number
~~~

This memo authorizes parking arrangements for the Christmas Extravaganza on the installation.

Please reserve accessible spaces in Lot B and designate loading zones near the shuttle terminal.

Ensure adequate signage and on-site personnel to guide attendees and prevent congestion.

Effective immediately, direct a 48-hour safety down day for all 23d Operations Group flying and sortie-generation activities in response to the Class C mishap that occurred on April 16, 2026. The safety down day will begin at 0001 hours local time on April 18, 2026, and conclude at 2359 hours local time on April 19, 2026. This direction applies to all assigned and attached fighter squadrons and to associated maintenance, intelligence, aircrew flight equipment, and operations-support personnel.

During the safety down day, suspend all training, operational, and test sorties except those specifically approved by me for urgent national-defense requirements, aircraft recovery, or mishap-response support. Preserve mishap evidence and records, and ensure no maintenance action disturbs relevant components or documentation unless required to protect personnel or property.

Use this period to complete a focused review of flight and ground-safety practices, aircraft and equipment status, current risk assessments, crew-rest compliance, and supervisory controls. Conduct face-to-face all-hands safety briefings before resuming normal operations. Squadron commanders will document identified hazards, immediate corrective actions, and unresolved risks, and provide those results to the Operations Group commander no later than 1200 hours local time on April 20, 2026.

Before authorizing the first sortie after the down day, provide me a consolidated assessment through the 23d Wing Safety Office confirming completion of the reviews and briefings, disposition of all immediately correctable hazards, and acceptance or mitigation of any remaining risk. No commander will treat schedule recovery or mission demand as grounds to bypass this direction.

Coordinate implementation with the 23d Wing Safety Office and the 366th Fighter Wing Inspector General as appropriate. Direct questions or requests for exception through your chain of command to the 23d Wing Commander.

# Organization or office symbol, rendered in uppercase. To address a specific person, add their rank and name in parentheses: 'ORG/SYMBOL (LT COL JANE DOE)'. For a long list, enter 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' and name the recipients in the Distribution field.
memo_for:

# YYYY-MM-DD, printed in the format the Memo Style field selects. Leave blank to use today's date.
date: "" # date<YYYY-MM-DD>
# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.
# e.g. FOR THE COMMANDER
authority_line: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Line 1: Name in UPPERCASE as signed, grade, and service. Line 2: Duty title.
signature_block: !must_fill # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
  - FIRST M. LAST, Rank, USAF
  - Duty Title
# Letterhead lines, top to bottom, all rendered in uppercase. The first is the department title, set larger than the rest. Change that line only for a Joint Command or a DoW agency. The lines below it are your unit's full organization name.
# e.g. [DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE, "HEADQUARTERS [UNIT NAME]"]
letterhead_title: # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
  - DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE
# Department of War (DoW) or Department of Defense (DoD) seal, shown at the top left of the letterhead. Leave blank for no seal.
letterhead_seal: dow # enum<dow | dod>
# Bold-caps line below the seal. Nothing prints when it is blank, or when there is no seal.
letterhead_seal_subtitle: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Organizational motto, centered in the footer of every page. Supports Markdown emphasis: *italics*, **bold**.
tag_line: "" # richtext(inline)<markdown>
# Classification marking, banner-printed at the top and bottom of every page. Leave blank for no banner, which is what an unclassified document normally carries. Mark per DAFI 16-1404, DoDM 5200.48 for CUI, and applicable DoD guidance.
# when CUI: controlled_by, poc, category, limited_dissemination
classification: # enum<UNCLASSIFIED | CUI | CONFIDENTIAL | SECRET | TOP SECRET>
  value: ""
# Suffix appended to the banner after a double slash, rendered in uppercase: 'NF' prints as CUI//NF. Leave blank for no suffix.
dissemination: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Cite each reference by organization, type, date, and title. Two or more print as a References block lettered (a), (b), (c); a single one prints in parentheses after the subject, per AFH 33-337. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. ["AFMAN 33-326, 25 November 2011, *Preparing Official Communications*", "AFI 33-360, *Publications and Forms Management*"]
references: [] # array<richtext(inline)<markdown>>
# Offices or people receiving a courtesy copy, one per line.
# e.g. ["Rank and Name, ORG/SYMBOL"]
cc: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
# Every recipient, listed here when 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' stands in the Memo For field.
# e.g. [ORG1/SYMBOL, ORG2/SYMBOL]
distribution: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
# Attachments in the order the memo mentions them. Describe each briefly; do not write 'as stated' or abbreviate. A lone attachment prints unnumbered, two or more are numbered. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. ["Attachment description, YYYY MMM DD"]
attachments: [] # array<richtext(inline)<markdown>>

The undersigned authorizes the 88th Communications Squadron, Wright-Patterson AFB, to issue temporary SIPR (Secret) network access tokens to forty (40) deploying maintainers assigned to support mission-essential communications and repair work associated with current operations. The tokens are to be issued for a temporary window while these personnel are deployed or otherwise away from their home station.

Suspense: 2026-09-15. All tokens must be issued, secured, and tracked in accordance with applicable DoD and USAF policy and the squadrons SIPR token management procedure. Tokens will be limited to the minimum required scope of access for the deployers duty tasks and must be deactivated and returned to the unit when deployment or assignment ends or upon request of the Information Assurance or Security Office. There shall be a contemporaneous audit trail for issuance, modification, and revocation.

Issuance responsibilities:

- Security and management: The Squadron Information Assurance Officer (IAO) or designated authority shall authorize token creation, assign the scope, expiry, and revocation conditions, and ensure appropriate monitoring.

- Token characteristics: Each token is restricted to the user and to the specified mission needs; tokens will be time-bound and automatically expire on the final day of the deployment window unless extended in writing by the approving authority.

- Accountability and reporting: All token issuance actions and revocations shall be recorded in the unit's SIPR token management system with a functional justification. A daily roll-up report shall be forwarded to the Squadron Commander and the Wing Information Security Office.

Distribution: This action memo is to be circulated to the 88th Communications Squadron Tenant Units as required for operational awareness and compliance.

This memorandum directs immediate safety actions following a Class C mishap involving a wing aircraft on 12 May 2026. The wing commander has determined a focused 48-hour safety down day is required to ensure all safety, maintenance, and operational risk management measures are complete before resuming normal flight operations.

1. Effective 0000 local, 15 May 2026, the 4th Fighter Wing (4FW) imposes a 48-hour safety down day for all flight and flying-related operations. The safety down day will end at 2359 local, 16 May 2026, unless extended in writing by the Wing Commander.

2. During the safety down day, the following actions are mandatory:

   a. All flight operations, sorties, and sortie generation directly supporting flight training, local aircrew proficiency, and operational missions are suspended. Non-flying mission-essential tasks (e.g., intelligence, command and control) that do not require aircraft will continue unless otherwise directed.

   b. Commanders at all levels will ensure each aircrew and maintenance member completes a mandatory safety brief led by their unit safety representative covering:

   - Details and initial findings related to the Class C mishap (as releasable),

   - Human factors and risk-environment considerations, and

   - Flight and maintenance standardization reminders and error mitigation techniques.

   c. Maintenance organizations will conduct focused inspections on aircraft and associated ground support equipment, to include:

   - A documented walk-around and systems check of affected aircraft types,

   - Verification of recent maintenance actions and configuration control, and

   - Spot inspections of maintenance logs for procedural compliance.

   d. Unit commanders will review local procedures, crew-rest and scheduling practices, and aircrew training currency to identify potential systemic contributors to the mishap.

   e. All personnel will report safety-related observations or potential hazards through established channels (e.g., ASAP, Military Flight Operations Quality Assurance reporting where applicable, or direct report to unit safety). Significant findings shall be elevated to Wing Safety immediately.

3. The Wing Safety Office (4FW/SE) will:

   a. Lead the wing-level mishap response and coordinate initial fact-finding consistent with AFI 91-204 and applicable investigation guidance.

   b. Provide consolidated safety brief material and inspection checklists to units by 0800 local, 15 May 2026.

   c. Maintain a daily summary of findings and corrective actions and provide a report to the Wing Commander not later than 1700 local, 16 May 2026.

4. The Operations Group Commander (4OG/CC) will:

   a. Ensure all flying squadrons comply with this directive and complete required briefs, inspections, and corrective actions prior to resuming flight activity.

   b. Designate an OG Safety POC (name, rank, and contact information) and provide that POC to Wing Safety no later than 0900 local, 15 May 2026.

   c. Coordinate with Maintenance Group leadership to resolve any maintenance or configuration issues that could affect flight safety.

5. Exceptions to this suspension (e.g., launch to save life, limb, or national-level tasking) require written approval from the Wing Commander.

6. Point of contact for this memorandum is Maj Emily R. Carter, Wing Safety Officer, 4FW/SE, DSN 312-555-0102, emily.carter@usaf.mil, or Capt Ryan T. Alvarez, Chief of Flight Safety, 4OG/SE, DSN 312-555-0150.

FOR THE COMMANDER

JOHN A. SMITH, Col, USAF Commander, 4th Fighter Wing

```

```

Please ensure all personnel who process medical-records requests follow these procedures and coordinate unusual or urgent requests with the point of contact before taking action.
