This memorandum tasks the 88th Communications Squadron (88 CS/SC) to issue temporary SIPR tokens to support an upcoming deployment of maintenance personnel from the 88th Maintenance Group.

1. Action. 88 CS will issue forty (40) temporary SIPR tokens to identified deploying maintainers to enable classified mission-related communications while deployed.

2. Requirements.

a. 88 CS will coordinate with 88 MXG operations and unit deployment managers to receive a roster of the 40 maintainers requiring tokens. The roster will include full name, rank, DoD ID, unit, and estimated deployment dates.

b. Tokens will be issued as temporary credentials with expiration dates matching the deploying members' authorized deployment periods. Tokens must be configured per applicable DAF and DoD guidance for SIPR access and information assurance.

c. 88 CS will maintain an issuance roster and return/expiration accountability record, and provide a copy to 88 MXG plans (88 MXG/CP) upon completion of issuance.

3. Security and accountability. 88 CS will ensure issuance and handling follow applicable information assurance and physical security procedures. No Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) is included with this tasking.

4. Coordination and support. 88 MXG will provide the deployment roster and any required authorization letters or orders no later than 48 hours after receipt of this memorandum.

5. Point of contact. For issuance coordination and questions, contact the 88 MXG deployment office at 88 MXG/CP or the 88 CS Security Office.

6. Suspense. Complete issuance and provide the issuance/ accountability report to 88 MXG/CP by 2026-09-09.

FOR THE COMMANDER

JOHN A. DOE, Col, USAF Commander, 88th Maintenance Group

This memorandum establishes procedures for responding to requests for patient medical records and other protected health information (PHI) received by the 81st Medical Group. Treat each request as controlled unclassified information (CUI) and limit access, use, and disclosure to personnel with an official need to know.

Before releasing any record, route the request to the 81 MDG/SGH Privacy Officer. The Privacy Officer will verify the requester's identity and authority, determine whether the requested disclosure is permitted or required, and document the disposition. Do not release records directly to a requester, an external provider, an attorney, a family member, or another government organization without Privacy Officer review, even when the requester presents an authorization or states that the request is urgent.

At a minimum, the request package must identify the patient, specify the records and date range sought, state the purpose of the request, identify the intended recipient, and include a valid authorization when one is required. Requests involving minors, deceased patients, personal representatives, subpoenas, litigation, law enforcement, occupational or safety investigations, or disclosures outside the Department of Defense must be referred to the Privacy Officer and 81 FSS/JA before any response is sent.

Use approved systems and transmission methods for all PHI. Do not place PHI in unrestricted email, personal cloud storage, removable media, or informal messaging applications. Verify the recipient and address immediately before transmission, use the required encryption or other approved safeguards, and retain the request, review record, authorization, response, and transmission confirmation in the designated patient-records system.

If an unauthorized disclosure, misdirected transmission, loss, or suspected compromise occurs, stop further distribution and notify the Privacy Officer and the 81 MDG/SGH chain of command immediately. Do not delete, alter, or attempt to retrieve evidence without direction. The Privacy Officer will coordinate reporting, mitigation, and any required notification with legal and information-protection officials.

Questions about this memorandum or a specific request will be directed to the 81 MDG/SGH Privacy Officer at 228-555-0147. The attached checklist may be used to screen and route requests, but it does not replace Privacy Officer or legal review.

This memorandum establishes procedures for responding to requests for patient medical records and other protected health information (PHI) received by the 81st Medical Group. Treat each request as controlled unclassified information (CUI) and limit access, use, and disclosure to personnel with an official need to know.

Before releasing any record, route the request to the 81 MDG/SGH Privacy Officer. The Privacy Officer will verify the requester's identity and authority, determine whether the requested disclosure is permitted or required, and document the disposition. Do not release records directly to a requester, an external provider, an attorney, a family member, or another government organization without Privacy Officer review, even when the requester presents an authorization or states that the request is urgent.

At a minimum, the request package must identify the patient, specify the records and date range sought, state the purpose of the request, identify the intended recipient, and include a valid authorization when one is required. Requests involving minors, deceased patients, personal representatives, subpoenas, litigation, law enforcement, occupational or safety investigations, or disclosures outside the Department of Defense must be referred to the Privacy Officer and 81 FSS/JA before any response is sent.

Use approved systems and transmission methods for all PHI. Do not place PHI in unrestricted email, personal cloud storage, removable media, or informal messaging applications. Verify the recipient and address immediately before transmission, use the required encryption or other approved safeguards, and retain the request, review record, authorization, response, and transmission confirmation in the designated patient-records system.

If an unauthorized disclosure, misdirected transmission, loss, or suspected compromise occurs, stop further distribution and notify the Privacy Officer and the 81 MDG/SGH chain of command immediately. Do not delete, alter, or attempt to retrieve evidence without direction. The Privacy Officer will coordinate reporting, mitigation, and any required notification with legal and information-protection officials.

Questions about this memorandum or a specific request will be directed to the 81 MDG/SGH Privacy Officer at 228-555-0147. The attached checklist may be used to screen and route requests, but it does not replace Privacy Officer or legal review.

1. PURPOSE. This memorandum documents a request for Protected Health Information (PHI) maintained by the 21st Medical Group (21 MDG) and establishes handling instructions for release as Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) under applicable Privacy and Records authorities.

2. REQUEST BASIS. The receiving office (21 SPT/SGS) is requesting PHI to support an official, mission-related review consistent with permitted disclosures and the HIPAA Privacy Rule. The request includes the minimum necessary data elements needed to accomplish the stated purpose.

3. RECORDS REQUEST DETAILS. a. Requested record type(s): outpatient encounter summaries, relevant diagnostic test results, and medication lists from 2025-01-01 through 2026-08-31. b. Patient identifier(s): name and DoD ID number as provided in Attachment 1. c. Specific date ranges and locations: visits occurring at JB Elmendorf-Richardson and associated contractor facilities as listed in Attachment 1. d. Format and delivery: electronic transfer via approved DoD channels to the named point of contact (POC) listed in the request.

4. CUI/PRIVACY HANDLING INSTRUCTIONS. a. Marking and distribution: any responsive PHI will be handled as CUI and shared only with authorized individuals performing the stated function. b. Safeguards: access will be limited on a need-to-know basis; systems used for transfer will meet applicable confidentiality and access-control requirements. c. Redaction review: 21 MDG will redact information not necessary to the stated purpose and will withhold data required by law to be protected.

5. RELEASE CONTROLS. a. Accounting of disclosures: a disclosure accounting will be maintained per applicable retention requirements. b. Verification: before release, 21 MDG will verify the requesting office’s authorization and the identity of the POC. c. Timing: PHI will be provided within the timeframes applicable to access/disclosure requests, subject to record retrieval and redaction review.

6. POINTS OF CONTACT. The 21 MDG Privacy and Information Protection office will serve as the primary coordination point for authorization verification, redaction considerations, and secure delivery.

7. ACTION. a. 21 SPT/SGS will confirm that the request includes the minimum necessary information and that the POC is authorized to receive CUI. b. 21 MDG will process the request, apply necessary redactions, and deliver responsive records through approved secure channels.

> If any portion of the request is ambiguous or lacks minimum-necessary justification, 21 MDG will return the request for clarification prior to release.

This memorandum documents the 375th Medical Group's handling of a recent request for Protected Health Information (PHI) received 28 August 2026 and provides instructions for authorized release consistent with controlling authorities.

1. Background. On 28 August 2026, the 375 MDG Privacy Office received a written request from an external legal representative seeking PHI for patient John A. Sample (DOB: 1985-04-12). The request included a signed authorization form dated 27 August 2026 and identification for the requester. The Privacy Office preliminarily validated the identity of the requester and the authenticity of the authorization, but additional verification is required before release.

2. Authorities. Release of PHI is governed by 45 C.F.R. §§160 and 164 (HIPAA Privacy Rule), Department of Defense Medical Records directives, and DoDM 5200.48 concerning Controlled Unclassified Information. When CUI is involved, follow the classification and dissemination controls stated above and consult the unit Privacy Officer.

3. Analysis.

   a. The authorization provided covers treatment records for the period 01 January 2020 through 31 December 2020 and is limited to diagnostic reports and outpatient visit summaries. It does not explicitly authorize release of behavioral health notes, substance abuse treatment records, or third-party psychotherapy notes, which require a separate, specific authorization under applicable law.

   b. The requester represents a non-federal party. Before release to external entities, the Privacy Office must verify the requester’s legal authority (e.g., power of attorney, court order) or receive an authorization that meets HIPAA requirements. Where a court order or subpoena is presented, consult the local SJA and follow DoD release procedures.

4. Action.

   a. Privacy Office (375 MDG/SGOP): Within 3 duty days, complete the following steps and document completion in the PHI Release Log:

   - Re-verify the requester’s identity and authority to receive the PHI.

   - Confirm the authorization specifically includes the categories of records requested; redact any non-authorized sensitive content (behavioral health, SUD treatment, psychotherapy notes) unless separate valid authorization or court order is provided.

   - Prepare redacted copies and a cover letter noting the legal basis for release and the CUI handling instructions.

   b. Legal (375 SJA): Within 2 duty days of receiving notification from the Privacy Office, review the requester’s authority and advise on any additional legal requirements for release.

   c. Release Approval (Group Commander or designated signatory): Approve final release package prior to dissemination; approval must be documented on the PHI Release Log.

5. Handling and Marking. All printed or electronic copies released externally must be marked per CUI guidance. Use the banner and marking: CUI//PRIV. Include the controlled\_by and POC information on the cover letter and on the internal release record. Transmit electronic files via an approved encrypted transfer mechanism; do not send PHI via unsecured email or consumer cloud services.

6. Recordkeeping. Retain copies of the authorization, verification steps, redactions, and the release cover letter in the medical record and in the Privacy Office release file for a minimum of 6 years, or per applicable records retention schedules, whichever is longer.

7. Point of Contact. For questions regarding this memorandum or the status of this request, contact the 375 MDG Privacy Office at (555) 123-4567 or usaf.privacy@us.af.mil.

Attachment: Attachment 1: Records Request and Authorization, 2026-08-28

JEREMY P. HARTMAN Col, USAF Commander, 375th Medical Group

1. Background. On 28 August 2026, the 375 MDG Privacy Office received a written request from an external legal representative seeking PHI for patient John A. Sample (DOB: 1985-04-12). The request included a signed authorization form dated 27 August 2026 and identification for the requester. The Privacy Office preliminarily validated the identity of the requester and the authenticity of the authorization, but additional verification is required before release.

2. Authorities. Release of PHI is governed by 45 C.F.R. §§160 and 164 (HIPAA Privacy Rule), Department of Defense Medical Records directives, and DoDM 5200.48 concerning Controlled Unclassified Information. When CUI is involved, follow the classification and dissemination controls stated above and consult the unit Privacy Officer.

3. Analysis.

   a. The authorization provided covers treatment records for the period 01 January 2020 through 31 December 2020 and is limited to diagnostic reports and outpatient visit summaries. It does not explicitly authorize release of behavioral health notes, substance abuse treatment records, or third-party psychotherapy notes, which require a separate, specific authorization under applicable law.

   b. The requester represents a non-federal party. Before release to external entities, the Privacy Office must verify the requester’s legal authority (e.g., power of attorney, court order) or receive an authorization that meets HIPAA requirements. Where a court order or subpoena is presented, consult the local SJA and follow DoD release procedures.

4. Action.

   a. Privacy Office (375 MDG/SGOP): Within 3 duty days, complete the following steps and document completion in the PHI Release Log:
      - Re-verify the requester’s identity and authority to receive the PHI.
      - Confirm the authorization specifically includes the categories of records requested; redact any non-authorized sensitive content (behavioral health, SUD treatment, psychotherapy notes) unless separate valid authorization or court order is provided.
      - Prepare redacted copies and a cover letter noting the legal basis for release and the CUI handling instructions.

   b. Legal (375 SJA): Within 2 duty days of receiving notification from the Privacy Office, review the requester’s authority and advise on any additional legal requirements for release.

   c. Release Approval (Group Commander or designated signatory): Approve final release package prior to dissemination; approval must be documented on the PHI Release Log.

5. Handling and Marking. All printed or electronic copies released externally must be marked per CUI guidance. Use the banner and marking: CUI//PRIV. Include the controlled_by and POC information on the cover letter and on the internal release record. Transmit electronic files via an approved encrypted transfer mechanism; do not send PHI via unsecured email or consumer cloud services.

6. Recordkeeping. Retain copies of the authorization, verification steps, redactions, and the release cover letter in the medical record and in the Privacy Office release file for a minimum of 6 years, or per applicable records retention schedules, whichever is longer.

7. Point of Contact. For questions regarding this memorandum or the status of this request, contact the 375 MDG Privacy Office at (555) 123-4567 or usaf.privacy@us.af.mil.

Col, USAF

Request waiver of the requirement in AFI 21-101, paragraph 9.3.4, for a dedicated backshop production superintendent during the period 2026 June 15 through 2026 September 30. The 23d Fighter Squadron is temporarily operating with a vacant position while its authorized superintendent completes a permanent change of station and the replacement reports.

The squadron will remain compliant with all aircraft safety, inspection, and documentation requirements. During the requested period, the assistant operations officer will conduct the daily production review, the lead production supervisor will perform the required technical oversight, and the 366th Maintenance Group will review the squadron's production metrics weekly. The attached justification identifies the affected requirement, operational impact, controls, and termination criteria.

Approval of this waiver will prevent an avoidable reduction in sortie-generation capacity while preserving maintenance discipline and commander visibility. The waiver will terminate automatically on 2026 September 30, or earlier upon assignment and qualification of the replacement superintendent.

AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.
authority_line: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Line 1: Name in UPPERCASE as signed, grade, and service. Line 2: Duty title.
signature_block:
  - IVY N. COLE, Col, USAF
  - Commander
# Letterhead lines, top to bottom, all rendered in uppercase. The first is the department title, set larger than the rest. Change that line only for a Joint Command or a DoW agency. The lines below it are your unit's full organization name.
# e.g. [DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE, "HEADQUARTERS [UNIT NAME]"]
letterhead_title:
  - DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE
# Department of War (DoW) or Department of Defense (DoD) seal, shown at the top left of the letterhead. Leave blank for no seal.
letterhead_seal: dow # enum<dow | dod>
# Bold-caps line below the seal. Nothing prints when it is blank, or when there is no seal.
letterhead_seal_subtitle: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Organizational motto, centered in the footer of every page. Supports Markdown emphasis: *italics*, **bold**.
tag_line: "" # richtext(inline)<markdown>
# Classification marking, banner-printed at the top and bottom of every page. Leave blank for no banner, which is what an unclassified document normally carries. Mark per DAFI 16-1404, DoDM 5200.48 for CUI, and applicable DoD guidance.

classification:
  value: ""
# Suffix appended to the banner after a double slash, rendered in uppercase: 'NF' prints as CUI//NF. Leave blank for no suffix.
dissemination: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Cite each reference by organization, type, date, and title. Two or more print as a References block lettered (a), (b), (c); a single one prints in parentheses after the subject, per AFH 33-337. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.

references: [] # array<richtext(inline)<markdown>>

cc: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>

$quill: usaf_memo@0.3.0 # keep verbatim
$kind: main
# U.S. Air Force and Space Force Official Memorandum
# Organization or office symbol, rendered in uppercase. To address a specific person, add their rank and name in parentheses: 'ORG/SYMBOL (LT COL JANE DOE)'. For a long list, enter 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' and name the recipients in the Distribution field.
memo_for:
  - 18 OG/CC
# The office symbol alone when every recipient is on this installation. The full mailing address as well when any recipient is elsewhere, so they can write back. Leave blank for a Memorandum for Record, which prints no FROM line.
memo_from:
  - 18 OSS/CC
# Keep it brief. Capitalize the first letter of each word except articles, prepositions, and conjunctions. Put any suspense date in parentheses. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. Subject of the Memorandum
subject: Airfield Driving Program Audit
# YYYY-MM-DD, printed in the format the Memo Style field selects. Leave blank to use today's date.
date: 2026-05-02
# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.
authority_line: ""
# Line 1: Name in UPPERCASE as signed, grade, and service. Line 2: Duty title.
signature_block:
  - NOAH E. SIMMS, Lt Col, USAF
  - Commander, 18 OSS
# Letterhead lines, top to bottom, all rendered in uppercase. The first is the department title, set larger than the rest. Change that line only for a Joint Command or a DoW agency. The lines below it are your unit's full organization name.
# e.g. [DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE, "HEADQUARTERS [UNIT NAME]"]
letterhead_title:
  - DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE
# Department of War (DoW) or Department of Defense (DoD) seal, shown at the top left of the letterhead. Leave blank for no seal.
letterhead_seal: dow
# Bold-caps line below the seal. Nothing prints when it is blank, or when there is no seal.
letterhead_seal_subtitle: ""
# Organizational motto, centered in the footer of every page. Supports Markdown emphasis: *italics*, **bold**.
tag_line: ""
# Classification marking, banner-printed at the top and bottom of every page. Leave blank for no banner, which is what an unclassified document normally carries. Mark per DAFI 16-1404, DoDM 5200.48 for CUI, and applicable DoD guidance.
# when CUI: controlled_by, poc, category, limited_dissemination
classification:
  value: ""
# Suffix appended to the banner after a double slash, rendered in uppercase: 'NF' prints as CUI//NF. Leave blank for no suffix.
dissemination: ""
# Cite each reference by organization, type, date, and title. Two or more print as a References block lettered (a), (b), (c); a single one prints in parentheses after the subject, per AFH 33-337. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. ["AFMAN 33-326, 25 November 2011, *Preparing Official Communications*", "AFI 33-360, *Publications and Forms Management*" ]
references: []
# Offices or people receiving a courtesy copy, one per line.
# e.g. ["Rank and Name, ORG/SYMBOL"]
cc: []
# Every recipient, listed here when 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' stands in the Memo For field.
distribution: []
# Attachments in the order the memo mentions them. Describe each briefly; do not write 'as stated' or abbreviate. A lone attachment prints unnumbered, two or more are numbered. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. ["Attachment description, YYYY MMM DD"]
attachments: []
# USAF memorandum or DAF headquarters memorandum, per AFH 33-337. DAF dates as 'September 15, 2026' rather than '15 September 2026', and leaves top-level paragraphs unnumbered with a first-line indent.
memo_style: usaf
# Body text size in points; decimals allowed, such as 11.5. AFH 33-337 §5 specifies 12.
font_size: 12
~~~

This memorandum provides the results of the Airfield Driving Program audit and communicates required corrective actions.

~~~
$kind: indorsement
# An endorsing official's response to the memo, or their forwarding of it onward. Indorsements are numbered in card order: 1st Ind, 2d Ind, 3d Ind.
# Office symbol or Rank Name of the endorsing official.
from: 18 OG/CC
# Office symbol or organization receiving the endorsed memo.
for: 18 OSS/CC
# YYYY-MM-DD, the date the endorser signs or forwards the memo — distinct from the originating memo's date, per AFH 33-337 Ch. 14. Leave blank to print a fillable PDF text field for the endorser to type into when signing.
date: ""
# Authority line for this indorsement, printed in uppercase above its signature block. An indorsement has a closing section of its own, so the same rules apply: fill it in when the endorser signs for the commander or the headquarters, leave it blank when the commander signs.
authority_line: ""
# Line 1: Name in UPPERCASE as signed, grade, and service. Line 2: Duty title.
signature_block:
  - INGRID P. CHO, Col, USAF
  - Commander
# 'standard' keeps the indorsement on the action document's page under a one-line header, and moves it to a page of its own, under the fuller header, when it no longer fits. 'separate_page' always begins a new page. 'informal' prints no header at all, so an informal indorsement with an empty body is nothing but a signature block — with no text of its own to hold it to the page, it can open a page alone. Give it a body or an action, or use 'standard'.
format: standard
# The endorser's decision, printed as an either/or line with the choice underlined and the rejected option struck out. Leave blank to omit the line.
action: approve
~~~

$quill: usaf_memo@0.3.0
$kind: main
# U.S. Air Force and Space Force Official Memorandum
# Organization or office symbol, rendered in uppercase. To address a specific person, add their rank and name in parentheses: 'ORG/SYMBOL (LT COL JANE DOE)'. For a long list, enter 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' and name the recipients in the Distribution field.
memo_for:
  - ORG1/SYMBOL
  - ORG2/SYMBOL
# The office symbol alone when every recipient is on this installation. The full mailing address as well when any recipient is elsewhere, so they can write back. Leave blank for a Memorandum for Record, which prints no FROM line.
# e.g. [ORG/SYMBOL, Organization Name, 123 Street Ave, City ST 12345-6789]
memo_from: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
# Keep it brief. Capitalize the first letter of each word except articles, prepositions, and conjunctions. Put any suspense date in parentheses. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. Subject of the Memorandum
subject: !must_fill # richtext(inline)<markdown>
# YYYY-MM-DD, printed in the format the Memo Style field selects. Leave blank to use today's date.
date: "" # date<YYYY-MM-DD>
# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.
# e.g. FOR THE COMMANDER
authority_line: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Line 1: Name in UPPERCASE as signed, grade, and service. Line 2: Duty title.
signature_block: !must_fill # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
  - FIRST M. LAST, Rank, USAF
  - Duty Title
# Letterhead lines, top to bottom, all rendered in uppercase. The first is the department title, set larger than the rest. Change that line only for a Joint Command or a DoW agency. The lines below it are your unit's full organization name.
# e.g. [DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE, "HEADQUARTERS [UNIT NAME]"]
letterhead_title: # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
  - DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE
letterhead_seal: dow # enum<dow | dod>
letterhead_seal_subtitle: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
tag_line: "" # richtext(inline)<markdown>
# Classification marking, banner-printed at the top and bottom of every page. Leave blank for no banner, which is what an unclassified document normally carries. Mark per DAFI 16-1404, DoDM 5200.48 for CUI, and applicable DoD guidance.
# when CUI: controlled_by, poc, category, limited_dissemination
classification: # enum<UNCLASSIFIED | CUI | CONFIDENTIAL | SECRET | TOP SECRET>
  value: ""
# Suffix appended to the banner after a double slash, rendered in uppercase: 'NF' prints as CUI//NF. Leave blank for no suffix.
dissemination: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Cite each reference by organization, type, date, and title. Two or more print as a References block lettered (a), (b), (c); a single one prints in parentheses after the subject, per AFH 33-337. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. ["AFMAN 33-326, 25 November 2011, *Preparing Official Communications*", "AFI 33-360, *Publications and Forms Management*"]
references: [] # array<richtext(inline)<markdown>>
# Offices or people receiving a courtesy copy, one per line.
# e.g. ["Rank and Name, ORG/SYMBOL"]
cc: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
# Every recipient, listed here when 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' stands in the Memo For field.
# e.g. [ORG1/SYMBOL, ORG2/SYMBOL]
distribution: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
# Attachments in the order the memo mentions them. Describe each briefly; do not write 'as stated' or abbreviate. A lone attachment prints unnumbered, two or more are numbered. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. ["Attachment description, YYYY MMM DD"]
attachments: [] # array<richtext(inline)<markdown>>
memo_style: usaf # enum<usaf | daf>
font_size: 12 # number
~~~

On March 18, 2026, I conducted a dormitory inspection of the unaccompanied housing facilities at Redstone Air Force Base, New Mexico. The inspection assessed room cleanliness, sanitation, fire-safety compliance, and adherence to installation standards.

The following rooms were found unsatisfactory during the inspection:

> Building 410, Room 214 — Excessive trash and food waste present; floor and kitchenette required cleaning.\
> Building 412, Room 108 — Egress path obstructed by personal items; smoke detector partially covered.\
> Building 415, Room 327 — Unsanitary bathroom conditions and mold-like substance observed around the shower caulking.

Residents of the identified rooms were notified of the deficiencies and directed to correct them. A follow-up inspection will be conducted no later than March 25, 2026. The dormitory manager will document completion of corrective actions and notify the first sergeant's office of any unresolved deficiencies.

This memorandum documents the inspection results and actions taken.

On 15 March 2026 I conducted a scheduled dormitory inspection of Building 742, Dormitory Section B, at Clearwater Air Force Base. The inspection focused on safety hazards, cleanliness, personal conduct in common areas, and adherence to dormitory policies outlined in the unit dormitory standards.

Overall, the building presented in satisfactory condition; however, I documented isolated deficiencies requiring corrective action. The following rooms were found unsatisfactory during the inspection and require immediate attention and remediation by the assigned occupants:

> Room 742-B101 — accumulation of trash and expired food in refrigerator; improper storage of combustible materials near heater\
> Room 742-B207 — visible mold growth in bathroom ceiling and inadequate ventilation\
> Room 742-B314 — multiple unauthorized electrical appliances and overloaded power strips creating fire hazard

I directed the residents of the identified rooms to correct the deficiencies within 72 hours and to coordinate with dormitory management for any maintenance or pest-control assistance. I also instructed unit leadership to document follow-on checks and to refer repeated or uncorrected violations to the commander for disciplinary action as appropriate.

Point of contact for this memorandum is the undersigned at (555) 123-4567 or john.rivera@clearwater.af.mil.

Respectfully,

JOHN A. RIVERA, SMSgt, USAF First Sergeant, 1st Squadron, 9th Wing

Memorandum for Record

On 2 April 2026, a near-miss occurred on the flightline involving an Aircraft Ground Equipment (AGE) tug during pushback operations near the flightline service area. While the tug and accompanying support personnel were maneuvering in the vicinity of active aircraft, a miscommunication regarding clearance and movement direction created a narrow margin between the tug and an inbound aircraft taxiing path. There were no reported injuries or damage following the incident. Immediate actions included a halt to operations, a stand-down of the affected shift for a safety briefing, and a review of standard operating procedures for tug operations in proximity to active runways.

Witnesses:

> Maj. John A. Smith, USAF Capt. Maria L. Chen, USAF SSgt. Kevin B. Turner, USAF

Further details, corrective actions, and any contributing factors will be documented in the aviation safety follow-up report and reviewed by the Wing Safety Office.


1. Purpose. Document a near-miss on the flightline involving an AGE tug on 2 April 2026.

2. Date/Time. 2026-04-02, approximately 1430 local.

3. Location. Flightline ramp area, AGE staging/turnaround lane.

4. Situation. During aircraft ground operations, an AGE tug (operator on foot) maneuvered adjacent to active work areas. While repositioning, the tug came within close proximity of ground personnel/vehicles moving in the same general area.

5. What Happened (Synopsis).

   a. The operator initiated a repositioning turn at low speed while monitoring immediate surroundings.

   b. Ground personnel with mission-tasked movement entered the area of the tug’s projected path.

   c. The operator stopped and secured the tug before contact; the tug did not strike personnel or equipment.

6. Immediate Actions Taken.

   a. Tug was stopped and removed from the immediate working area.

   b. Personnel were directed to re-establish separation and conform to current ground-movement procedures.

   c. The supervisor on duty was notified and an on-the-spot safety brief was conducted.

7. Witnesses (Roster).

> SGT LUCAS MARTINEZ, USAF\
> TSgt NATALIE WRIGHT, USAF\
> AMN RYAN KIM, USAF\
> CIVILIAN JORDAN REED, Contractor

8. Observed Contributing Factors.

   a. Tug route/turn geometry placed ground movement in the same corridor.

   b. Limited situational cues at the intersection point reduced early recognition of converging paths.

9. Corrective/Preventive Actions.

   a. Reinforce AGE tug movement boundaries and required spotter/signal procedures during ground-activity briefs.

   b. Update local signage/marker placement in the maneuver area to improve visibility of pedestrian/vehicle routing.

   c. Review this event during the next safety stand-down and incorporate into ground-operations training.

10. Point of Contact. 1st Fighter Wing Safety Office.

2. Date/Time. 2026-04-02, approximately 1430 local.

3. Location. Flightline ramp area, AGE staging/turnaround lane.

4. Situation. During aircraft ground operations, an AGE tug (operator on foot) maneuvered adjacent to active work areas. While repositioning, the tug came within close proximity of ground personnel/vehicles moving in the same general area.

5. What Happened (Synopsis).

   a. The operator initiated a repositioning turn at low speed while monitoring immediate surroundings.

   b. Ground personnel with mission-tasked movement entered the area of the tug’s projected path.

   c. The operator stopped and secured the tug before contact; the tug did not strike personnel or equipment.

6. Immediate Actions Taken.

   a. Tug was stopped and removed from the immediate working area.

   b. Personnel were directed to re-establish separation and conform to current ground-movement procedures.

   c. The supervisor on duty was notified and an on-the-spot safety brief was conducted.

7. Witnesses (Roster).

> SGT LUCAS MARTINEZ, USAF\
> TSgt NATALIE WRIGHT, USAF\
> AMN RYAN KIM, USAF\
> CIVILIAN JORDAN REED, Contractor

8. Observed Contributing Factors.

   a. Tug route/turn geometry placed ground movement in the same corridor.

   b. Limited situational cues at the intersection point reduced early recognition of converging paths.

9. Corrective/Preventive Actions.

   a. Reinforce AGE tug movement boundaries and required spotter/signal procedures during ground-activity briefs.

   b. Update local signage/marker placement in the maneuver area to improve visibility of pedestrian/vehicle routing.

   c. Review this event during the next safety stand-down and incorporate into ground-operations training.

10. Point of Contact. 1st Fighter Wing Safety Office.

AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.

# Suffix appended to the banner after a double slash, rendered in uppercase: 'NF' prints as CUI//NF. Leave blank for no suffix.

# Cite each reference by organization, type, date, and title. Two or more print as a References block lettered (a), (b), (c); a single one prints in parentheses after the subject, per AFH 33-337. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.

$quill: usaf_memo@0.3.0
$kind: main
# U.S. Air Force and Space Force Official Memorandum
# Organization or office symbol, rendered in uppercase. To address a specific person, add their rank and name in parentheses: 'ORG/SYMBOL (LT COL JANE DOE)'. For a long list, enter 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' and name the recipients in the Distribution field.
memo_for: !must_fill
  - ORG1/SYMBOL
  - ORG2/SYMBOL
# The office symbol alone when every recipient is on this installation. The full mailing address as well when any recipient is elsewhere, so they can write back. Leave blank for a Memorandum for Record, which prints no FROM line.
# e.g. [ORG/SYMBOL, Organization Name, 123 Street Ave, City ST 12345-6789]
memo_from: []
# Keep it brief. Capitalize the first letter of each word except articles, prepositions, and conjunctions. Put any suspense date in parentheses. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. Subject of the Memorandum
subject: !must_fill
# YYYY-MM-DD, printed in the format the Memo Style field selects. Leave blank to use today's date.
date: 2026-02-18
# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.
# e.g. FOR THE COMMANDER
authority_line: ""
# Line 1: Name in UPPERCASE as signed, grade, and service. Line 2: Duty title.
signature_block: !must_fill
  - FIRST M. LAST, Rank, USAF
  - Duty Title
# Letterhead lines, top to bottom, all rendered in uppercase. The first is the department title, set larger than the rest. Change that line only for a Joint Command or a DoW agency. The lines below it are your unit's full organization name.
# e.g. [DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE, "HEADQUARTERS [UNIT NAME]"]

COL LENA M. BROOKS, USAF Commander

This memorandum announces a budget lock for Fiscal Year (FY) 27 Communications accounts managed by 42 CS. Effective immediately, no changes, realignments, obligation, or de-obligation actions may be initiated against FY27 communications funds without prior written approval from 42 CS/CC.

This freeze is necessary to ensure accurate close-out, prevent inadvertent obligations that could create cascading funding shortfalls, and allow leadership to reconcile outstanding requirements before fiscal year-end. The budget lock applies to all communications-related O\&M, MILPERS, and reimbursable lines of accounting under 42 CS purview.

Requests for exceptions must be submitted in writing to 42 CS/CC and include:

- Description of the requirement and justification for immediate funding action.

- Amount, funding line(s) of accounting, and anticipated obligation date.

- Impact if the request is denied, including mission degradation or safety concerns.

42 CS/CC will adjudicate exception requests on a case-by-case basis. For planning and scheduling, organizations are encouraged to review open purchase requests and planned obligations now and coordinate with 42 CS Financial Management and Budget personnel.

Point of contact for this action is Capt John A. Example, 42 CS/FM, at (555) 123-4567 or john.example@us.af.mil.

Respectfully,

RHEA T. GOMEZ, Lt Col, USAF Commander

The transfer includes electronically transmitted and paper outpatient records for a limited cohort of patients for treatment-related purposes only. All records were screened to ensure release is consistent with Privacy Act and HIPAA requirements; disclosures were limited to the minimum necessary information, and appropriate patient authorizations and consent documentation were obtained and retained in the health record.

The 88 MDG implemented procedural safeguards during the transfer, including encrypted electronic transmission where applicable, secured courier handling for paper records, and a recipient-point-of-contact validation process at Mercy General Hospital to confirm authorized receipt. Any subsequent requests for additional records or disclosures from the civilian facility will require documentation of patient authorization or a valid legal authority and should be coordinated through 88 MDG/SGH to ensure continued compliance with applicable privacy and medical records regulations.

CTI Sharing Procedures for Coalition Partners

This memorandum provides the CTI sharing procedures applicable to Coalition Partners per the 67th Wing/Intelligence Network, including limitations and dissemination controls. The procedures herein are intended to standardize how CTI is shared with coalition partners to protect sensitive information and ensure secure collaboration.

1. Applicability and scope

- This memorandum applies to all CTI shared with coalition partners under CTI category handling.

2. Roles and responsibilities

- POC: Maj Owen Blake, DSN 312-555-0199, owen.blake@us.af.mil.

- 67 CW/IN coordinates CTI sharing with 16 AF/A2 and coalition partners.

3. Procedures

- CTI sharing shall follow established classification, labeling, and dissemination controls.

- Information marked CUI and CTI must be shared on a NOFORN basis with eligible coalition partners as defined by the sharing agreement.

4. References

- *DOD Information Security Program, DoD Directive 5210.48*

- *Coalition Partnership Information Sharing, Best Practices for Multinational Intelligence Cooperation*

CTI Sharing Procedures for Coalition Partners

This memorandum provides the CTI sharing procedures applicable to Coalition Partners per the 67th Wing/Intelligence Network, including limitations and dissemination controls. The procedures herein are intended to standardize how CTI is shared with coalition partners to protect sensitive information and ensure secure collaboration.

1. Applicability and scope

- This memorandum applies to all CTI shared with coalition partners under CTI category handling.

2. Roles and responsibilities

- POC: Maj Owen Blake, DSN 312-555-0199, owen.blake@us.af.mil.

- 67 CW/IN coordinates CTI sharing with 16 AF/A2 and coalition partners.

3. Procedures

- CTI sharing shall follow established classification, labeling, and dissemination controls.

- Information marked CUI and CTI must be shared on a NOFORN basis with eligible coalition partners as defined by the sharing agreement.

4. References

- *DOD Information Security Program, DoD Directive 5210.48*

- *Coalition Partnership Information Sharing, Best Practices for Multinational Intelligence Cooperation*

This memorandum establishes the CTI sharing procedures applicable to Coalition Partners in accordance with the controls and restrictions associated with CTI and CUI markings. The procedures herein standardize how CTI is shared with coalition partners to protect sensitive information and ensure secure collaboration, while complying with NOFORN dissemination restrictions.

1. Applicability and scope

- Point of Contact (POC): Maj Owen Blake, DSN 312-555-0199, owen.blake@us.af.mil.

- Information marked CUI and CTI must be shared on a NOFORN basis with eligible coalition partners as defined by the sharing agreement.
- All CTI shared with coalition partners must be treated as controlled and handled in accordance with the DoD Information Security Program and related policies.

4. References
- *DOD Information Security Program*
- *Coalition Partnership Information Sharing: Best Practices*

This memorandum delineates procedures for sharing Controlled Technical Information (CTI) with authorized coalition partners. It establishes required handling, approval, and transmission steps to ensure compliance with CUI policy and to protect CTI from unauthorized disclosure.

1. Authorities and Scope

a. This memo implements CTI sharing within the scope of existing DoD and Air Force guidance, and applies to all 67 CW personnel who create, process, or transmit CTI to coalition partners.

b. CTI shared under these procedures remains CUI and is controlled by 67 CW/IN. Dissemination is limited as indicated above (NOFORN).

2. Approval and Sponsorship

a. All CTI disclosures to coalition partners require prior written approval from the 67 CW/IN Director of Intelligence or their delegated representative.

b. Requests for CTI sharing will include a justification, list of recipients, handling instructions, and the authorization period. Submit requests to 67 CW/IN via secure channels.

3. Handling and Marking

a. Mark all CTI with the CUI banner and the controlling authority (67 CW/IN). Clearly annotate any additional dissemination controls (e.g., NOFORN).

b. Maintain accountability records for each CTI transmission, including date, recipients, transmission method, and approval authority.

4. Transmission Methods

a. Transmit CTI to coalition partners only over approved secure networks or encrypted email systems that meet DoD security requirements.

b. When physical transfer is necessary, use validated courier services and ensure materials are sealed and logged.

5. Recipient Obligations

a. Confirm that coalition recipients have the requisite authorization and safeguarding measures in place before transmitting CTI.

b. Require recipients to acknowledge handling restrictions and to report suspected compromise immediately to 67 CW/IN.

6. Reporting and Oversight

a. Report any actual or suspected unauthorized disclosures to 67 CW/IN and follow applicable incident response procedures.

b. 67 CW/IN will conduct periodic reviews of CTI sharing activity and compliance with these procedures.

Point of contact for this memorandum is Maj Owen Blake, DSN 312-555-0199, owen.blake@us.af.mil.

FOR THE DIRECTOR OF INTELLIGENCE

OWEN BLAKE, Maj, USAF Director of Intelligence

The memorandum reviews the privacy considerations associated with the transfer of outpatient medical records from 88 MDG to a civilian hospital. Ensuring compliance with pertinent privacy regulations, the transfer process has been scrutinized to safeguard Protected Health Information (PHI). All documentation and data sharing protocols follow the established guidelines to prevent unauthorized access or dissemination.

The transfer involved coordination with the civilian healthcare provider to ensure secure handling of medical records. This process included verifying recipient credentials, encrypting electronic records, and documenting the transfer for accountability. By adhering to the strict privacy standards, the transfer maintains the confidentiality and integrity of service members’ medical information.

The memorandum reviews the privacy considerations associated with the transfer of outpatient medical records from 88 MDG to a civilian hospital. Ensuring compliance with pertinent privacy regulations, the transfer process has been scrutinized to safeguard Protected Health Information (PHI). All documentation and data sharing protocols follow the established guidelines to prevent unauthorized access or dissemination.

The transfer involved coordination with the civilian healthcare provider to ensure secure handling of medical records. This process included verifying recipient credentials, encrypting electronic records, and documenting the transfer for accountability. By adhering to the strict privacy standards, the transfer maintains the confidentiality and integrity of service members’ medical information.

Controlled Technical Information (CTI) is essential to mission success and requires strict handling protocols to ensure its protection while enabling coalition partner collaboration. This memorandum outlines the procedures for sharing CTI with coalition partners under the authority of 67 CW/IN.

1. Sharing Authorization and Controls

1\.1. All CTI sharing with coalition partners must be coordinated through and authorized by 67 CW/IN, the controlling office, which manages dissemination controls and access permissions.

1\.2. Recipients are required to adhere to all applicable regulations governing CTI, including but not limited to DAFI 16-1404 and DoDM 5200.48.

2. Points of Contact

2\.1. For all matters concerning CTI sharing procedures, the primary point of contact is Maj Owen Blake, Director of Intelligence, 67 CW/IN.

2\.2. Contact details are DSN 312-555-0199 and owen.blake@us.af.mil.

3. Dissemination Restrictions

3\.1. Dissemination of CTI authorized by this memorandum is strictly limited to NOFORN (No Foreign Nationals) and controlled accordingly.

3\.2. Unauthorized sharing, reproduction, or transmission of controlled information outside authorized channels is prohibited and subject to disciplinary action.

4. Training and Compliance

4\.1. Personnel handling CTI must complete required training on handling classified and controlled information and remain compliant with all pertinent directives.

4\.2. Regular audits and reviews will be conducted by 67 CW/IN to ensure ongoing compliance with CTI sharing protocols.

Maj Owen Blake Director of Intelligence 67 CW/IN

**Subject:** Personally Identifiable Information Incident (PII) — Incident Response

This memorandum announces the Air Force/Space Force incident response for a PII event. The 502nd Air Base Wing (502 ABW) has activated the appropriate incident response measures and will conduct a comprehensive assessment of the incident to determine scope, data affected, and mitigation actions. All applicable components will coordinate with the Defense Privacy Office and follow DoD privacy guidance to protect affected individuals and minimize risk of further exposure. The incident response will be executed in accordance with AFI/DoD privacy requirements and applicable DoD policy.

This office designates a single point of contact and oversight for the PII incident. The PII incident response team will solicit, collect, and maintain evidence, preserve chain of custody where required, and report findings to leadership and designated stakeholders. Concurrently, the team will implement containment, eradication, and recovery steps and prepare a lessons-learned brief for continuous improvement.

- Reporting steps: 
  - PII incident reports must be directed to SMSgt Dana Ruiz, POC, DSN 312-429-7701, dana.ruiz@us.af.mil.
  - Provide incident details including date/time discovered, data types involved, number of affected individuals, and initial containment actions.
  - Initiate immediate containment and mitigate exposure; preserve logs and evidence; notify appropriate authorities per DoD policy.
  - Coordinate with affected individuals and program managers on notification requirements and remediation actions.
  - Document actions, timelines, and responsible owners for auditability; prepare the final incident closure package.

This memorandum notifies addressees of a recently discovered incident involving the unauthorized exposure of personally identifiable information (PII) within 502nd Air Base Wing systems. Initial analysis indicates the incident may affect a limited number of personnel records. The purpose of this notice is to (a) inform responsible offices, (b) direct immediate reporting and containment steps, and (c) establish a suspense for initial incident reporting and mitigation actions.

Upon receipt of this memorandum, organizations with potential involvement or responsibility will take immediate actions to limit further exposure, preserve evidence, and support investigative efforts. Do not alter, delete, or destroy any system logs or records that could pertain to the incident. Coordinate all actions with 502 ABW/A6 and legal counsel to ensure chain-of-custody and privileged communications are maintained.

Reporting steps (take all that apply):

- Immediately notify 502 ABW/A6 (Controlled By office) with the subject line: "PII Incident — Initial Report".

- Contact POC: SMSgt Dana Ruiz, DSN 312-429-7701, dana.ruiz@us.af.mil to report findings and obtain further instructions.

- Submit an initial incident report to 502 ABW/JA and 502 ABW/A1 within the suspense date of 22 May 2026.

- Preserve all relevant logs, files, removable media, and communications in accordance with guidance from 502 ABW/A6 and 502 ABW/JA.

- If Personally Identifiable Information of Service members or DoD civilians is confirmed, follow applicable notification and credit protection procedures as directed by 502 ABW/JA and higher headquarters.

Point of contact for technical coordination is 502 ABW/A6: SMSgt Dana Ruiz, DSN 312-429-7701, dana.ruiz@us.af.mil.

\~

$quill: usaf_memo@0.3.0
$kind: main
# U.S. Air Force and Space Force Official Memorandum
# Organization or office symbol, rendered in uppercase. To address a specific person, add their rank and name in parentheses: 'ORG/SYMBOL (LT COL JANE DOE)'. For a long list, enter 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' and name the recipients in the Distribution field.
memo_for:
  - 67 CW/IN
# The office symbol alone when every recipient is on this installation. The full mailing address as well when any recipient is elsewhere, so they can write back. Leave blank for a Memorandum for Record, which prints no FROM line.
# e.g. [ORG/SYMBOL, Organization Name, 123 Street Ave, City ST 12345-6789]
memo_from: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
# Keep it brief. Capitalize the first letter of each word except articles, prepositions, and conjunctions. Put any suspense date in parentheses. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. Subject of the Memorandum
subject: CTI Sharing Procedures for Coalition Partners
date: 2026-07-11
# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.
# e.g. FOR THE COMMANDER
authority_line: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Line 1: Name in UPPERCASE as signed, grade, and service. Line 2: Duty title.
signature_block: !must_fill # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
  - OWEN BLAKE, Maj, USAF
  - Director of Intelligence
# Letterhead lines, top to bottom, all rendered in uppercase. The first is the department title, set larger than the rest. Change that line only for a Joint Command or a DoW agency. The lines below it are your unit's full organization name.
# e.g. [DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE, "HEADQUARTERS [UNIT NAME]"]
letterhead_title: # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
  - DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE
# Department of War (DoW) or Department of Defense (DoD) seal, shown at the top left of the letterhead. Leave blank for no seal.
letterhead_seal: dow # enum<dow | dod>
# Bold-caps line below the seal. Nothing prints when it is blank, or when there is no seal.
letterhead_seal_subtitle: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Organizational motto, centered in the footer of every page. Supports Markdown emphasis: *italics*, **bold**.
tag_line: "" # richtext(inline)<markdown>
# Classification marking, banner-printed at the top and bottom of every page. Leave blank for no banner, which is what an unclassified document normally carries. Mark per DAFI 16-1404, DoDM 5200.48 for CUI, and applicable DoD guidance.
# when CUI: controlled_by, poc, category, limited_dissemination
classification: # enum<UNCLASSIFIED | CUI | CONFIDENTIAL | SECRET | TOP SECRET>
  value: ""
# Suffix appended to the banner after a double slash, rendered in uppercase: 'NF' prints as CUI//NF. Leave blank for no suffix.
dissemination: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Cite each reference by organization, type, date, and title. Two or more print as a References block lettered (a), (b), (c); a single one prints in parentheses after the subject, per AFH 33-337. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. ["AFMAN 33-326, 25 November 2011, *Preparing Official Communications*", "AFI 33-360, *Publications and Forms Management*"]
references:
  - islands: []
    lines:
      - containers: []
        kind: para
    marks:
      - end: 79
        start: 35
        type: emph
    text: Joint Task Force Operations, 2023, Guidelines for Coalition Information Sharing
  - islands: []
    lines:
      - containers: []
        kind: para
    marks:
      - end: 79
        start: 29
        type: emph
    text: DOD Directive 5200.48, 2022, Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) Guidance
# Offices or people receiving a courtesy copy, one per line.
# e.g. ["Rank and Name, ORG/SYMBOL"]
cc: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
# Every recipient, listed here when 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' stands in the Memo For field.
# e.g. [ORG1/SYMBOL, ORG2/SYMBOL]
distribution: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
# Attachments in the order the memo mentions them. Describe each briefly; do not write 'as stated' or abbreviate. A lone attachment prints unnumbered, two or more are numbered. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. ["Attachment description, YYYY MMM DD"]
attachments: [] # array<richtext(inline)<markdown>>
# USAF memorandum or DAF headquarters memorandum, per AFH 33-337. DAF dates as 'September 15, 2026' rather than '15 September 2026', and leaves top-level paragraphs unnumbered with a first-line indent.
memo_style: usaf # enum<usaf | daf>
# Body text size in points; decimals allowed, such as 11.5. AFH 33-337 §5 specifies 12.
font_size: 12 # number
~~~

The first paragraph. Top-level paragraphs are auto-numbered; do not add manual numbering.

- Nested bullets are automatically lettered.

Lines that take no number, letter, or bullet — a roster of names, an address — go in a block quote, typeset as written. End a line with a backslash to break it.

> MAJ Owen Blake, Maj, USAF\

To: 76 MXW/CC Depot Throughput Reporting Change

1. This policy memo informs depot throughput reporting requirements and reflects the HQ AFMC/A4 position.

2. The change requires a 48-hour throughput reporting metric for depot operations. Current capability does not consistently meet this standard without additional resources.

3. Rationale: The depot cannot meet the 48-hour metric without overtime funding and accompanying personnel authorities to sustain extended operations and overflow management, particularly during surge conditions. The current staffing and funding profile constrains our ability to align with the new metric without impacting other critical operations.

4. Effect: If implemented without overtime funding, the depot risks increased backlogs, degraded on-time delivery, and reduced mission readiness.

5. Requested action: HQ AFMC/A4 is requested to review and approve the policies, or propose corrective actions and resource requirements to enable meeting the 48-hour target.

Effective immediately, depot throughput reporting will use a 48-hour metric for the applicable depot maintenance workload. This change is intended to provide a consistent measure of responsiveness and improve visibility of production performance across the command.

Implementation of the new metric requires the 76th Maintenance Wing to sustain production activity beyond the currently funded duty day. The wing cannot meet the 48-hour metric without overtime funding. Accordingly, 76 MXW/CC is requested to identify the overtime requirement and coordinate funding before the metric is used as a performance expectation.

Until overtime funding is provided, report actual throughput against the 48-hour metric and identify cases in which the metric was not met because available duty-hour resources were insufficient. ~~~

The 76th Maintenance Wing cannot meet the new 48-hour depot throughput metric without overtime funding. Existing funded manpower and duty-hour resources are insufficient to sustain the required turnaround time. We therefore disapprove implementation of the metric as a performance expectation until the necessary overtime funding is provided.

1. Purpose. This memorandum announces a change to depot throughput reporting requirements to support improved visibility of repair-cycle performance.

2. Reporting Metric. Effective immediately, depots will report performance against the new 48-hour metric for throughput processing.

3. Implementation Guidance. HQ AFMC/A4 will provide the associated reporting instructions and system updates through separate coordination.

4. Point of Contact. Questions regarding interpretation of the new reporting metric should be directed to HQ AFMC/A4, Logistics Division.

~~~
$kind: indorsement
# composable (0..N)
# An endorsing official's response to the memo, or their forwarding of it onward. Indorsements are numbered in card order: 1st Ind, 2d Ind, 3d Ind.
# Office symbol or Rank Name of the endorsing official.
from: 76 MXW/CC # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Office symbol or organization receiving the endorsed memo.
for: HQ AFMC/A4 # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# YYYY-MM-DD, the date the endorser signs or forwards the memo — distinct from the originating memo's date, per AFH 33-337. Leave blank to print a fillable PDF text field for the endorser to type into when signing.
date: "" # date<YYYY-MM-DD>
# Authority line for this indorsement, printed in uppercase above its signature block. An indorsement has a closing section of its own, so the same rules apply: fill it in when the endorser signs for the commander or the headquarters, leave it blank when the commander signs.
authority_line: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Line 1: Name in UPPERCASE as signed, grade, and service. Line 2: Duty title.
signature_block:
  - NATHAN Y. BROOKS, Col, USAF
  - Commander
# 'standard' keeps the indorsement on the action document's page under a one-line header, and moves it to a page of its own, under the fuller header, when it no longer fits. 'separate_page' always begins a new page. 'informal' prints no header at all, so an informal indorsement with an empty body is nothing but a signature block — with no text of its own to hold it to the page, it can open a page alone. Give it a body or an action, or use 'standard'.
format: standard
# The endorser's decision, printed as an either/or line with the choice underlined and the rejected option struck out. Leave blank to omit the line. The wording follows the indorsement's place in the chain: the last one is the approval authority and reads Approve/Disapprove, every earlier one is a coordinating official and reads Concur/Nonconcur. Use 'undecided' to print the pair unmarked, for the endorser to mark by hand.
action: disapprove
~~~

The 76th Maintenance Wing cannot meet the new 48-hour depot throughput metric as directed without additional overtime funding. Current resource levels and scheduled labor availability are insufficient to sustain the throughput processing timelines required to achieve the metric consistently.

The 76th Maintenance Wing cannot meet the newly mandated 48-hour depot throughput reporting metric without supplemental funding to cover required overtime. Our current manning and scheduled workload make the 48-hour turnaround unachievable within allocated duty hours. Implementing this metric without overtime resources will risk maintenance quality, increase fatigue-related errors, and negatively impact aircraft availability.

Recommendation: Disapprove the new 48-hour metric as currently funded. Request HQ AFMC/A4 either provide overtime funding to support the accelerated reporting tempo or adopt a phased implementation that allows units to adjust manpower and procedures.

Effective October 1, 2026, organizations will apply the civilian hiring freeze guidance to civilian hiring actions within their areas of responsibility. The Ready Aircrew Program (RAP) adjustments described herein are intended to enhance readiness, training continuity, and safety across the Air Force. The adjustments streamline qualification timelines, emphasize crew resource management, and align with the latest combat readiness directives to ensure our aircrews are proficient and prepared for accelerating pacing and evolving mission demands.

Key changes include revised minimum flight-hour thresholds, updated simulator and training-device requirements, and expanded cross-crew interchange policies to support mission pacing and redeployment cycles. These changes are designed to reduce scheduling friction while preserving rigorous training standards and operational safety.

All field commands and aircrew units will implement these changes within the current training cycle, with progress tracked through established RAP governance mechanisms. For policy clarification or implementation support, questions should be directed to HQ USAF/A3.

tag_line: ""

# Suffix appended to the banner after a double slash, rendered in uppercase: 'NF' prints as CUI//NF. Leave blank for no suffix.

references: []

attachments: []

This memorandum provides adjustments to the Ready Aircrew Program to enhance squadron readiness and standardize administrative processes across ALMAJCOM. Effective immediately, commanders will update local SOPs to align with HQ USAF/A3 guidance on crew availability reporting, currency tracking, and contingency recall procedures.

Commanders will ensure aircrew training schedules prioritize critical mission-essential qualifications and risk-manage non-mission-critical training when necessary to preserve deployable crew packages. HQ USAF/A3 will publish a follow-on implementation checklist and point of contact for validation of locally generated waivers or deviations.

Please direct questions regarding implementation or policy interpretation to HQ USAF/A3's Aircrew Readiness Division. Thank you for your support in maintaining combat-ready aircrew and ensuring consistent application of these adjustments across the command.

The Satellite Catalog Hygiene Sprint will improve the accuracy, currency, and operational utility of space object records supporting Space Operations Command. S3 will lead a focused review of catalog data and coordinate corrections with responsible mission partners.

The sprint will complete the following catalog clean-up tasks:

- Validate catalog records against authoritative source data.

  - Reconcile object names, identifiers, and ownership fields.

  - Flag records with conflicting or missing values.

- Remove or resolve duplicate entries.

  - Compare duplicate candidates using provenance and update history.

  - Preserve the authoritative record and document disposition.

- Establish follow-up controls for catalog maintenance.

  - Assign owners for unresolved discrepancies.

  - Record corrective actions and review dates.

S3 will provide a completion summary to SpOC/CC identifying corrected records, unresolved discrepancies, and recommended controls for sustaining catalog hygiene.

# U.S. Air Force and Space Force Official Memorandum
# Organization or office symbol, rendered in uppercase. To address a specific person, add their rank and name in parentheses: 'ORG/SYMBOL (LT COL JANE DOE)'. For a long list, enter 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' and name the recipients in the Distribution field.
memo_for:
  - 42 ABW/CC

# The office symbol alone when every recipient is on this installation. The full mailing address as well when any recipient is elsewhere, so they can write back. Leave blank for a Memorandum for Record, which prints no FROM line.
memo_from: []

# Keep it brief. Capitalize the first letter of each word except articles, prepositions, and conjunctions. Put any suspense date in parentheses. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. Subject of the Memorandum
subject: Fiscal Year 27 Communications Budget Lock

yyyy_mm_dd, printed in the format the Memo Style field selects. Leave blank to use today's date.
date: 2026-09-15

# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.
authority_line: ""

# Line 1: Name in UPPERCASE as signed, grade, and service. Line 2: Duty title.
signature_block:
  - RHEA T. GOMEZ, Lt Col, USAF
  - Commander

# Letterhead lines, top to bottom, all rendered in uppercase. The first is the department title, set larger than the rest. Change that line only for a Joint Command or a DoW agency. The lines below it are your unit's full organization name.
# e.g. [DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE, "HEADQUARTERS [UNIT NAME]"]
letterhead_title:
  - DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE
# Department of War (DoW) or Department of Defense (DoD) seal, shown at the top left of the letterhead. Leave blank for no seal.
letterhead_seal: ""
# Bold-caps line below the seal. Nothing prints when it is blank, or when there is no seal.
letterhead_seal_subtitle: ""
# Organizational motto, centered in the footer of every page. Supports Markdown emphasis: *italics*, **bold**.
tag_line: ""
# Classification marking, banner-printed at the top and bottom of every page. Leave blank for no banner, which is what an unclassified document normally carries. Mark per DAFI 16-1404, DoDM 5200.48 for CUI, and applicable DoD guidance.
classification:
  value: ""
# Suffix appended to the banner after a double slash, rendered in uppercase: 'NF' prints as CUI//NF. Leave blank for no suffix.
dissemination: ""
# Cite each reference by organization, type, date, and title. Two or more print as a References block lettered (a), (b), (c); a single one prints in parentheses after the subject, per AFH 33-337. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. ["AFMAN 33-326, 25 November 2011, *Preparing Official Communications*", "AFI 33-360, *Publications and Forms Management*"]
references: []
# Offices or people receiving a courtesy copy, one per line.
# e.g. ["Rank and Name, ORG/SYMBOL"]
cc: []
# Every recipient, listed here when 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' stands in the Memo For field.

The Space Force will execute a satellite catalog hygiene sprint to improve the accuracy, completeness, and timeliness of resident space object records. This effort will focus on rapid identification and correction of duplicate entries, stale element sets, and unresolved object associations that degrade operational decision-making.

During the sprint, the S3 team will coordinate the following catalog clean-up tasks:

- Review and reconcile duplicate catalog entries across current mission data sets.

  - Validate ownership, launch source, and current status for each duplicate candidate.

  - Remove or merge records only after source-data confirmation and peer review.

- Identify stale or low-confidence element sets for update or retirement.

  - Prioritize objects with extended periods of non-corroborated tracking.

  - Flag records requiring additional sensor coverage or analytic validation.

- Resolve unresolved object associations and improve record traceability.

  - Match debris fragments, maneuvering objects, and parent bodies where feasible.

  - Document all changes in the catalog audit trail for future review.

This sprint supports improved space domain awareness and will be coordinated with affected mission partners as needed. Please direct questions or recommended additions to S3.


This memorandum initiates a focused Satellite Catalog Hygiene Sprint to improve the accuracy, completeness, and timeliness of our orbital object catalog. The sprint will prioritize removal of duplicate entries, reconciliation of uncertain track data, and updates to metadata fields that directly affect tasking and conjunction assessment workflows. S3 requests SpOC/CC endorsement to allocate cross-functional support from flight dynamics, space surveillance, and C2 units for a concentrated effort during the first quarter of CY27.

Planned tasks for the catalog clean-up effort include:

- a. Verify and merge duplicate catalog entries where corroborating tracking data exists

  - (1) Cross-check radar and optical track correlations to confirm identity prior to merge

  - (2) Retain provenance fields and log merge rationale for auditability

- b. Reconcile objects with uncertain orbital elements

  - (1) Schedule follow-up observations and incorporate refined state vectors

  - (2) Flag objects requiring further characterization and assign assessment leads

- c. Update and standardize metadata fields impacting operations

  - (1) Ensure launch/source, owner/operator, and object type fields conform to authoritative catalogs

  - (2) Propagate corrected metadata to downstream consumers and notify stakeholders

KIRA L. DONOVAN Col, USSF Director of Operations


The 26th North Operating Squadron (26 NOS) will establish a 24/7 Network Operations Help Desk to support the 67th Wing network services and incident response. The desk will function as the central point of contact for network-related incidents, service requests, and routine inquiries, ensuring rapid triage and escalation to appropriate augmentees as needed.

- Core mission: sustain continuous monitoring, fault diagnosis, and remediation for critical network services.

  - Tiered response: 24/7 front-line triage, on-call escalation, and rapid escalation to specialized teams when required.

  - Service coverage: primary data pathways, firewall policies, VPN access, and network performance metrics.

- Ancillary roles: liaison with information assurance, security operations, and help desk coordination with external vendors.

The Manning section below outlines staffing, shift coverage, and a concise on-call roster to ensure 24/7 availability.

> CESAR A. MOLINA Lt Col, USAF Commander, 26 NOS roster may be expanded as needed for surge periods or major incidents.

- Manning and roster

  - 24/7 Desk Manager

  - Network Operations Technician (2x)

  - Help Desk Specialist (2x)

  - On-call Tier-2 Escalation Lead

  - Roster (four-person sample):

    > 1. AMANDA R. LOPEZ, Capt, USAF
    >
    > 2. DANIEL J. REYES, Maj, USAF
    >
    > 3. KEVIN L. PARKER, SMSgt, USAF
    >
    > 4. SARAH K. NGUYEN, MSgt, USAF

Hours of operation and service hours:

- 24/7 operations with minimum staffing to meet incident demand and service level targets.

  - Core hours: 0000-2300 local with on-call coverage during off-hours for escalation.

  - Surge periods: temporary reallocation of personnel during major incidents or maintenance windows.

Escalation procedure:

- When incidents require escalation beyond front-line triage, the Desk Manager will engage:

  - Tier-2 escalation: Network Engineer on-call

  - Tier-3 escalation: Subject-matter expert or vendor liaison

- Time to initial response targets:

  - Critical network outages: acknowledge within 15 minutes

  - High-priority incidents: acknowledge within 30 minutes

Suspense for comments and coordination:

- Comments due by 15 March 2026 to 26 NOS/CC. The memo will be revised for distribution to 67 CW and 26 NOS leadership based on feedback received by the suspense date.
