$quill: usaf_memo@0.3.0
$kind: main
# U.S. Air Force and Space Force Official Memorandum
# Organization or office symbol, rendered in uppercase. To address a specific person, add their rank and name in parentheses: 'ORG/SYMBOL (LT COL JANE DOE)'. For a long list, enter 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' and name the recipients in the Distribution field.
memo_for:
  - 88th Communications Squadron
  - Wright-Patterson AFB
# The office symbol alone when every recipient is on this installation. The full mailing address as well when any recipient is elsewhere, so they can write back. Leave blank for a Memorandum for Record, which prints no FROM line.
# e.g. [ORG/SYMBOL, Organization Name, 123 Street Ave, City ST 12345-6789]
memo_from: []
# Keep it brief. Capitalize the first letter of each word except articles, prepositions, and conjunctions. Put any suspense date in parentheses. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. Subject of the Memorandum
subject: Continuity of Operations Tabletop After Action
# YYYY-MM-DD, printed in the format the Memo Style field selects. Leave blank to use today's date.
date: "2026-03-12"
# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.
# e.g. FOR THE COMMANDER
authority_line: ""
# Line 1: Name in UPPERCASE as signed, grade, and service. Line 2: Duty title.
signature_block:
  - Jordan Hale, Capt, USAF
  - Flight Commander
# Letterhead lines, top to bottom, all rendered in uppercase. The first is the department title, set larger than the rest. Change that line only for a Joint Command or a DoW agency. The lines below it are your unit's full organization name.
# e.g. [DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE, "HEADQUARTERS [UNIT NAME]"]
letterhead_title:
  - DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE
# Department of War (DoW) or Department of Defense (DoD) seal, shown at the top left of the letterhead. Leave blank for no seal.
letterhead_seal: ""
# Bold-caps line below the seal. Nothing prints when it is blank, or when there is no seal.
letterhead_seal_subtitle: ""
# Organizational motto, centered in the footer of every page. Supports Markdown emphasis: *italics*, **bold**.
tag_line: ""
# Classification marking, banner-printed at the top and bottom of every page. Leave blank for no banner, which is what an unclassified document normally carries. Mark per DAFI 16-1404, DoDM 5200.48 for CUI, and applicable DoD guidance.
# when CUI: controlled_by, poc, category, limited_dissemination
classification:
  value: ""
# Suffix appended to the banner after a double slash, rendered in uppercase: 'NF' prints as CUI//NF. Leave blank for no suffix.
dissemination: ""
# Cite each reference by organization, type, date, and title. Two or more print as a References block lettered (a), (b), (c); a single one prints in parentheses after the subject, per AFH 33-337. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. ["AFMAN 33-326, 25 November 2011, *Preparing Official Communications*", "AFI 33-360, *Publications and Forms Management*"]
references: []
# Offices or people receiving a courtesy copy, one per line.
# e.g. ["Rank and Name, ORG/SYMBOL"]
cc: []
# Every recipient, listed here when 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' stands in the Memo For field.
# e.g. [ORG1/SYMBOL, ORG2/SYMBOL]
distribution: []
# Attachments in the order the memo mentions them. Describe each briefly; do not write 'as stated' or abbreviate. A lone attachment prints unnumbered, two or more are numbered. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. ["Attachment description, YYYY MMM DD"]
targets: []
# USAF memorandum or DAF headquarters memorandum, per AFH 33-337. DAF dates as 'September 15, 2026' rather than '15 September 2026', and leaves top-level paragraphs unnumbered with a first-line indent.
memo_style: usaf
# Body text size in points; decimals allowed, such as 11.5. AFH 33-337 §5 specifies 12.
font_size: 12
~~~

The first paragraph. Top-level paragraphs are auto-numbered; do not add manual numbering.

- Nested bullets are automatically lettered.

Lines that take no number, letter, or bullet — a roster of names, an address — go in a block quote, typeset as written. End a line with a backslash to break it.

> Jordan Hale, Capt, USAF\
> ---

$kind: indorsement
# composable (0..N)
# An endorsing official's response to the memo, or their forwarding of it onward. Indorsements are numbered in card order: 1st Ind, 2d Ind, 3d Ind.
# Office symbol or Rank Name of the endorsing official.
from: !must_fill ORG/SYMBOL
# Office symbol or organization receiving the endorsed memo.
for: !must_fill ORG/SYMBOL
# YYYY-MM-DD, the date the endorser signs or forwards the memo — distinct from the originating memo's date, per AFH 33-337 Ch. 14. Leave blank to print a fillable PDF text field for the endorser to type into when signing.
date: ""
# Authority line for this indorsement, printed in uppercase above its signature block. An indorsement has a closing section of its own, so the same rules apply: fill it in when the endorser signs for the commander or the headquarters, leave it blank when the commander signs.
authority_line: ""
# Line 1: Name in UPPERCASE as signed, grade, and service. Line 2: Duty title.
signature_block: !must_fill
  - FIRST M. LAST, Rank, USAF
  - Duty Title
# 'standard' keeps the indorsement on the action document's page under a one-line header, and moves it to a page of its own, under the fuller header, when it no longer fits. 'separate_page' always begins a new page. 'informal' prints no header at all, so an informal indorsement with an empty body is nothing but a signature block — with no text of its own to hold it to the page, it can open a page alone. Give it a body or an action, or use 'standard'.
format: standard
# The endorser's decision, printed as an either/or line with the choice underlined and the rejected option struck out. Leave blank to omit the line. The wording follows the indorsement's place in the chain: the last one is the approval authority and reads Approve/Disapprove, every earlier one is a coordinating official and reads Concur/Nonconcur. Use 'undecided' to print the pair unmarked, for the endorser to mark by hand.
action: ""

This memorandum establishes the concept of operations for a 24/7 Network Operations Help Desk at 26 NOS to provide a single, reliable point of contact for network users and mission partners. The help desk will improve mission assurance by receiving, triaging, and tracking network incidents, service requests, and user assistance issues; maintaining visibility of current outages; and coordinating timely restoration actions with affected work centers. The desk will not replace existing technical authorities; instead, it will consolidate intake, improve customer communication, and standardize the path from initial report to resolution.

The help desk will support the mission in two primary ways:

- It will reduce time to answer for users who need immediate assistance during duty and non-duty hours.

  - It will also improve transparency by ensuring each issue is logged, prioritized, and tracked to closure.

- It will strengthen operational tempo by giving commanders and supervisors a common picture of recurring network problems and outage trends.

  - It will also create a repeatable process for identifying trends that require sustainment, training, or infrastructure action.

Manning for the initial operating capability will be built from organic 26 NOS personnel augmented by trained shift leads to ensure continuous coverage across all hours. The roster below identifies the initial lead structure for implementation planning; final duty rosters will be published separately by the Operations Flight and updated as required to meet mission demands.

> ALEX J. RIVERA, SrA, USAF\
> MONICA L. NGUYEN, SSgt, USAF\
> DAVID P. HARRIS, TSgt, USAF\
> ERIN K. PATEL, SrA, USAF

The help desk will operate 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, with recurring shift handoffs to preserve continuity of operations and reduce missed calls, dropped tickets, and untracked outages. Standard shift turnover will include an open incident review, status of unresolved actions, and identification of high-priority items requiring immediate follow-up. When mission tempo requires additional support, the shift lead will request surge coverage through the flight chief or designated on-call supervisor.

Escalation will follow a tiered process designed to move urgent issues to the right authority without delay.

- The initial technician will attempt first-line troubleshooting, verify the reported impact, and document all actions taken.

  - If the issue cannot be resolved quickly, the technician will escalate to the on-call system or network specialist, notify the shift lead, and update the ticket with a clear problem statement and recommended next step.

- The 26 NOS/CC will review proposed changes to this concept of operations and provide comments, recommended edits, or concurrence no later than 15 March 2026. Consolidated feedback should identify mission impacts, additional manning requirements, and any coordination needed with 67 CW elements before implementation is finalized.


1. Mission Purpose and Scope. This Concept of Operations (CONOPS) establishes a new 24/7 Network Operations Help Desk at 26 NOS to provide single-pane-of-glass support for recurring network service issues, user-reported faults, and operational assistance requests originating from 67 CW mission partners and internal stakeholders. The Help Desk will serve as the front door for triage, coordination, and escalation while ensuring problems are tracked to resolution or to an agreed holding action. This CONOPS also defines roles, service levels, and the escalation approach to maintain operational continuity during nights, weekends, and holidays.

2. Manning and Team Composition. The Help Desk will operate on three overlapping watch rotations covering 24/7 service with trained personnel empowered to triage, document, and coordinate corrective action. A dedicated roster of qualified SMEs will support surge validation, complex troubleshooting, and time-critical escalation when first-line personnel require additional technical direction.

> ALEXANDER P. KIM, Maj, USAF\\ JENNIFER L. REED, Capt, USAF\\ RYAN D. SANTOS, Capt, USAF\\ MICHAEL T. PARK, TSgt, USAF

Baseline staffing is:

- 1 first-line Help Desk Technician (FLT) per active watch

- 1 duty network engineer (on-call/available) for consult and second-level support

- 1 shift lead responsible for triage quality assurance and escalation decisions

- SME duty roster available for protocol, routing, switching, and endpoint network dependencies

3. Hours of Operation and Customer Experience. The Help Desk will be available 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, including designated federal holidays, and will maintain a standardized intake workflow for all reports. Customers will submit requests through the approved reporting channels, after which the Help Desk will (1) validate the request type, (2) capture required operational metadata, (3) perform initial impact assessment, and (4) coordinate next actions with the appropriate response team.

Service expectations for each intake are:

- Intake acknowledgment within the first SLA tier (target: 5 minutes for urgent network impact, 15 minutes for standard assistance)

- Initial triage within the second SLA tier (target: 30 minutes for urgent tickets, 2 hours for standard tickets)

- Communication cadence that is proportional to impact level, with updates at agreed intervals until closure

A typical customer journey will follow:

- **A**cknowledge receipt and gather incident details

  - Confirm whether the issue is an incident, service request, or advisory

  - Identify affected capability, site, and operational timeframe

- **B**egin triage and coordinate action

  - Correlate with known issues, monitoring alerts, and prior tickets

  - Route to second-level support or initiate escalation when criteria are met

4. Escalation and Authority to Act. Escalation will be driven by impact, safety-of-flight and mission assurance considerations, and the inability of first-line triage to restore service within established thresholds. The Help Desk shift lead has authority to open, manage, and escalate tickets through defined pathways, including contacting on-call engineers and notifying command-level stakeholders when required by severity classification. Escalation pathways are designed to minimize cycle time while preserving traceability for auditing, after-action reviews, and continuous improvement.

Escalation criteria and method:

- Severity classification triggers

  - **Sev 1 (Mission Critical):** total loss of service, degraded command-and-control visibility, or inability to support mission tasking

    - Escalate immediately to duty engineer and initiate time-critical response procedures

  - **Sev 2 (Significant Impact):** partial loss of service or repeated intermittent failures affecting multiple users/segments

    - Escalate within SLA threshold to duty engineer for coordinated troubleshooting

  - **Sev 3 (Limited Impact):** localized impairment or non-critical assistance request

    - Coordinate remediation plan without immediate command-level notification unless trending worsens

- Escalation steps and documentation

  - Notify duty engineer and log the escalation decision with timestamps

    - Record affected service, evidence collected, and attempted mitigations

  - If restoration is not achieved within the severity-specific threshold

    - Escalate to the 26 NOS operational lead and provide a consolidated status briefing

5. Implementation, Feedback, and Way Ahead. 26 NOS will stand up the Help Desk with standardized intake scripts, triage checklists, and a ticketing workflow that supports end-to-end transparency from report to closure. We will measure performance using acknowledgement/triage timeliness, resolution rate by severity, and quality of problem characterization to reduce repeat failures and improve knowledge-driven troubleshooting. Your review and operational feedback are requested to ensure the Help Desk aligns with 67 CW command priorities, identifies any required integration changes early, and supports sustained 24/7 service delivery. We provide a suspense of **15 March 2026** for comments and implementation guidance.

This memorandum establishes the concept of operations for a 24/7 Network Operations Help Desk at 26 NOS. The Help Desk will provide a single, continuously available point of contact for reporting, triaging, coordinating, and communicating the status of network operations incidents and service requests affecting the wing. Its mission is to restore or sustain reliable mission-enabling network services, improve user communication, preserve operational awareness, and ensure issues are routed to the organization best positioned to resolve them.

The Help Desk will receive contacts through the designated telephone number, organizational mailbox, and approved ticketing system. The on-duty technician will validate the request, assign an initial priority, open or update the ticket, provide the requester a tracking identifier, and maintain the record through closure. The following operating standards apply:

- Acknowledge urgent or mission-impacting reports within 15 minutes; acknowledge routine requests within 60 minutes.

- Record the affected service, location, symptoms, time discovered, operational impact, troubleshooting performed, and requester contact information.

- Provide status updates at least hourly for priority incidents and at each material change for routine requests.

Manning will use a four-person minimum roster organized into continuous rotating coverage, with one primary technician on duty and an identified alternate for each shift. The 26 NOS/CC will designate the roster, approve shift schedules, and adjust coverage for leave, training, exercises, and surge operations. The initial roster is:

> ALEXIS R. CARTER, TSgt, USAF\\ BRYAN K. FIELDS, SSgt, USAF\\ MARISOL T. HAYES, SrA, USAF\\ DEVON P. REED, SrA, USAF

The Help Desk will operate 24 hours a day, seven days a week, including holidays. Shift turnovers will include an oral or written handoff covering open tickets, degraded services, pending actions, scheduled maintenance, elevated risks, and required follow-up. The on-duty technician will remain responsible for the ticket queue until formally relieved and will protect personally identifiable information and other sensitive operational details in accordance with applicable policy.

Escalation will be based on mission impact, scope, duration, safety or security concern, and inability to restore service at the current tier. The on-duty technician will immediately notify the shift lead and affected service owner for a critical outage, suspected cybersecurity event, or issue with wing-wide or higher impact; the shift lead will notify the 26 NOS/CC and coordinate with the appropriate command post, communications focal point, or supporting organization. The following actions are required for every escalation:

- Preserve logs, ticket history, communications, and other relevant evidence; do not alter systems beyond authorized troubleshooting.

- Keep the requester and leadership informed until service is restored, the issue is accepted by the responsible resolver, or the 26 NOS/CC directs another disposition.

Please provide comments, recommended changes, and identified resource constraints to 26 NOS/CC through 67 CW/A3 no later than 15 March 2026. The 26 NOS/CC will consolidate comments, resolve conflicts, and publish the approved operating procedures and duty roster following review. Questions may be directed to the 26 NOS/CC.

This memorandum presents the Concept of Operations (CONOPS) for a new 24/7 Network Operations Help Desk (NOHD) to be established by the 26th Network Operations Squadron (26 NOS). The NOHD will provide continuous, centralized first-line support for base network, cybersecurity, and communications issues, ensuring rapid incident intake, troubleshooting, and documented escalation to Tier II/III teams. Mission objectives include minimizing downtime, improving incident visibility, enforcing ticketing discipline, and providing after-action data to inform resourcing and training decisions.

The NOHD will be manned by a core shift structure supplemented with surge augmentation during high-tempo events. Primary staffing will consist of three rotating shifts to cover 24 hours daily, with an on-call roster to backfill gaps and handle surge incidents. Manning commitments and initial personnel assignments are as follows (roster provided as a reference block):

> SSgt ALEX R. HERNANDEZ, NCOIC, Network Operations\
> TSgt MARIA L. ONG, Lead Analyst\
> A1C JAMAL T. RILEY, Help Desk Technician\
> SrA HANNA K. LEE, Communications Analyst

Manning details:

- Shift composition:

  - Day Shift (0600–1800): NCOIC + 2 technicians

  - Night Shift (1800–0600): Lead Analyst + 1 technician

- On-call and surge:

  - One senior analyst on 30-minute recall for major incidents

  - Cross-trained personnel from 26 NOS and 67 CW/A3 for planned events and exercises

The NOHD will operate continuously (24/7/365) with the following service delivery model and hours of operation: initial call intake and triage, ticket creation and categorization, basic remediation where possible, and escalation thresholds. Service hours and primary actions:

- Normal operations: continuous 24/7 intake and triage

- Scheduled maintenance windows: NOHD will coordinate pre-notification and ticket handling

Escalation procedures will follow a clear, documented path to ensure timely resolution and command awareness. Escalation steps:

1. Tier I (Help Desk) — initial triage and attempt basic remediation within established SLAs. If unresolved after 30 minutes or upon detection of widespread impact, escalate to Tier II.

2. Tier II — specialized analysts perform deeper diagnostics and remediation. If Tier II cannot resolve within 60 minutes or identifies mission degradation, escalate to Tier III and notify 67 CW/A3.

Notification and command reporting:

- All incidents meeting the Major Incident criteria will trigger immediate notification to 67 CW/A3 and 26 NOS/CC.

- A daily summary and weekly trend report will be produced for 67 CW leadership to support resourcing decisions.

A request for coordination and comment: please provide any comments, recommended changes, or concurrence no later than 15 March 2026. Consolidated feedback will be incorporated into the final NOHD standing order and staffing plan. Point of contact for this CONOPS is the 26 NOS NCOIC, SSgt Alex R. Hernandez, at DSN XXX-XXXX or alex.hernandez@us.af.mil.

letterhead_seal_subtitle: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>

references: [] # array<richtext(inline)<markdown>>

cc: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>

Effective immediately, all retrograde cargo produced and shipped in our area of responsibility will follow the Packaging Standards for Retrograde Cargo in order to reduce damage, improve handling efficiency, and standardize receipt processing.

For each shipment, ensure the outer packaging is sufficient for expected transport conditions, all required markings and identifying labels are clearly visible, and the contents are secured to prevent movement during transit. Questions regarding compliant packaging configuration, labeling requirements, or exceptions should be routed through your local logistics channels to HQ AFMC/A4 for resolution.

This memorandum establishes packaging standards for retrograde cargo processed by units under ALMAJCOM/A4. All retrograde shipments must be packaged to prevent damage during handling and transport, comply with DoD and Air Force packaging specifications, and be palletized and secured when applicable.

Specifically, units will inspect items for contamination, apply corrosion prevention materials as required, use adequate cushioning and overpack for fragile items, and ensure standardized labeling including NSN, quantity, weight, and destination routing. Documentation (DD Forms and shipping manifests) must accompany each shipment and be attached to the exterior of the package in a weatherproof pouch.

Compliance with these standards is effective immediately. Unit logisticians will coordinate with HQ AFMC/A4 for clarification or waiver requests and report any packaging deficiencies through established supply and transportation channels.

This memorandum announces a stand-down for an Operational Risk Management (ORM) reset within the 355th Fighter Wing. The stand-down is intended to provide all personnel the opportunity to refresh their knowledge and commitment to managing risks effectively in all mission areas and daily duties.

The 355th Fighter Wing Commander, Colonel Joanna P. Reed, authorizes and directs this stand-down for ORM reset to enhance safety awareness and operational readiness throughout the wing.

All units under the 355th Operations Group are expected to actively participate and ensure compliance with ORM principles during this period.

Further details and scheduling instructions will be communicated through the 355 OG/CC offices.

Colonel Reed herself signs this memorandum, so no authority line is included.

This realignment requires close coordination with Operations, Intelligence, and Maintenance to minimize risk and preserve overall mission effectiveness. This memorandum notifies the commander of a channel mission diversion executed on 19 March 2026. Due to unforeseen maintenance issues at the planned forward location, the affected sortie was rerouted to an alternate installation to preserve aircrew and cargo timelines. All aircrew, passengers, and cargo were accounted for; there were no injuries or classified material involved. The operations team coordinated with the alternate base and applicable higher headquarters to ensure airfield and sustainment support met mission requirements.

Post-mission actions completed include a formal maintenance write-up for the primary aircraft, crew debriefs, and an initial safety review. Finance and logistics cells were notified to adjust funding and cargo accounts as required; AMC/A3 and 62 AW/FM were consulted during the diversion. Recommend no further action at this time pending completion of the maintenance investigation and the final lessons-learned report, which A3 will provide to the commander within five duty days.

1. Purpose. This memorandum directs and coordinates snow removal actions at Minot Air Force Base to ensure safe and continuous access for mission operations.

2. Scope. Effective immediately for forecasted and actual snow and freezing precipitation events, 5 CES will provide snow removal and ice control for Base mission critical areas, including primary vehicle routes and priority sidewalks, in accordance with established installation plans and response levels.

3. Responsibilities. a. 5 CES/CC will direct operations, prioritize routes and locations based on mission impact, and coordinate augmenting assets when snowfall exceeds routine capabilities. b. Base organizations will ensure occupants support access to cleared areas by removing vehicles parked in plow paths and relocating parked equipment/vehicles as directed by 5 CES personnel. c. 5 BW/CC will coordinate internal communication to affected units so personnel and contractors comply with posted movement and access restrictions during active snow removal.

4. Prioritization. a. Priority 1: Life safety and emergency access routes; access to command and control facilities; and support routes required for emergency response. b. Priority 2: Mission critical vehicle routes and primary pedestrian routes supporting daily operations. c. Priority 3: Secondary/adjacent areas and parking lots after completion of higher-priority tasks.

5. Request Process. When additional clearance, access waivers, or targeted area treatment is required, request support through the 5 CES operations channel. Provide location, urgency, and estimated duration of need.

6. Point of Contact. Questions or operational coordination should be directed to the 5 CES/CC staff on duty during the event.

Snow removal at Minot AFB is a critical winter readiness function that demands coordinated action across the 5 CES and the 5 BW/CC to ensure safe, reliable operations for flying and mission support. Effective immediately, the following priorities and operating procedures apply during winter weather events:

- Priority 1: Runways, instrument approach and taxiways to support immediate mission readiness; access for emergency and essential personnel; and operations of airfield facilities.

- Priority 2: Taxiways, ramps, and aircraft parking areas essential to safe aircraft movement and safety of operations.

- Priority 3: Non-mission-critical parking lots and roadways that do not impact airfield operations but affect daily base operations and personnel safety.

Procedures:

- 5 CES/CC will coordinate snow removal operations in concert with 5 BW/CC to ensure readiness, reporting status to affected units every four hours or as weather updates require.

- All plowing and de-icing activities must comply with applicable safety and environmental guidelines. De-icing agents shall be applied per base policy and environmental requirements.

- In the event of a severe weather event, a prioritized plan will be executed, with a standing schedule and communication cadence established between 5 CES/CC and 5 BW/CC.

This memo supersedes prior local guidance related to snow removal and replaces it with a unified, cross-unit approach to maintaining safe and accessible airfield operations during winter conditions.

Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave it blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.
# e.g. FOR THE COMMANDER
authority_line: FOR 4 AF/CC FROM 4 AF/IG # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Line 1: Name in UPPERCASE as signed, grade, and service. Line 2: Duty title.
signature_block:
  - GINA T. MARSH, Col, USAF
  - Inspector General
# Letterhead lines, top to bottom, all rendered in uppercase. The first is the department title, set larger than the rest. Change that line only for a Joint Command or a DoW agency. The lines below it are your unit's full organization name.

letterhead_title: # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
  - DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE
# Department of War (DoW) or Department of Defense (DoD) seal, shown at the top left of the letterhead. Leave blank for no seal.
letterhead_seal: dow # enum<dow | dod>
# Bold-caps line below the seal. Nothing prints when it is blank, or when there is no seal.
letterhead_seal_subtitle: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Organizational motto, centered in the footer of every page. Supports Markdown emphasis: *italics*, **bold**.
tag_line: "" # richtext(inline)<markdown>
# Classification marking, banner-printed at the top and bottom of every page. Leave blank for no banner, which is what an unclassified document normally carries. Mark per DAFI 16-1404, DoDM 5200.48 for CUI, and applicable DoD guidance.
# when CUI: controlled_by, poc, category, limited_dissemination

  value: ""
# Suffix appended to the banner after a double slash, rendered in uppercase: 'NF' prints as CUI//NF. Leave blank for no suffix.
dissemination: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Cite each reference by organization, type, date, and title. Two or more print as a References block lettered (a), (b), (c); a single one prints in parentheses after the subject, per AFH 33-337. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. ["AFMAN 33-326, 25 November 2011, *Preparing Official Communications*", "AFI 33-360, *Publications and Forms Management*"]

# Offices or people receiving a courtesy copy, one per line.

cc: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
# Every recipient, listed here when 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' stands in the Memo For field.

distribution: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
# Attachments in the order the memo mentions them. Describe each briefly; do not write 'as stated' or abbreviate. A lone attachment prints unnumbered, two or more are numbered. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.

# Body text size in points; decimals allowed, such as 11.5. AFH 33-337 §5 specifies 12.

This memorandum notifies SAF/AA that 88th Air Base Wing Records Management will conduct a Records Disposition Sweep across wing organizations beginning 1 June 2026 to ensure compliance with applicable retention schedules and disposition procedures. The sweep will identify records requiring transfer, destruction, or accession to the National Archives and Records Administration per governing guidance and will provide commanders with findings and recommended actions.

Organizations will prepare records for review, ensure accountable tracking of temporary and permanent records, and provide a point of contact to Records Management by 15 June 2026. Questions about required disposition actions or schedule applicability may be directed to the 88 ABW Records Manager at the contact information on file.

This memorandum establishes responsibilities and priorities for snow removal operations at Minot Air Force Base (AFB) to ensure safe and continuous mission operations during winter weather events.

1. Scope. This guidance applies to all 5th Bomb Wing (5 BW) units, tenant organizations, and base support agencies operating at Minot AFB.

2. Priorities. Snow and ice removal priorities are:

- a. Primary: Runways, taxiways, aircraft ramps, and other flightline surfaces necessary to maintain sortie generation and safe aircraft movement.

- b. Secondary: Emergency response routes, fire and medical access roads, and vehicle traffic routes to critical mission facilities.

- c. Tertiary: Parking lots, administrative building entrances, and sidewalks.

3. Responsibilities.

- a. 5 CES/CC will coordinate and execute base snow removal operations, to include planning, equipment allocation, contractor oversight, and real-time execution during events. CES will maintain sufficient resources to sustain continuous snow and ice control actions and will prioritize actions per paragraph 2.

- b. Wing and tenant unit commanders will:

  - (1) Ensure personnel and unit equipment are made available as tasked to support snow removal and emergency operations.

  - (2) Ensure parking areas and unit-controlled exterior spaces are cleared of vehicles as directed to allow snow removal equipment access.

- c. 5 MXG and operations units will ensure flightline access and aircraft parking areas are coordinated with 5 CES to minimize disruptions to snow removal activities while preserving sortie generation capability.

- d. 5 SFS will manage traffic control, enforce access restrictions during active snow removal, and ensure safety per applicable instructions.

4. Force Protection and Safety. All snow removal operations will comply with safety procedures. Operators will receive pre-mission briefings, wear required personal protective equipment, and employ spotters when operating heavy equipment near aircraft, pedestrians, or buildings.

5. Parking and Vehicle Policy. During declared snow removal operations, vehicle relocation may be required to facilitate clearance. Unit commanders must disseminate parking relocation instructions and ensure personnel comply. Vehicles impeding snow removal may be towed at the owner's expense.

6. Communications.

- a. 5 CES will publish a snow removal status and priority list to the 5 BW operations center and unit leadership at the onset of significant weather events and provide updates every 2 hours or as conditions change.

- b. Unit POCs shall coordinate directly with 5 CES for specific area requirements and report impediments to clearance efforts.

7. Reporting and After-Action.

- a. 5 CES will compile an after-action summary following significant snow events documenting actions taken, equipment usage, contractor performance, and recommended improvements.

- b. Unit commanders will report any safety incidents or damage resulting from snow removal operations to 5 CES and the wing safety office within 24 hours.

8. Point of Contact. For questions regarding this memorandum or snow removal operations, contact Capt John A. Example, 5 CES/Ready \& Emergency Management, at (701) 555-1234 or john.example@us.af.mil.

Thank you for your cooperation in maintaining safe and effective operations throughout the winter season.

FIRST ENDORSEMENT NOT REQUIRED.

FIRST M. LAST, Maj, USAF\
5 Civil Engineer Squadron

MAJ COLIN P. HAYES, MAJ, USAF Commander

$quill: usaf_memo@0.3.0
$kind: main
# U.S. Air Force and Space Force Official Memorandum
# Organization or office symbol, rendered in uppercase. To address a specific person, add their rank and name in parentheses: 'ORG/SYMBOL (LT COL JANE DOE)'. For a long list, enter 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' and name the recipients in the Distribution field.
memo_for: !must_fill
  - ORG1/SYMBOL
  - ORG2/SYMBOL
# The office symbol alone when every recipient is on this installation. The full mailing address as well when any recipient is elsewhere, so they can write back. Leave blank for a Memorandum for Record, which prints no FROM line.
# e.g. [ORG/SYMBOL, Organization Name, 123 Street Ave, City ST 12345-6789]
memo_from: []
# Keep it brief. Capitalize the first letter of each word except articles, prepositions, and conjunctions. Put any suspense date in parentheses. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. Subject of the Memorandum
subject: Alert Facility Quiet Hours
# YYYY-MM-DD, printed in the format the Memo Style field selects. Leave blank to use today's date.
date: 2026-02-14
# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.
# e.g. FOR THE COMMANDER
authority_line: ""
# Line 1: Name in UPPERCASE as signed, grade, and service. Line 2: Duty title.
signature_block: !must_fill
  - FIRST M. LAST, Rank, USAF
  - Duty Title
# Letterhead lines, top to bottom, all rendered in uppercase. The first is the department title, set larger than the rest. Change that line only for a Joint Command or a DoW agency. The lines below it are your unit's full organization name.
# e.g. [DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE, "HEADQUARTERS [UNIT NAME]"]
letterhead_title:
  - DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE
# Department of War (DoW) or Department of Defense (DoD) seal, shown at the top left of the letterhead. Leave blank for no seal.
letterhead_seal: ""
# Bold-caps line below the seal. Nothing prints when it is blank, or when there is no seal.
letterhead_seal_subtitle: ""
# Organizational motto, centered in the footer of every page. Supports Markdown emphasis: *italics*, **bold**.
tag_line: ""
# Classification marking, banner-printed at the top and bottom of every page. Leave blank for no banner, which is what an unclassified document normally carries. Mark per DAFI 16-1404, DoDM 5200.48 for CUI, and applicable DoD guidance.
# when CUI: controlled_by, poc, category, limited_dissemination
classification: # enum<UNCLASSIFIED | CUI | CONFIDENTIAL | SECRET | TOP SECRET>
  value: ""
# Suffix appended to the banner after a double slash, rendered in uppercase: 'NF' prints as CUI//NF. Leave blank for no suffix.
dissemination: ""
# Cite each reference by organization, type, date, and title. Two or more print as a References block lettered (a), (b), (c); a single one prints in parentheses after the subject, per AFH 33-337. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. ["AFMAN 33-326, 25 November 2011, *Preparing Official Communications*", "AFI 33-360, *Publications and Forms Management*"]
references: []
# Offices or people receiving a courtesy copy, one per line.
# e.g. ["Rank and Name, ORG/SYMBOL"]
cc: []
# Every recipient, listed here when 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' stands in the Memo For field.
# e.g. [ORG1/SYMBOL, ORG2/SYMBOL]
distribution: []
# Attachments in the order the memo mentions them. Describe each briefly; do not write 'as stated' or abbreviate. A lone attachment prints unnumbered, two or more are numbered. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. ["Attachment description, YYYY MMM DD"]
attachments: []

# U.S. Air Force and Space Force Official Memorandum
# Organization or office symbol, rendered in uppercase. To address a specific person, add their rank and name in parentheses: 'ORG/SYMBOL (LT COL JANE DOE)'. For a long list, enter 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' and name the recipients in the Distribution field.

# e.g. [ORG/SYMBOL, Organization Name, 123 Street Ave, City ST 12345-6789]
memo_from: []
# Keep it brief. Capitalize the first letter of each word except articles, prepositions, and conjunctions. Put any suspense date in parentheses. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. Subject of the Memorandum
subject: Installation Access Credential Reset
# YYYY-MM-DD, printed in the format the Memo Style field selects. Leave blank to use today's date.
date: ""
# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.
# e.g. FOR THE COMMANDER
authority_line: FOR THE COMMANDER
# Line 1: Name in UPPERCASE as signed, grade, and service. Line 2: Duty title.
signature_block: - WALTER J. POPE, Lt Col, USAF
  - Commander
# Letterhead lines, top to bottom, all rendered in uppercase. The first is the department title, set larger than the rest. Change that line only for a Joint Command or a DoW agency. The lines below it are your unit's full organization name.
# e.g. [DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE, "HEADQUARTERS [UNIT NAME]"]
letterhead_title:
  - DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE
# Department of War (DoW) or Department of Defense (DoD) seal, shown at the top left of the letterhead. Leave blank for no seal.
letterhead_seal: dow
# Bold-caps line below the seal. Nothing prints when it is blank, or when there is no seal.
letterhead_seal_subtitle: ""
# Organizational motto, centered in the footer of every page. Supports Markdown emphasis: *italics*, **bold**.
tag_line: ""
# Classification marking, banner-printed at the top and bottom of every page. Leave blank for no banner, which is what an unclassified document normally carries. Mark per DAFI 16-1404, DoDM 5200.48 for CUI, and applicable DoD guidance.
# when CUI: controlled_by, poc, category, limited_dissemination
classification:
  value: "UNCLASSIFIED"
# Suffix appended to the banner after a double slash, rendered in uppercase: 'NF' prints as CUI//NF. Leave blank for no suffix.
dissemination: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Cite each reference by organization, type, date, and title. Two or more print as a References block lettered (a), (b), (c); a single one prints in parentheses after the subject, per AFH 33-337. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. ["AFMAN 33-326, 25 November 2011, *Preparing Official Communications*", "AFI 33-360, *Publications and Forms Management*"]
references: []
# Offices or people receiving a courtesy copy, one per line.

cc: []
# Every recipient, listed here when 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' stands in the Memo For field.

distribution: []
# Attachments in the order the memo mentions them. Describe each briefly; do not write 'as stated' or abbreviate. A lone attachment prints unnumbered, two or more are numbered. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
attachments: []

# U.S. Air Force and Space Force Official Memorandum
# Organization or office symbol, rendered in uppercase. To address a specific person, add their rank and name in parentheses: 'ORG/SYMBOL (LT COL JANE DOE)'. For a long list, enter 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' and name the recipients in the Distribution field.
memo_for:
  - 11 WG/CC
# The office symbol alone when every recipient is on this installation. The full mailing address as well when any recipient is elsewhere, so they can write back. Leave blank for a Memorandum for Record, which prints no FROM line.
# e.g. [ORG/SYMBOL, Organization Name, 123 Street Ave, City ST 12345-6789]
memo_from:
  - 11 CS/CC
# Keep it brief. Capitalize the first letter of each word except articles, prepositions, and conjunctions. Put any suspense date in parentheses. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. Subject of the Memorandum
subject: Directory Listing of Unlisted DSN Numbers
# YYYY-MM-DD, printed in the format the Memo Style field selects. Leave blank to use today's date.
date: 2026-11-11
# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.
# e.g. FOR THE COMMANDER
authority_line: ""
# Line 1: Name in UPPERCASE as signed, grade, and service. Line 2: Duty title.
signature_block:
  - ASHA RAMAN, 1st Lt, USAF
  - Cyber Operations Officer
# Letterhead lines, top to bottom, all rendered in uppercase. The first is the department title, set larger than the rest. Change that line only for a Joint Command or a DoW agency. The lines below it are your unit's full organization name.
# e.g. [DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE, "HEADQUARTERS [UNIT NAME]"]
letterhead_title:
  - DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE
# Department of War (DoW) or Department of Defense (DoD) seal, shown at the top left of the letterhead. Leave blank for no seal.
letterhead_seal: dow
# Bold-caps line below the seal. Nothing prints when it is blank, or when there is no seal.
letterhead_seal_subtitle: ""
# Organizational motto, centered in the footer of every page. Supports Markdown emphasis: *italics*, **bold**.
tag_line: ""
# Classification marking, banner-printed at the top and bottom of every page. Leave blank for no banner, which is what an unclassified document normally carries. Mark per DAFI 16-1404, DoDM 5200.48 for CUI, and applicable DoD guidance.
# when CUI: controlled_by, poc, category, limited_dissemination
classification:
  value: CUI
  controlled_by: 11 CS/SCX
  poc: 1st Lt Asha Raman, DSN 312-612-4400, asha.raman@us.af.mil
  category: ""
  limited_dissemination: ""
# Suffix appended to the banner after a double slash, rendered in uppercase: 'NF' prints as CUI//NF. Leave blank for no suffix.
dissemination: ""
# Cite each reference by organization, type, date, and title. Two or more print as a References block lettered (a), (b), (c); a single one prints in parentheses after the subject, per AFH 33-337. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. ["AFMAN 33-326, 25 November 2011, *Preparing Official Communications*", "AFI 33-360, *Publications and Forms Management*"]
references: []
# Offices or people receiving a courtesy copy, one per line.
# e.g. ["Rank and Name, ORG/SYMBOL"]
cc: []
# Every recipient, listed here when 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' stands in the Memo For field.
# e.g. [ORG1/SYMBOL, ORG2/SYMBOL]
distribution: []
# Attachments in the order the memo mentions them. Describe each briefly; do not write 'as stated' or abbreviate. A lone attachment prints unnumbered, two or more are numbered. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. ["Attachment description, YYYY MMM DD"]
attachments: []
# USAF memorandum or DAF headquarters memorandum, per AFH 33-337. DAF dates as 'September 15, 2026' rather than '15 September 2026', and leaves top-level paragraphs unnumbered with a first-line indent.
memo_style: usaf
# Body text size in points; decimals allowed, such as 11.5. AFH 33-337 §5 specifies 12.
font_size: 12
~~~

The 11th Communications Squadron is providing the directory listing of currently unlisted Defense Switched Network (DSN) numbers to support accurate official contact information across the 11th Wing. Please review the listing and use the identified numbers for official communications as appropriate.

Please direct corrections, additions, or questions concerning the listing to the point of contact identified in the classification banner. Updates will be coordinated through the 11th Communications Squadron to maintain an accurate directory.

1. I nominate Capt Luis Mendez for the Lance P. Sijan Award and recommend him without reservation for consideration at 12 AF. During the past year, Capt Mendez distinguished himself through sustained, mission-first leadership that turned complex operational friction into measurable combat capability. He combined disciplined execution with uncommon judgment, repeatedly aligning people, equipment, and timelines across competing demands so the wing could meet every commitment while preserving readiness and morale. His actions reflected not only technical competence, but also the calm courage and selfless service that define this award.

2. Capt Mendez's impact extended far beyond normal duty expectations. He led critical problem solving in high-tempo conditions, identified risks before they matured into mission delay, and drove solutions that improved sortie generation, strengthened coordination with partner agencies, and reduced avoidable rework at every level. Equally important, he built trust wherever he worked: airmen sought his counsel because he listened with patience, acted with integrity, and refused to accept anything less than the standard that protects the force and the mission. Captain Luis Mendez’s nomination for the Lance P. Sijan Award is anchored in a record of deliberate, sustained actions that embody the highest ideals of the Air Force — a blend of personal courage, selfless service, and tactical excellence conducted under conditions demanding resilience and decisive leadership. In flight operations over multiple combat sorties, Mendez demonstrated an unyielding commitment to mission success, coordinating complex airspace management and rapidly adapting to evolving threat environments. His calm, purposeful demeanor under pressure enabled his team to execute precision tasks that directly reduced risk to joint force units and enhanced overall mission effectiveness in contested airspace. The tangible outcomes of his leadership — accelerated joint integration, improved threat detection, and safer sortie generation — reflect a professional standard that transcends ordinary duty performance.

Beyond his direct operational impact, Mendez’s mentorship and initiative catalyzed a culture of accountability across the unit. He instituted a cross-check protocol that reduced miscommunication and enabled his peers to anticipate adverse developments before they emerged on the tactical commercial screens. When a mission tempo threatened to erode unit cohesion, he led a targeted training program that elevated the performance of junior airmen while preserving morale and welfare. His approach to leadership—combining technical mastery with an ethic of service—raised the entire team’s readiness and resilience, ensuring that the squad could absorb surges in workload without compromising safety or precision.

In recognition of his professional maturity and unwavering devotion to the Air Force’s contribution to national security, Mendez consistently translated strategic intent into executable action. He advanced a suite of risk mitigation measures that reduced potential exposure during high-threat operations and enhanced the team’s ability to maneuver in complex electromagnetic environments. This fusion of strategic thinking and meticulous execution enabled sustained, superior performance across successive deployments, earning him recognition from peer units and supervisory leadership alike. Capt Mendez’s record of achievement exemplifies the caliber of leadership the Lance P. Sijan Award seeks to honor: a star performer whose courage, competence, and character elevate the entire force and advance the nation’s security interests.

This memorandum provides implementation guidance for parental leave across the major commands. Commanders will ensure the guidance is communicated to eligible personnel and applied consistently with applicable Department of Defense and Department of the Air Force policy.

Active duty members, Air National Guard members serving on qualifying active service, and Air Force Reserve members serving on qualifying active service are eligible for parental leave when they meet the requirements established in applicable policy. Eligibility and authorized leave amounts depend on the member's status and the qualifying birth, adoption, or placement event.

Members will submit required documentation through their servicing military personnel section or designated leave-approval process. Documentation must establish the qualifying event and identify the applicable parent or guardian relationship. Supervisors and personnel offices will protect personally identifiable information and retain records in accordance with governing records-management requirements.

Questions regarding implementation should be directed to the servicing military personnel section or the appropriate major command manpower and personnel office. HQ USAF/A1 will provide additional clarification through established personnel policy channels as needed.

This memorandum provides implementation guidance for parental leave across Air Force and Space Force organizations. It establishes consistent application of leave entitlements, clarifies key administrative requirements, and directs units to align internal processes with existing policy and reporting expectations.

All eligible Service members are entitled to parental leave when the criteria in governing parental leave authorities are met. Commanders will ensure leave approval is administered fairly and consistently, and that operational requirements are considered without creating unequal access to entitlements.

Questions regarding implementation should be submitted to HQ USAF/A1 for manpower policy guidance. Points of contact within each organization should coordinate internally to ensure eligibility determinations, documentation handling, and system processing are standardized for their respective commands.

# Organization or office symbol, rendered in uppercase. To address a specific person, add their rank and name in parentheses: 'ORG/SYMBOL (LT COL JANE DOE)'. For a long list, enter 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' and name the recipients in the Distribution field.
memo_for:
  - 11 WG/CC
# The office symbol alone when every recipient is on this installation. The full mailing address as well when any recipient is elsewhere, so they can write back. Leave blank for a Memorandum for Record, which prints no FROM line.
# e.g. [ORG/SYMBOL, Organization Name, 123 Street Ave, City ST 12345-6789]
memo_from:
  - 11 CS/CC
# Keep it brief. Capitalize the first letter of each word except articles, prepositions, and conjunctions. Put any suspense date in parentheses. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. Subject of the Memorandum
subject: Directory Listing of Unlisted DSN Numbers
# YYYY-MM-DD, printed in the format the Memo Style field selects. Leave blank to use today's date.
date: 2026-11-11 # date<YYYY-MM-DD>
# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave it blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.
# e.g. FOR THE COMMANDER
authority_line: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>

signature_block:
  - ASHA RAMAN, 1ST LT, USAF
  - Cyber Operations Officer

letterhead_title:

letterhead_seal: dow # enum<dow | dod>
# Bold-caps line below the seal. Nothing prints when it is blank, or when there is no seal.
letterhead_seal_subtitle: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Organizational motto, centered in the footer of every page. Supports Markdown emphasis: *italics*, **bold**.
tag_line: "" # richtext(inline)<markdown>
# Classification marking, banner-printed at the top and bottom of every page. Leave blank for no banner, which is what an unclassified document normally carries. Mark per DAFI 16-1404, DoDM 5200.48 for CUI, and applicable DoD guidance.

memo_for:

# when CUI: controlled_by, poc, category, limited_dissemination

  value: CUI
dissemination: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
controlled_by: 11 CS/SCX
poc: 1st Lt Asha Raman, DSN 312-612-4400, asha.raman@us.af.mil
category: "" # left blank per request
limited_dissemination: "" # left blank per request
# Cite each reference by organization, type, date, and title. Two or more print as a References block lettered (a), (b), (c); a single one prints in parentheses after the subject, per AFH 33-337. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.

# e.g. ["Rank and Name, ORG/SYMBOL"]

This memorandum provides a directory listing of recently identified DSN numbers that were not previously included in base contact directories. The attached listing consolidates the unlisted DSNs by organization and includes point-of-contact information where available to assist wing staff and communications personnel in updating authoritative directories and routing tables.

Please review the listing and coordinate any corrections or additions through 11 CS/SCX. If you have updates or require direct assistance, contact the point of contact below. Thank you for your prompt attention to ensuring our DSN directories remain complete and current.

- Airlift

  - Confirm readiness to support patient movement and report any medical or transportation shortfalls.

- Communications

  - Establish and validate deployable communications capabilities for command and control.

  - Report communications equipment, trained personnel, connectivity, and interoperability limitations.

Captain Mendez's decision-making under pressure produced operational outcomes with strategic implications for the wing. Beyond technical acumen, he exhibited moral courage by challenging entrenched procedures that hindered speed and safety, negotiating process changes with higher headquarters that were later adopted across the group. He also established enduring liaison relationships with allied maintainers and local contractor teams, smoothing supply-chain friction and enabling collaborative repairs that saved critical hours during surge operations. These cumulative achievements—technical excellence, decisive leadership under stress, and a persistent investment in others—make Captain Mendez an outstanding candidate for the Lance P. Sijan Leadership Award.

1. Situation. The National Weather Service forecasts hurricane conditions that are expected to impact operational areas within the command’s area of interest. Immediate force generation is required to support Department of Defense and civil authorities with rapid movement of personnel and medical resources.

2. Mission. Provide immediate airlift and medevac capabilities and establish required communications support to enable hurricane relief operations in coordination with applicable federal, state, and local authorities.

3. Specified Tasks. Generate and task forces as follows:

a. Airlift. Provide mission-ready aircraft, crews, and support personnel to move relief supplies and response elements to designated staging locations.

b. Medevac. Stand up medical evacuation support (aircrew, medical personnel, and required equipment) capable of supporting casualty movement and en route care.

c. Communications. Establish and maintain communications interoperability (primary and alternate methods), ensuring connectivity between deployed forces, command and control elements, and supported relief coordinators.

This memorandum documents the recent bird aircraft strike hazard activity observed within the 4th Fighter Wing and identifies actions to reduce the risk of future strikes.

The following strike events were recorded during the after-action review:

> 2026-04-22, 1435L — Runway 14 approach corridor\
> 2026-04-28, 0710L — East perimeter near Taxiway Bravo\
> 2026-05-03, 1818L — Departure end of Runway 32

To reduce bird aircraft strike hazard exposure, the 4th Fighter Wing should implement the following mitigations:

- Increase airfield wildlife surveys and dispersal operations during peak bird-activity periods.

  - Schedule focused patrols before first launch, during the morning migration window, and before evening recovery.

  - Record bird species, flock size, location, and response effectiveness in the airfield hazard log.

- Improve coordination between Airfield Management, Air Traffic Control, and flying units.

  - Publish timely bird-activity advisories and include recurring hazard areas in daily flight briefings.

  - Review strike data weekly to identify trends and adjust patrol locations and flight-line controls.

The 4th Fighter Wing Safety Office will track implementation and provide a follow-up assessment after 30 days. Commanders should emphasize immediate reporting of bird activity and suspected strikes through established safety channels.

1. This memorandum provides an after-action summary for a Bird Aircraft Strike Hazard (BASH) event affecting aircraft operations under 4 FW.

2. The following strike information was recorded:

> 2026-05-01 0645L — Departure leg near the departure end, runway 18\
> 2026-05-02 1920L — Downwind over the northern grass overrun\
> 2026-05-06 0810L — Final approach corridor, runway 36\\

3. Recommended mitigations are as follows:

- Reduce wildlife attractants and improve habitat management through routine base grounds inspections

  - Increase mowing/vegetation control frequency along fence lines and approach/departure corridors

  - Ensure prompt litter removal and audit trash-storage areas during peak wildlife activity periods

- Strengthen detection and response to hazardous conditions

  - Update local BASH spot-check checklists and require documented bird-activity observations during preflight briefings

  - Coordinate with airfield operations to adjust traffic flow/altitudes when hazardous bird concentrations are reported

4. Points of contact are available through the Safety office for follow-up actions, trend analysis, and additional risk-reduction recommendations.

This memorandum documents the Bird Aircraft Strike Hazard after action for the 4th Fighter Wing. Three bird aircraft strikes were reported during the period under review:

> 2026-05-06, 0835 local — Runway 17 approach\
> 2026-05-07, 1010 local — Taxiway Charlie\
> 2026-05-08, 1545 local — Runway 35 departure corridor

The strike locations indicate recurring exposure along the runway environment and departure and arrival corridors. Continued coordination among airfield management, operations, and safety personnel is necessary to reduce the risk of additional strikes.

Recommend implementing the following mitigations:

- Apply focused wildlife-management measures in the affected areas:

  - Increase airfield wildlife surveys during the identified high-activity periods.

  - Remove or treat attractants near the runway and taxiway surfaces.

- Improve operational reporting and real-time hazard communication:

  - Require immediate reporting of bird concentrations and strikes through established airfield channels.

  - Include current bird activity in airfield advisories and appropriate preflight briefings.

Please direct the 4 FW/SE to track mitigation completion and provide a 30-day effectiveness update.

SITUATION: The passage of a major hurricane in the Atlantic has created an immediate requirement for rapid force generation and surge readiness to support joint relief operations in affected regions. The 23d Wing/CC requires ready air mobility assets, medical evacuation (medevac) capabilities, and resilient communications to sustain screening, assessment, and relief coordination in the first 72 hours post-landfall. ACC/A3 and higher headquarters anticipate a potentially extended relief effort with concurrent civilian coordination and security considerations.

MISSION: To mobilize and posture immediate force generation within 18 hours to enable airlift lift and sustainment, medevac, and critical comms support for hurricane relief operations, in order to deliver life-saving capabilities and stabilize affected populations in coordination with civil authorities and partner services. Specific readiness actions will be conducted in close alignment with theater commands and the Joint Task Force commands as directed.

SPECIFIED TASKS:

- AIRLIFT

  - Establish and surge air mobility capacity (rotary and fixed-wing) for urgent personnel, equipment, and relief supplies to multiple affected sites.

  - Prioritize availability of medical supplies and partner with approved contractors to ensure rapid embarkation and delivery timelines.

- MEDEVAC

  - Ensure prioritized MEDEVAC assets and medical staging areas are ready to receive casualties and critical patients, with a focus on rapid extraction and evacuation to definitive care.

- COMMS

  - Restore and reinforce communications architectures to enable interagency coordination, situational awareness, and casualty reporting among joint and civil authorities.

Situation. A Category 4 hurricane is forecast to make landfall within the next 72 hours in a region supported by 23 Wing installations. State and local authorities have requested immediate Department of Defense assistance to support evacuation, medical evacuation, and emergency communications. Air Combat Command (ACC) is directing rapid force generation and deployment of airlift, aeromedical, and communications capabilities to support civil authorities and save lives.

Mission. 23 WG/CC directs immediate generation and preparation of assigned and tasked resources to execute hurricane relief operations in support of civil authorities and FEMA, with a suspense for initial readiness reporting to ACC/A3 not later than 4 September 2026.

Specified Tasks.

- Airlift

  - Rapidly prepare organic and surge airlift assets for tasking to move personnel, emergency responders, and critical supplies to affected areas.

  - Coordinate scheduling, manifesting, and prioritization with ACC/A3 and airlift control authorities to support immediate movement requirements.

- Medevac

  - Ready aeromedical evacuation crews and enablers for contingency medevac missions, including preparation of MEDEVAC-configured aircraft, patient movement plans, and medical equipment.

  - Ensure trained medical personnel and requisite supplies are available to conduct casualty evacuation and sustain patient care during transit.

- Communications

  - Posture and prepare deployable communications packages to restore and augment critical command, control, and public safety communications in impacted areas.

  - Coordinate with ACC/A3 and supporting communications units to establish prioritized connectivity and interoperability with civil authorities.

Point of Contact for this tasker is ACC/A3 Operations at the email and phone on file with 23 WG staff. Report initial readiness status, shortfalls, and any requirement for additional support to ACC/A3 no later than 4 September 2026.

This memorandum documents a Bird Aircraft Strike Hazard (BASH) after action and recommends mitigations to reduce future strike risk.

The event summary follows:

> 2026-05-07 0745L, Perimeter Fence Line West of Runway 09/27\
> 2026-05-07 0812L, Taxiway B (near intersection B3)\
> 2026-05-07 0830L, Runway 09 Threshold

Observations: There were multiple small flocks noted in the airfield vicinity during morning launch operations. No aircrew injuries occurred; one aircraft reported minor bird-strike damage to the nose radome during takeoff. Wildlife control responded and conducted standard dispersal actions.

Recommendations:

- Increase wildlife patrol frequency during high-risk windows

  - Implement patrols at 30-minute intervals during morning launch and recovery periods (first 2 hours after sunrise)

  - Coordinate with operations to establish a go/no-go bird advisories threshold and a real-time notification procedure

- Enhance habitat and attractant reduction measures

  - Remove or modify standing water and open food sources within 2,000 feet of the airfield where feasible

  - Conduct vegetation management along perimeter and approach corridors to reduce perching and nesting sites

Please direct questions or requests for additional information to 4 FW/SE.

Respectfully,

LT COL PRISCILLA N. ORTIZ, USAF Chief of Safety

Per your request, this office reviewed the proposed Off-Limits Order. Based on the materials provided, the proposed order is legally supportable in principle and may be implemented with the clarifications below to ensure compliance with applicable Air Force policy and legal constraints.

Legal bases considered include:

- AFI 31-115, *Law Enforcement Operations*, which sets forth Air Force policy and procedures governing establishment of off-limits areas and related law enforcement actions.

  - The instruction outlines required coordination, notice procedures, and the limited scope of authority for restricting access to locations in order to protect health, safety, good order, and discipline.

- General authority of installation commanders to regulate conduct and access on the installation to protect mission readiness, safety, and good order and discipline, as implemented through Air Force and DoD regulations.

- Constitutional and due process considerations, which require that any restriction be reasonably related to a legitimate governmental interest, be neither arbitrary nor overbroad, and provide affected individuals with appropriate notice and an opportunity to seek relief where required.

Prior to signature, this office recommends the order be revised to: (1) specify the factual basis for the restriction with sufficient detail to permit affected persons to understand the conduct or conditions prompting the order; (2) include clear start and end dates (or review triggers) and a process for administrative review; and (3) document coordination with Security Forces and the legal office. With those revisions, the order should meet Air Force policy and legal norms.

Subject: Below-the-Zone Promotion Board Timeline

1. This memorandum outlines the timeline for the Below-the-Zone (BTZ) Promotion Board as it applies to personnel under the command of 11 WG. All eligible Airmen should be aware of eligibility windows, required documentation, and board dates as established by applicable Air Force policy. The BTZ process is time-sensitive; unit execution must ensure timely submission of packets and communications to support fair and accurate consideration.

2. Responsibilities fall to Squadron Commanders and Section Chiefs to verify eligibility, compile recommended records, and ensure proper routing prior to board convening. The personnel readiness office will coordinate with the Promotion/BTZ team to track deadlines, validate senior rater inputs, and prepare the official board package package for dissemination to the promotion board. All required forms and supporting documentation must be complete and accurate to avoid delays.

3. Any questions regarding the BTZ timeline, required documents, or board-specific submission instructions should be directed to the 11 WG/A1 administrator, with a copy to 11 WG/CC as appropriate. This memorandum remains in effect until superseded or cancelled.

Partner Air Force intelligence reporting containing Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) will be handled as Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and protected from unauthorized access, use, or dissemination. Personnel will limit access to those with an authorized mission need and will not release CTI outside approved channels or to foreign partners unless the release has been reviewed and authorized under applicable policy and disclosure procedures.

To strengthen IFF student proficiency and ensure adequate repetition before live-flight events, the 33d Operations Group will provide four additional simulator sorties. These events will be scheduled in coordination with the 33d Fighter Wing training calendar and will not displace required syllabus events.

The additional simulator sorties will focus on the following training objectives:

- **Event 1—Basic Intercept Repetition:** Refine radar intercept procedures, communications, and weapons employment fundamentals.

- **Event 2—Dissimilar Aircraft Integration:** Practice identification, sorting, and engagement decisions during a complex formation scenario.

- **Event 3—Degraded-Systems Operations:** Execute IFF procedures with simulated radar, datalink, and communications limitations.

- **Event 4—Mission-Level Evaluation:** Integrate the preceding skills in a graded scenario and identify any remaining training deficiencies.

To strengthen instrument flight rules proficiency and accelerate mission qualification, the 33d Operations Group will provide four additional simulator sorties for IFF students. These events will be scheduled through the appropriate squadron training managers and integrated with each student's existing syllabus without displacing required live-fly training.

The additional simulator events are:

- Instrument approach and missed-approach procedures in degraded weather.

- Emergency procedures and abnormal indications during departure and recovery.

- Air-to-air intercept setup, communications, and weapons employment fundamentals.

- Night and low-visibility navigation, including divert and lost-communications procedures.

Squadron commanders will identify students requiring the additional training and submit scheduling priorities to the 33 OG training office. The training office will publish the final schedule and track completion before each student's next evaluation event.

To: 33 FW/CC; 33 OG/CC Subject: Additional SIM Sorties for IFF Students.

Colleagues, in support of the ongoing IFF training program, the 33rd Operations Group requests authorization to increase the number of simulator sorties available to IFF students. This adjustment will balance instructional time between critical decision-making under simulated fatigue and realistic crew coordination, ensuring students achieve the required proficiency prior to live-fire or tactical training events.

- Additional SIM sorties for IFF students:

  - Event I: Enhanced radar alignment and threat cue discrimination in the MIDS simulator, including updated threat sets and timed response requirements.

  - Event II: High-fidelity cooperation drills within the A-10/F-15 joint-simulation environment, focusing on voice communication and radio discipline under increasing load.

  - Event III: Multi-ship intercept scenarios that emphasize formation integrity, callouts, and tactical maneuvering with simulated altitude- and airspeed-constraints.

  - Event IV: Post-flight evaluation session with objective debrief metrics, focusing on decision accuracy, coordination, and adherence to standard operating procedures.

These additional sorties will be scheduled within existing training blocks and will not impact other essential flight training requirements. Please indicate approval at your earliest convenience so we can finalize the training calendar.

  - Event II: High-fidelity cooperation drills within the A-10/F-15 joint-simulation environment, focusing on voice communication and radio discipline under increasing load.

  - Event III: Multi-ship intercept scenarios that emphasize formation integrity, callouts, and tactical maneuvering with simulated altitude- and airspeed-constraints.

  - Event IV: Post-flight evaluation session with objective debrief metrics, focusing on decision accuracy, coordination, and adherence to standard operating procedures.

These additional sorties will be scheduled within existing training blocks and will not impact other essential flight training requirements. Please indicate approval at your earliest convenience so we can finalize the training calendar.

# e.g. Subject of the Memorandum

# YYYY-MM-DD, printed in the format the Memo Style field selects. Leave blank to use today's date.

AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD.   - Duty Title

  - DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE
