18 WG/CC records the decisions from the 18 April 28 2026 (12-person) commander's conference held on 2026-04-28.

> LT COL JANE DOE, USAF\
> MAJ RICHARD ROE, USAF\
> CAPT AMANDA BLACK, USAF\
> MS. KAREN WHITE, SES\
> LT COL MICHAEL GREEN, USAF\
> MAJ SARAH BROWN, USAF\
> CAPT DAVID JONES, USAF\
> TECH SGT ROBERT TAYLOR, USAF

1. Decision: Priority priorities for the next 90 days will be executed in the following order:

- Mission readiness and training throughput

  - Publish weekly training status briefs by 0900 every Monday

  - Identify shortfalls within 72 hours of detection

- Base resilience and sustainment

  - Complete risk reviews for critical systems by 2026-05-15

  - Validate maintenance backlog metrics at each unit stand-up

- Squadron-level execution controls

  - Implement a common tracker for tempo, manpower, and procurement

  - Hold biweekly cross-directorate synchronization

2. Decision: Risk management will be standardized across directorates for all major initiatives beginning immediately:

- Governance

  - Establish a single risk register owner per initiative

  - Require risk acceptance documentation for residual risks rated moderate or higher

- Reporting

  - Submit consolidated risk changes to the Wing Executive Board every Friday

  - Conduct a monthly trend review and provide mitigations within 10 duty days

- Compliance

  - Ensure reporting alignment with applicable headquarters taskers

  - Track action item due dates to closure and flag slippage at first notice

3. Decision: Communication and governance routines will improve execution transparency and commander visibility:

- Staff alignment

  - Use a standard agenda template for WG/CC stand-ups

  - Provide action item status with owners and due dates on every brief

- Decision documentation

  - Record outcomes in this memorandum and maintain an action register for 180 days

  - Close actions with evidence of completion or documented rationale

- Stakeholder engagement

  - Coordinate with functional communities prior to major policy updates

  - Brief major changes to affected units at least 10 duty days before implementation

LEON W. PRUITT, Brig Gen, USAF\
Commander

The 18 WG/CC convened a 12-person wing offsite on April 28, 2026, to align senior leaders on near-term priorities, resource allocation, and execution standards. The following eight attendees are recorded; the complete participant count was 12.

> LEON W. PRUITT, Brig Gen, USAF\\ MARIA T. SANTOS, Col, USAF\\ DAVID R. KIM, Col, USAF\\ ANGELA J. HARRIS, CMSgt, USAF\\ ROBERT L. WEBB, Lt Col, USAF\\ NICOLE A. FIELDS, Lt Col, USAF\\ THOMAS E. GRANT, Maj, USAF\\ JEREMY K. PRICE, Capt, USAF

The wing will focus its next planning cycle on mission readiness, installation resilience, and deliberate risk reduction. The group agreed to:

- Use the existing wing readiness indicators as the common baseline for monthly command reviews.

  - Each group will identify its two most consequential readiness gaps by May 8, 2026.

  - The staff will consolidate the submissions and provide the commander a prioritized cross-wing view by May 15, 2026.

- Treat unresolved readiness risks as command-discussion items rather than deferring them to routine staff processes.

The wing will strengthen installation resilience by coordinating operational, infrastructure, and personnel dependencies before committing to major changes. The group agreed to:

- Establish a quarterly resilience synchronization led by the wing staff.

  - The first session will review communications, facilities, supply, and force-support dependencies.

  - Each group will bring one exercise-tested lesson and one proposed corrective action.

- Assign an action owner and a suspense date for every accepted corrective action.

The wing will improve execution discipline by converting offsite priorities into a small number of measurable actions and reviewing progress at command level. The group agreed to:

- Limit the initial execution plan to the highest-value actions that can be resourced and tracked.

  - The wing staff will publish the plan by May 22, 2026.

  - Group commanders will brief status, barriers, and decisions required at the monthly command review.

- Reassess the priorities at the end of the next quarter and adjust them when mission demands or risk conditions change.

# U.S. Air Force and Space Force Official Memorandum
# Organization or office symbol, rendered in uppercase. To address a specific person, add their rank and name in parentheses: 'ORG/SYMBOL (LT COL JANE DOE)'. For a long list, enter 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' and name the recipients in the Distribution field.
memo_for:
  - 12 AF
  - USAF
# The office symbol alone when every recipient is on this installation. The full mailing address as well when any recipient is elsewhere, so they can write back. Leave blank for a Memorandum for Record, which prints no FROM line.
# e.g. [ORG/SYMBOL, Organization Name, 123 Street Ave, City ST 12345-6789]
memo_from: []
# Keep it brief. Capitalize the first letter of each word except articles, prepositions, and conjunctions. Put any suspense date in parentheses. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. Subject of the Memorandum
subject: Nomination of Capt Luis Mendez for the Lance P. Sijan Award
date: "2026-01-31"
# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.
# e.g. FOR THE COMMANDER
authority_line: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Line 1: Name in UPPERCASE as signed, grade, and service. Line 2: Duty title.
signature_block:
  - JOANNA P. REED, Colonel, USAF
  - Commander
# Letterhead lines, top to bottom, all rendered in uppercase. The first is the department title, set larger than the rest. Change that line only for a Joint Command or a DoW agency. The lines below it are your unit's full organization name.
# e.g. [DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE, "HEADQUARTERS [UNIT NAME]"]
letterhead_title:
  - DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE
letterhead_seal: dow
letterhead_seal_subtitle: ""
tag_line: ""
classification: 
  value: ""
# Suffix appended to the banner after a double slash, rendered in uppercase: 'NF' prints as CUI//NF. Leave blank for no suffix.
dissemination: ""
# Cite each reference by organization, type, date, and title. Two or more print as a References block lettered (a), (b), (c); a single one prints in parentheses after the subject, per AFH 33-337. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. ["AFMAN 33-326, 25 November 2011, *Preparing Official Communications*", "AFI 33-360, *Publications and Forms Management*"]
references: []
# Offices or people receiving a courtesy copy, one per line.
# e.g. ["Rank and Name, ORG/SYMBOL"]
cc: []
# Every recipient, listed here when 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' stands in the Memo For field.
# e.g. [ORG1/SYMBOL, ORG2/SYMBOL]
distribution: []
# Attachments in the order the memo mentions them. Describe each briefly; do not write 'as stated' or abbreviate. A lone attachment prints unnumbered, two or more are numbered. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. ["Attachment description, YYYY MMM DD"]
attachments: ["AF Form 1206, 2026 Jan 30"]

This memorandum for the record captures decisions made at the 18th Wing commander's conference, an offsite attended by 12 personnel on 28 April 2026. The conference was convened to align priorities, assign actions, and clarify resource timelines for the upcoming fiscal year.

> COLIN D. HAWKINS, Col, USAF\
> SARAH J. MENDOZA, Lt Col, USAF\
> RICHARD P. O'NEIL, Maj, USAF\
> LILA M. TORRES, Capt, USAF\
> GREGORY S. HALL, SMSgt, USAF\
> MELISSA K. YU, TSgt, USAF\
> THOMAS A. KERR, Civ, GS-14\
> DAVID L. NGUYEN, Civ, GS-12

1. Strategic Priorities: The commander established the top three wing priorities for FY26 and directed implementation steps.

- Priority 1: Readiness and Lethality. The wing will accelerate training and maintenance efforts to ensure unit readiness.

  - Increase sortie generation by optimizing maintenance scheduling and sparing (target: 10% sortie increase by Q3).

  - Implement a cross-functional sortie recovery team to reduce maintenance downtimes.

- Priority 2: People and Professional Development. Improve retention and professional military education opportunities.

  - Expand on-base PME seat allocations and fund travel for critical career-broadening assignments.

  - Launch a mentorship pilot pairing senior NCOs and junior officers for career development.

- Priority 3: Infrastructure and Modernization. Prioritize facility upgrades and information technology resilience.

  - Approve phased funding for runway resurfacing and munitions storage improvements.

  - Task CE and LRS to deliver a prioritized scope and funding estimate within 60 days.

2. Resource Allocation: Decisions were made concerning the distribution of manpower and fiscal resources to support the priorities above.

- Manpower Actions:

  - Authorize limited reprogramming of 12 authorizations within the wing to critical squadrons (implementation to follow HQ coordination).

  - Establish a hiring surge plan for key civilian billets with delegated authority to expedite appointments.

- Fiscal Actions:

  - Allocate one-time readiness funds to cover critical spares and depot-level repairs (cap: $1.2M).

  - Require OPRs to submit expenditure plans and metrics within 30 days for quarterly review.

3. Command and Control / Communication: The commander directed changes to improve decision speed and internal communication across groups.

- C2 Adjustments:

  - Create a weekly cross-functional sync chaired by the Vice Wing Commander to address emergent issues and escalate decisions.

  - Define clear authority delegations for contingency responses and publish a one-page decision matrix.

- Communication Enhancements:

  - Standardize a weekly commander’s update to all wing members summarizing priorities, actions, and accomplishments.

  - Direct PA to refresh internal communication templates to ensure accessibility and consistency across units.

LEON W. PRUITT Brig Gen, USAF Commander

The 18th Wing Commander convened an offsite commander's conference on 28 April 2026 with twelve senior leaders to discuss strategic priorities and operational concerns. Eight attendees from diverse units participated in focused sessions that generated three key decisions to guide Wing activities and initiatives.

Attendance roster:

> COL JAMES T. HARRIS, USAF\
> LTC EMILY R. SANCHEZ, USAF\
> MAJ KEVIN L. PARK, USAF\
> SMSGT LARA W. BISHOP, USAF\
> CMSGT DEREK J. FOSTER, USAF\
> CAPT MARIA S. VELASQUEZ, USAF\
> MSgt BRYAN P. CLARK, USAF\

- The Wing will allocate additional resources and funding to enhance aircraft and personnel readiness.
- Embrace modernized equipment upgrades and training programs to sustain superior operational capabilities.

2. Enhancement of Leadership Development Programs

- Launch a comprehensive leadership initiative to develop mid-level and senior officers.
- Incorporate innovative mentoring tools and cross-functional training to prepare leaders for complex assignments.

3. Strengthening Community and Interagency Partnerships

- Intensify collaboration with local government agencies and community organizations.
- Establish recurring joint exercises and outreach projects to foster mutual support and readiness.

These decisions will be monitored and assessed through periodic reviews coordinated by the Wing Operations and Plans offices. Action plans are expected to be finalized and disseminated within the next quarter to ensure alignment with Wing objectives.

This memorandum summarizes the results of Operational Risk Management (ORM) spot checks conducted across 366th Fighter Wing units on 2–4 June 2026. Safety personnel evaluated adherence to ORM principles during mission planning, pre-flight briefings, and maintenance actions. Overall compliance with documented ORM procedures was satisfactory; inspectors observed consistent use of risk matrices and appropriate risk mitigation controls. Identified shortcomings included incomplete mitigation tracking in two squadrons and occasional lapses in documenting briefed hazards during high-tempo operations.

Corrective actions are underway: the Safety Office directed affected unit safety representatives to update their risk-tracking logs and conduct refresher ORM briefings by 16 June 2026. The Safety Office will also provide a brief on best practices at the next wing safety meeting and follow up with focused spot checks in July to verify sustained compliance. Please contact MAJ FELIX A. CHOI, Chief of Safety, at 366 FW/SE for questions or to coordinate support.

The Department of the Air Force directs a refreshed Close Air Support doctrine that aligns training, planning, and execution with current operational needs. This refresh emphasizes effects-based targeting, joint terminal attack controller integration, and rapid feedback loops to improve responsiveness for Allied airpower and joint maneuver. Commanders and staff should adopt updated procedures for CAS planning, execution, and assessment to ensure unity of effort in close support across all combatant commands.

Three lines of effort guide the refresh: doctrine clarity, interoperability with land forces, and sustainable, scalable readiness. Units should integrate updated CAS procedures into training cycles, wargames, and after-action reviews to ensure that air power remains responsive, proportional, and deliberate in support of mission objectives. A focus on risk management and safety remains foundational to all CAS operations.

This refresh also calls for improved coordination with joint, allied, and coalition partners to maximize the effectiveness of CAS in complex environments. Training and standard operating procedures will reflect current threats, terrain, and rules of engagement to ensure that close air support remains precise, predictable, and protective of friendly forces and civilians alike.

This memorandum announces a refresh of Close Air Support (CAS) doctrine to align employment concepts with emerging threat environments, joint force integration priorities, and advances in precision engagement capabilities. The refreshed doctrine will emphasize improved integration with ground maneuver elements, streamlined terminal attack control procedures, and expanded use of networked sensors and munitions to increase timeliness and reduce fratricide risk. Commands will retain tactical flexibility while adhering to standardized command-and-control constructs that support interoperability with joint and coalition partners.

AF/A3 directs ALMAJCOMs to review current tactics, techniques, and procedures for CAS employment and identify doctrinal, training, and equipment shortfalls by 15 January 2027. Submissions should include recommended changes to local training syllabi, required updates to joint terminal attack controller (JTAC) certification, and capability gaps affecting integration with distributed command-and-control architecture. Where appropriate, propose interim measures to mitigate identified risks pending formal incorporation into higher-level doctrine.

AF/A3 will consolidate inputs and publish a coordinated doctrine update and implementation plan by 31 March 2027. Fielding timelines, resource implications, and training guidance will accompany the update to ensure a deliberate transition that preserves combat readiness. Point of contact for this action is the CAS Doctrine Branch, AF/A3 Operations Directorate, at (703) 555-0100 or af.a3.cas-doctrine@us.af.mil.

2. During this period, suspend all local flying operations, simulator events, weapons loads, and aircraft maintenance actions that are not required for launch and recovery safety, emergency response, or commander-directed mission assurance tasks. Effective 0001 hours local time on April 20, 2026, direct a 48-hour safety down day for all 20th Operations Group flying and flying-related operations. This action follows the Class C mishap involving a 20th Operations Group aircraft and is intended to preserve operational focus, complete an initial safety assessment, and ensure all personnel understand and apply immediate risk controls.

During the safety down day, suspend all sortie generation and flight operations except those specifically approved by the 20th Fighter Wing Commander. Do not construe this direction as limiting emergency response, aircraft recovery, maintenance actions required to protect life or property, or other activities expressly approved by the Operations Group Commander in coordination with the 20th Fighter Wing Safety Office.

Direct each squadron commander to conduct a face-to-face safety stand-down before resuming normal operations. At a minimum, the stand-down will address mishap notification and reporting, hazard identification, risk management, aircraft and equipment status, supervision, and the duty to stop operations when conditions are unsafe. Ensure all aircrew, maintainers, and supporting personnel are included or receive an equivalent documented briefing before returning to duty.

Coordinate the stand-down plan and restart criteria with 20 FW/SE. Provide this headquarters a consolidated execution plan by 1600 hours local time on April 17, 2026, and a completion report, including unresolved hazards and recommended corrective actions, by 1600 hours local time on April 22, 2026. Request deviations or extensions through the 20th Fighter Wing Vice Commander before resuming affected operations.

Direct questions to the 20th Fighter Wing Safety Office at DSN 965-XXXX.

Effective upon receipt, direct a 48-hour safety down day for all 20th Operations Group flying operations following the Class C mishap involving an assigned F-16CM aircraft on 16 April 2026. The safety down day will begin at 0001 local time on 18 April 2026 and conclude at 2359 local time on 19 April 2026. No 20th Operations Group flight operations will be conducted during this period unless specifically authorized in writing by the 20th Fighter Wing Commander.

During the safety down day, accomplish the following actions:

- Conduct a command-directed safety stand-down for all Operations Group personnel, including aircrew, maintenance personnel, intelligence personnel, and supporting agencies. Emphasize mishap prevention, risk management, supervisory engagement, and strict adherence to technical data and established operating procedures.

- Complete a formal review of the mishap sequence, known hazards, applicable risk controls, and immediate lessons identified to date. Do not speculate on causation or assign blame; protect privileged safety information and coordinate all releasable information through the safety office and public affairs.

- Review the risk management worksheets and operational risk controls for the next scheduled flying period. $quill: usaf_memo@0.3.0
$kind: main
# U.S. Air Force and Space Force Official Memorandum
# Organization or office symbol, rendered in uppercase. To address a specific person, add their rank and name in parentheses: 'ORG/SYMBOL (LT COL JANE DOE)'. For a long list, enter 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' and name the recipients in the Distribution field.
memo_for: !must_fill # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
  - ORG1/SYMBOL
  - ORG2/SYMBOL
# The office symbol alone when every recipient is on this installation. The full mailing address as well when any recipient is elsewhere, so they can write back. Leave blank for a Memorandum for Record, which prints no FROM line.
# e.g. [ORG/SYMBOL, Organization Name, 123 Street Ave, City ST 12345-6789]
memo_from: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
# Keep it brief. Capitalize the first letter of each word except articles, prepositions, and conjunctions. Put any suspense date in parentheses. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. Subject of the Memorandum
subject: !must_fill # richtext(inline)<markdown>
# YYYY-MM-DD, printed in the format the Memo Style field selects. Leave blank to use today's date.
date: "" # date<YYYY-MM-DD>
# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.
# e.g. FOR THE COMMANDER
authority_line: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Line 1: Name in UPPERCASE as signed, grade, and service. Line 2: Duty title.
signature_block: !must_fill # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
  - FIRST M. LAST, Rank, USAF
  - Duty Title
# Letterhead lines, top to bottom, all rendered in uppercase. The first is the department title, set larger than the rest. Change that line only for a Joint Command or a DoW agency. The lines below it are your unit's full organization name.
# e.g. [DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE, "HEADQUARTERS [UNIT NAME]"]
letterhead_title: # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
  - DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE
# Department of War (DoW) or Department of Defense (DoD) seal, shown at the top left of the letterhead. Leave blank for no seal.
letterhead_seal: dow # enum<dow | dod>
# Bold-caps line below the seal. Nothing prints when it is blank, or when there is no seal.
letterhead_seal_subtitle: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Organizational motto, centered in the footer of every page. Supports Markdown emphasis: *italics*, **bold**.
tag_line: "" # richtext(inline)<markdown>
# Classification marking, banner-printed at the top and bottom of every page. Leave blank for no banner, which is what an unclassified document normally carries. Mark per DAFI 16-1404, DoDM 5200.48 for CUI, and applicable DoD guidance.
# when CUI: controlled_by, poc, category, limited_dissemination
classification: # enum<UNCLASSIFIED | CUI | CONFIDENTIAL | SECRET | TOP SECRET>
  value: ""
# Suffix appended to the banner after a double slash, rendered in uppercase: 'NF' prints as CUI//NF. Leave blank for no suffix.
dissemination: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Cite each reference by organization, type, date, and title. Two or more print as a References block lettered (a), (b), (c); a single one prints in parentheses after the subject, per AFH 33-337. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. ["AFMAN 33-326, 25 November 2011, *Preparing Official Communications*", "AFI 33-360, *Publications and Forms Management*"]
references: [] # array<richtext(inline)<markdown>>
# Offices or people receiving a courtesy copy, one per line.
# e.g. ["Rank and Name, ORG/SYMBOL"]
cc: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
# Every recipient, listed here when 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' stands in the Memo For field.
# e.g. [ORG1/SYMBOL, ORG2/SYMBOL]
distribution: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
# Attachments in the order the memo mentions them. Describe each briefly; do not write 'as stated' or abbreviate. A lone attachment prints unnumbered, two or more are numbered. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. ["Attachment description, YYYY MMM DD"]
attachments: [] # array<richtext(inline)<markdown>>
# USAF memorandum or DAF headquarters memorandum, per AFH 33-337. DAF dates as 'September 15, 2026' rather than '15 September 2026', and leaves top-level paragraphs unnumbered with a first-line indent.

# Organization or office symbol, rendered in uppercase. To address a specific person, add their rank and name in parentheses: 'ORG/SYMBOL (LT COL JANE DOE)'. For a long list, enter 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' and name the recipients in the Distribution field.

  - ORG2/SYMBOL

# Keep it brief. Capitalize the first letter of each word except articles, prepositions, and conjunctions. Put any suspense date in parentheses. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. Subject of the Memorandum
subject: !must_fill # richtext(inline)<markdown>
# YYYY-MM-DD, printed in the format the Memo Style field selects. Leave blank to use today's date.
date: "" # date<YYYY-MM-DD>
# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander.   - Duty Title
# Letterhead lines, top to bottom, all rendered in uppercase. The first is the department title, set larger than the rest. Change that line only for a Joint Command or a DoW agency. The lines below it are your unit's full organization name.
# e.g. [DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE, "HEADQUARTERS [UNIT NAME]"]
letterhead_title: # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>

This memorandum establishes procedures for receiving and responding to requests for medical records and related protected health information. Treat each request as Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and limit access, use, and disclosure to personnel with an official need to know.

Medical-group personnel will route every request to the 60 MDG HIPAA Privacy Officer before releasing records. The request package must identify the requester, the patient, the records sought, the intended recipient, and the legal or patient authorization supporting the request. Do not rely on an informal email, telephone statement, or unsupported claim of urgency as authority to disclose records.

The Privacy Officer will verify the requester's identity and authority, determine whether the requested disclosure is permitted, and document the decision in the request log. When authorization is incomplete, unclear, expired, or inconsistent with the request, pause processing and obtain clarification. Release only the minimum information necessary for the authorized purpose, unless a more restrictive rule applies.

Personnel will transmit approved records by an authorized method, confirm the recipient before transmission, and retain the request, authorization, approval, disclosure accounting, and transmission evidence in the designated record set. Do not place patient identifiers or unencrypted medical records in an unapproved collaboration site or personal email account.

Report suspected loss, misdirection, unauthorized access, or improper disclosure immediately to the Privacy Officer and the medical-group security manager. Preserve relevant messages and files, do not delete or alter evidence, and follow incident-response direction. Questions about a request or this memorandum should be directed to the 60 MDG HIPAA Privacy Officer.

Attachment:

> Request intake checklist and response worksheet, 2026 Feb 21

This memorandum directs a 48-hour safety stand-down for all 4th Fighter Wing flying and maintenance activities in response to the Class C mishap that occurred on 13 August 2026. The purpose of this action is to ensure immediate risk mitigation, reinforce adherence to applicable safety procedures, and identify corrective actions to prevent recurrence.

1. Effective 14 August 2026 at 0800 local, the 4th Fighter Wing will implement a 48-hour safety stand-down. During this period:

a. All flight operations will cease except for those missions required to preserve life, property, or national security and those specifically authorized in writing by the 4 FW/CC.

b. Maintenance and weapons activities will pause non-mission-essential tasks to permit focused safety reviews and revalidation of procedures.

c. Commanders, superintendents, and flight leads will ensure all assigned personnel attend the locally scheduled safety briefings. Briefings will cover the facts known to date, immediate hazards, lessons learned, and unit-specific risk mitigation measures.

2. Unit safety officers and flight safety representatives will complete the following deliverables prior to the end of the stand-down period and forward them to 4 FW/SE (office symbol: 4 FW/SE) by 16 August 2026 at 1200 local:

a. A unit After Action Report (AAR) summarizing findings, immediate corrective actions taken, and recommended follow-on actions.

b. A review of applicable technical orders, checklists, and local procedures influenced by the mishap, with any discrepancies documented and proposed corrections.

c. A roster of personnel who received the stand-down briefing and confirmation of completion for any mandated refresher training or computer-based training (CBT).

3. The wing mishap investigation board will continue investigative actions per applicable instructions. The stand-down does not replace the formal investigation; it is an immediate risk reduction measure. Units will preserve all evidence and documentation related to the mishap and coordinate with 4 FW/JA and 4 FW/SE for investigative guidance.

4. Command emphasis: commanders at all levels will use this stand-down to emphasize adherence to published procedures, the importance of briefing and cross-checking, and the imperative to report hazards and mishap precursors without fear of undue repercussion.

5. Points of contact: primary — 4 FW Safety (4 FW/SE), DSN 312-555-1234, civ: (123) 555-1234; secondary — 4 OG/DO, DSN 312-555-5678.

If you have questions or require additional guidance during the stand-down, contact 4 FW/CC's action cell at 4 FW/CC@usaf.mil.

JOHN A. DOE, Col, USAF Commander, 4th Fighter Wing

UNCLASSIFIED

This memorandum directs a 48-hour safety stand-down for all 4th Fighter Wing flying and maintenance activities in response to the Class C mishap that occurred on 13 August 2026. The purpose of this action is to ensure immediate risk mitigation, reinforce adherence to applicable safety procedures, and identify corrective actions to prevent recurrence.

1. Effective 14 August 2026 at 0800 local, the 4th Fighter Wing will implement a 48-hour safety stand-down. During this period:

a. All flight operations will cease except for those missions required to preserve life, property, or national security and those specifically authorized in writing by the 4 FW/CC.

b. Maintenance and weapons activities will pause non-mission-essential tasks to permit focused safety reviews and revalidation of procedures.

c. Commanders, superintendents, and flight leads will ensure all assigned personnel attend the locally scheduled safety briefings. Briefings will cover the facts known to date, immediate hazards, lessons learned, and unit-specific risk mitigation measures.

2. Unit safety officers and flight safety representatives will complete the following deliverables prior to the end of the stand-down period and forward them to 4 FW/SE (office symbol: 4 FW/SE) by 16 August 2026 at 1200 local:

a. A unit After Action Report (AAR) summarizing findings, immediate corrective actions taken, and recommended follow-on actions.

b. A review of applicable technical orders, checklists, and local procedures influenced by the mishap, with any discrepancies documented and proposed corrections.

c. A roster of personnel who received the stand-down briefing and confirmation of completion for any mandated refresher training or computer-based training (CBT).

3. The wing mishap investigation board will continue investigative actions per applicable instructions. The stand-down does not replace the formal investigation; it is an immediate risk reduction measure. Units will preserve all evidence and documentation related to the mishap and coordinate with 4 FW/JA and 4 FW/SE for investigative guidance.

4. Command emphasis: commanders at all levels will use this stand-down to emphasize adherence to published procedures, the importance of briefing and cross-checking, and the imperative to report hazards and mishap precursors without fear of undue repercussion.

5. Points of contact: primary — 4 FW Safety (4 FW/SE), DSN 312-555-1234, civ: (123) 555-1234; secondary — 4 OG/DO, DSN 312-555-5678.

If you have questions or require additional guidance during the stand-down, contact 4 FW/CC's action cell at 4 FW/CC@usaf.mil.

JOHN A. DOE, Col, USAF Commander, 4th Fighter Wing

UNCLASSIFIED

Per operational requirements to support upcoming deployment, the 88th Communications Squadron (88CS/COMM) is tasked to issue temporary SIPR tokens to 40 deploying maintenance personnel assigned to the 88th Maintenance Group (88MXG/MX). This authorized action will ensure secure access to SIPR networks during the deployment period.

The 88CS/COMM will coordinate directly with the 88MXG Maintenance Deployment Office to verify the identity and deployment status of each maintainer requiring a token. Tokens are to be activated no earlier than 10 days prior to deployment and deactivated upon redeployment unless extended authorization is granted.

The issuance process must adhere to all applicable cybersecurity policies and safeguards to protect classified information.

Per this memorandum, the Maintenance Squadron requests the 88th Communications Squadron issue temporary SIPR tokens to support an upcoming deployment.

1. Action. Issue 40 temporary SIPR tokens to the deploying maintainer roster provided at paragraph 2. Tokens will be configured for standard user access required by maintenance personnel to perform deployed mission-essential duties.

2. Details.

   a. Number of tokens: 40 (forty).

   b. Intended users: deploying maintainers assigned to the Maintenance Squadron. A roster with full names, ranks, and PII-free usernames will be provided to 88 CS/SC point of contact by the suspense below.

   c. Token duration: Temporary tokens valid for the duration of the deployment not to exceed 90 days unless otherwise coordinated and approved in writing by the Maintenance Squadron commander.

   d. Access level: Standard SIPR user accounts appropriate for maintenance and logistics functions. Do not grant elevated administrative privileges unless specifically requested in writing and approved by 88 CS leadership.

   e. Token distribution method: Coordinate issuance with the Maintenance Squadron POC listed at paragraph 4. Tokens may be distributed in-person at Wright-Patterson AFB or mailed to the deploying individual's official duty address per 88 CS policy.

3. Security and accountability.

   a. 88 CS/SC will record token serials, issuance dates, and recipient acknowledgment of receipt. Records will be retained for audit in accordance with applicable guidance.

   b. Recipients will be briefed on SIPR security responsibilities and reporting requirements for lost, stolen, or compromised tokens.

4. Point of contact. MAJ SARAH L. ANDERSON, Maintenance Squadron, commercial (937) 555-1234, sarah.anderson@wpafb.af.mil. Provide the final authorized roster and any special access requirements to this POC no later than the suspense date.

5. Suspense. Provide confirmation that all 40 temporary SIPR tokens have been issued and provide issuance records to the Maintenance Squadron POC by 2026-09-10.

6. Coordination. If 88 CS requires additional deconfliction, technical details, or approvals to meet this request, coordinate with the Maintenance Squadron POC at the earliest opportunity.

FOR THE MAINTENANCE SQUADRON

JOHN A. SMITH, Maj, USAF Commander, Maintenance Squadron

~~~

1. The 17th Fighter Squadron requests a waiver to the approved readiness training window in order to conduct its June 2026 integrated combat-turn training from June 22 through June 26, 2026. The requested waiver would permit execution during the final week of the month rather than the currently approved June 8 through June 19 window.

2. The squadron's primary instructor pilot will be unavailable during the approved window because of an assigned evaluation at the Air Force Weapons School. Rescheduling the training to the requested period preserves the required instructor-to-student ratio and prevents cancellation of the squadron's only available range complex reservation. The proposed training remains within all applicable flying-hour, crew-rest, safety, and airspace limitations.

3. The requested adjustment does not reduce required readiness standards. The squadron will complete a documented risk review before execution, maintain daily commander oversight, and report any schedule or safety deviation through the 432d Air Expeditionary Group. The attached Training Risk Mitigation Plan identifies controls, responsible personnel, and stop-training criteria.

4. I recommend approval of this waiver for the period June 22 through June 26, 2026. Approval will allow the squadron to meet its readiness objective without requesting additional resources or changing the authorized training syllabus.

5. Point of contact is Maj Jordan K. Ellis, 17 FS/DO, at (555) 410-0170 or jordan.ellis@us.af.mil.

~~~

from: 432 AEG/CC

  - Commander
format: separate_page
action: approve
~~~

1. I have reviewed the request and the attached risk mitigation plan. The requested training window is operationally justified, adequately controlled, and supports the group's readiness objectives.

2. The 432d Air Expeditionary Group endorses approval of the waiver for June 22 through June 26, 2026, and forwards the package to the 4th Air Force Wing for final action.

~~~
$kind: indorsement
from: 4 AFW/CC
for: 17 FS/CC

authority_line: ""

  - Commander
format: separate_page
action: approve
~~~

1. I have reviewed the squadron commander's request and the 432d Air Expeditionary Group indorsement. The operational need is valid, and the identified controls sufficiently mitigate the associated scheduling and training risks.

2. Approved. The 17th Fighter Squadron may conduct the integrated combat-turn training from June 22 through June 26, 2026, subject to all applicable safety, crew-rest, range, and airspace requirements. This approval applies only to the waiver requested in this package and does not alter other readiness or training obligations.

1. The 9th Flight Test Squadron requests a waiver to paragraph 5.2.2 of Department of the Air Force Instruction (DAFI) 36-2903, *Dress and Appearance*, to permit assigned aircrew members to wear an approved squadron morale patch on the right sleeve of the Operational Camouflage Pattern uniform during the 9th Flight Test Squadron's flight-test operations from June 15 through December 31, 2026.

2. The requested waiver supports safe and efficient flight-test operations at Edwards Air Force Base.  The patch provides an immediate visual identifier for test aircrew working across the 4120 Test Group's dispersed test areas and distinguishes them from maintenance, range, and contractor personnel during launch, recovery, and emergency-response activities.  The patch will be subdued, no larger than 3.5 inches in diameter, free of unauthorized text or imagery, and identical for all squadron aircrew.

3. The squadron will control the patch design and distribution through the first sergeant and operations superintendent.  Members will remove the patch before wearing the uniform outside approved flight-test operations or when directed by higher headquarters.  The squadron will review compliance monthly and terminate the practice immediately if it creates a standards, safety, or mission concern.

4. The waiver will not alter rank, name-tape, identification, safety-equipment, or grooming requirements.  The requested period will allow the squadron to evaluate the identifier during the 2026 flight-test cycle and provide the group commander a recommendation for permanent disposition.  The waiver request justification and risk mitigation plan is attached.

This memorandum documents receipt and initial handling guidance for a request for Protected Health Information (PHI) received by the 81st Medical Group (81 MDG) on 2026-09-01. The request seeks medical records for a current beneficiary and was submitted by a third party claiming legal authority to receive the records. The material at issue meets the definition of Controlled Unclassified Information — Privacy (CUI-P) and is subject to HIPAA and DoD/DAF CUI handling and disclosure rules.

1. Background. The Privacy Office received a signed records request on 2026-09-01 at 0905 local. The request includes patient identifiers and treatment information from medical encounters on 2025-11-10 and 2026-02-18. Supporting documentation accompanying the request alleges the third party holds a state court order; the Privacy Office has not yet validated the order.

2. Assessment and Legal Considerations.

a. Records that contain PHI are protected by the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) and qualifying DoD/DAF privacy and CUI policies. Disclosure outside the DoD or to third parties requires either the patient’s valid authorization, a statutory exception, or a valid court order. Absent an authorization or a validated order, release is prohibited.

b. The submitted court order appears to be outside our direct jurisdiction and contains redactions; Privacy and SJA coordination is required to determine its validity and scope. Any release must be the minimum necessary to satisfy the legal requirement and must follow CUI handling controls (marking, limited dissemination, secure transmission).

3. Actions Taken.

a. The Privacy Office placed a provisional hold on the requested records to prevent inadvertent release pending legal review.

b. The Privacy Office requested verification of the court order from the requesting party and asked for proof of identity and authority. That request for verification was sent on 2026-09-01 at 1015 local; no response has been received as of this memo date.

c. A request for legal review was submitted to Staff Judge Advocate (SJA) 81 ABW on 2026-09-01.

4. Required Recipient Actions.

a. Privacy Office (81 MDG): Continue to hold records and maintain chain-of-custody documentation. Do not disclose PHI until SJA completes its legal sufficiency review or a valid patient authorization is provided.

b. SJA (81 ABW): Provide written legal determination on the validity and scope of the submitted court order, and advise on whether disclosure is required and, if so, the minimum necessary content, authorized recipients, and acceptable secure transmission methods.

c. Requesting Office/Individual: Respond to Privacy Office request for verification within 7 calendar days. Failure to validate legal authority will result in denial of the disclosure request.

5. Point of Contact. For coordination and additional information, contact:

- Privacy Officer, 81st Medical Group

- Phone: (228) 377-XXXX

- Email: 81mdg.privacy@us.af.mil

6. Classification and Handling. This memorandum contains CUI-P. Mark and store attached records per DoDM 5200.48 and local CUI procedures. Limit dissemination to those with an operational need and CUI handling training. Do not transmit attachments via non-secure email. When release is authorized, use encrypted channels and document what was released, to whom, and under what authority.

7. Recommended Disposition. Retain this memorandum and associated records per DOD and DAF privacy recordkeeping requirements and local records disposition schedules. Coordinate final disposition with SJA and the base Records Management Office.

If you have questions or require further assistance, Privacy Office will coordinate with SJA and the applicable treatment teams to finalize the release decision.

Respectfully,

FIRST M. LAST, Col, USAF Commander, 81st Medical Group

1. Request: I request a waiver to authorize extended temporary duty (TDY) beyond 180 continuous days for Captain Sara L. Moreno, 23d Operations Squadron, to support an emergent Distributed Flight Operations (DFO) tasking in support of a joint exercise. The requested extension is from 2026-06-15 through 2026-12-15 (183 days), a 3-day extension beyond the 180-day regulatory limit.

2. Background: Capt Moreno was assigned TDY effective 2026-01-15 to provide instructor support and systems integration expertise for a coalition DFO event under Air Combat Command's Exercise STEADFAST COURIER. Ongoing operational requirements and candidate training schedule adjustments require Captain Moreno to remain to complete certification of adjacent instructor cadre and finalize network security testing.

3. Justification: Extending Capt Moreno's TDY by 3 days will:

- Ensure completion of instructor cadre certification, preventing loss of trained instructors and preserving training continuity for 4 follow-on student sorties.

- Allow closure of a critical cybersecurity risk item discovered during final interoperability testing, which cannot be mitigated remotely without rescheduling the coalition event.

- Avoid high impact to readiness and increased operational risk associated with backfilling a subject-matter expert on short notice.

4. Impact: Operational impact to 23d Operations Squadron is assessed as low: unit mission essential tasks remain covered by cross-trained personnel and planned shift adjustments. Estimated cost impact is limited to per diem adjustments for 3 additional days (approx. $180) and negligible travel surcharge.

5. Risk Mitigation: To mitigate personnel tempo and continuity risks, the following actions are in place:

- Primary and alternate instructor schedules adjusted to cover local sorties during Capt Moreno's absence.

- 72-hour handover with on-site briefings completed for all critical tasks prior to the originally scheduled return date.

- A contingency recall date of 2026-12-20 established should residual items remain unresolved.

6. Recommendation: I recommend approval of the 3-day waiver to extend Capt Sara L. Moreno's TDY beyond 180 days, from 2026-12-12 through 2026-12-15 (inclusive), to complete required certification and close interoperability test findings.

7. Point of contact for this request is the undersigned at (555) 555-1234 or james.harper@us.af.mil.

MEMORANDUM FOR: U.S. AIR FORCE ACC STAFFING OFFICE

FROM: 1st Fighter Squadron, Cannon AFB, NM

Major John Doe Squadron Commander 1st Fighter Squadron Cannon AFB, NM

Col. Jane Smith Vice Commander 12th Air Expeditionary Wing

2. Please proceed with the necessary adjustments.

**Signature:**

Maj. Gen. Alex Johnson Commander, Air Combat Command

letterhead_title:

letterhead_seal_subtitle: ""

tag_line: "*Integrity First*"

classification:

dissemination: ""

references: []

attachments: []

# e.g. [ORG/SYMBOL, Organization Name, 123 Street Ave, City ST 12345-6789]
memo_from: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
# Keep it brief. Capitalize the first letter of each word except articles, prepositions, and conjunctions. Put any suspense date in parentheses. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. Subject of the Memorandum
subject: !must_fill # richtext(inline)<markdown>
# YYYY-MM-DD, printed in the format the Memo Style field selects. Leave blank to use today's date.
date: "2026-07-02" # date<YYYY-MM-DD>
# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.
# e.g. FOR THE COMMANDER
authority_line: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Line 1: Name in UPPERCASE as signed, grade, and service. Line 2: Duty title.
signature_block: !must_fill # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
  - FIRST M. LAST, Rank, USAF
  - Duty Title
# Letterhead lines, top to bottom, all rendered in uppercase. The first is the department title, set larger than the rest. Change that line only for a Joint Command or a DoW agency. The lines below it are your unit's full organization name.
# e.g. [DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE, "HEADQUARTERS [UNIT NAME]"]
letterhead_title: # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
  - DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE
# Department of War (DoW) or Department of Defense (DoD) seal, shown at the top left of the letterhead. Leave blank for no seal.
letterhead_seal: dow # enum<dow | dod>
# Bold-caps line below the seal. Nothing prints when it is blank, or when there is no seal.
letterhead_seal_subtitle: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Organizational motto, centered in the footer of every page. Supports Markdown emphasis: *italics*, **bold**.
tag_line: "" # richtext(inline)<markdown>
# Classification marking, banner-printed at the top and bottom of every page. Leave blank for no banner, which is what an unclassified document normally carries. Mark per DAFI 16-1404, DoDM 5200.48 for CUI, and applicable DoD guidance.
# when CUI: controlled_by, poc, category, limited_dissemination
classification: # enum<UNCLASSIFIED | CUI | CONFIDENTIAL | SECRET | TOP SECRET>

# Suffix appended to the banner after a double slash, rendered in uppercase: 'NF' prints as CUI//NF. Leave blank for no suffix.
dissemination: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Cite each reference by organization, type, date, and title. Two or more print as a References block lettered (a), (b), (c); a single one prints in parentheses after the subject, per AFH 33-337. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. ["AFMAN 33-326, 25 November 2011, *Preparing Official Communications*", "AFI 33-360, *Publications and Forms Management*"]
references: [] # array<richtext(inline)<markdown>>
# Offices or people receiving a courtesy copy, one per line.

action: "" # enum<undecided | approve | disapprove>

# U.S. Air Force and Space Force Official Memorandum
# Organization or office symbol, rendered in uppercase. To address a specific person, add their rank and name in parentheses: 'ORG/SYMBOL (LT COL JANE DOE)'. For a long list, enter 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' and name the recipients in the Distribution field.
memo_for:
  - 366 FW/CC
  - 366 FW/SE
# The office symbol alone when every recipient is on this installation. The full mailing address as well when any recipient is elsewhere, so they can write back. Leave blank for a Memorandum for Record, which prints no FROM line.
# e.g. [ORG/SYMBOL, Organization Name, 123 Street Ave, City ST 12345-6789]
memo_from: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
# Keep it brief. Capitalize the first letter of each word except articles, prepositions, and conjunctions. Put any suspense date in parentheses. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. Subject of the Memorandum
subject: ORM Spot Check Results
# YYYY-MM-DD, printed in the format the Memo Style field selects. Leave blank to use today's date.
date: "2026-06-09"
# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.
# e.g. FOR THE COMMANDER
authority_line: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Line 1: Name in UPPERCASE as signed, grade, and service. Line 2: Duty title.
signature_block:
  - FELIX A. CHOI
  - Chief of Safety
# Letterhead lines, top to bottom, all rendered in uppercase. The first is the department title, set larger than the rest. Change that line only for a Joint Command or a DoW agency. The lines below it are your unit's full organization name.
# e.g. [DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE, "HEADQUARTERS [UNIT NAME]"]
letterhead_title:
  - DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE
# Department of War (DoW) or Department of Defense (DoD) seal, shown at the top left of the letterhead. Leave blank for no seal.
letterhead_seal: dow # enum<dow | dod>
# Bold-caps line below the seal. Nothing prints when it is blank, or when there is no seal.
letterhead_seal_subtitle: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Organizational motto, centered in the footer of every page. Supports Markdown emphasis: *italics*, **bold**.
tag_line: ""
# Classification marking, banner-printed at the top and bottom of every page. Leave blank for no banner, which is what an unclassified document normally carries. Mark per DAFI 16-1404, DoDM 5200.48 for CUI, and applicable DoD guidance.
# when CUI: controlled_by, poc, category, limited_dissemination
classification:
  value: ""
# Suffix appended to the banner after a double slash, rendered in uppercase: 'NF' prints as CUI//NF. Leave blank for no suffix.
dissemination: ""

# e.g. ["AFMAN 33-326, 25 November 2011, *Preparing Official Communications*", "AFI 33-360, *Publications and Forms Management*"]
references: []

# e.g. ["Rank and Name, ORG/SYMBOL"]
cc: []

distribution: []

Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. letterhead_seal_subtitle: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>

tag_line: "" # richtext(inline)<markdown>

dissemination: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>

The inspection identified several deficiencies that require corrective action by residents and oversight by squadron leadership.

- Report any barriers to compliance to the First Sergeant within 2 business days.

This memorandum serves to document the condition observed during the inspection and to outline necessary corrective steps. No endorsement is included in this document.

DORMITORY INSPECTION SUMMARY AND REQUIRED ACTIONS

I conducted a routine dormitory inspection of the 74th Wing Base Housing facilities on 2026-03-15. The purpose was to verify sanitation, safety, and general upkeep of living spaces in support of housing standards and occupant well-being. The inspection identified several deficiencies that require corrective action by residents and oversight by squadron leadership.

> Room 101 – Bedding not stored properly; visible dust and debris under beds; trash receptacle not emptied as required.
> Room 203 – Shared bathroom grout mold present; inadequate ventilation; cleaning schedule not posted or followed.
> Room 305 – Kitchenette counter surfaces dirty; dishes left in sink; food debris on floor near pantry.

Actions Required:
- Residents assigned to Rooms 101, 203, and 305 must perform immediate cleaning to standard within 7 days.
- Squadron leadership to verify completion and conduct a follow-up inspection by 2026-03-22.
- Reinforce dormitory cleanliness expectations during next housing briefing and post the updated cleaning schedule in each floor lounge.
- Report any barriers to compliance to the First Sergeant within 2 business days.

This memorandum serves to document the condition observed during the inspection and to outline necessary corrective steps. No endorsement is included in this document.

This memorandum documents the results of a scheduled dormitory inspection conducted on 12 March 2026 of facilities under the responsibility of the 123rd Force Support Squadron. The inspection assessed cleanliness, safety, fire prevention, and adherence to dormitory policies.

Summary of findings:

1. Overall condition of the dormitory common areas met standards; however, several individual rooms were found unsatisfactory and require corrective action by the occupiers.

2. Safety deficiencies observed included blocked egress in some rooms and one instance of an unauthorized space heater. These issues were documented and occupants were counseled on immediate corrective steps.

3. Fire prevention and electrical safety guidance was reinforced with occupants during the inspection. Room occupants with identified hazards were given written notice and a 48-hour suspense to correct conditions.

Lines listing the rooms found unsatisfactory are shown in the block quote below.

> Room 214 — personal items blocking egress at the doorway; multiple overloaded power strips observed. Room 307 — unauthorized electric space heater present; combustible materials stored against a heat source. Room 412 — excessive trash accumulation and food waste attracting pests; general sanitation standard not met.

Action taken:

- Occupants of the three rooms above were provided written notice and instructed to correct the identified deficiencies within 48 hours. Failure to correct deficiencies will result in referral to unit leadership for disciplinary action and possible housing relocation.

- Facilities Management was notified of minor maintenance items requiring attention (door threshold repair in Building 2, common-area light fixture replacement) and a work order was submitted.

Point of contact for this memorandum is the undersigned at (555) 123-4567 or john.harris@fictionalafb.af.mil.

FOR THE RECORD:

FIRST SGT JOHN D. HARRIS, USAF First Sergeant, 123rd Force Support Squadron

1. On 2026-04-02, during flightline operations, a near-miss occurred involving an AGE tug operating in the vicinity of aircraft turnaround activities.

2. The AGE tug was transiting along the flightline in support of equipment repositioning. At the same time, personnel were moving near the intended path of travel to support immediate aircraft servicing and readiness actions.

3. As the tug approached the area, the tug operator observed pedestrians and established immediate situational awareness through reduced speed and controlled repositioning. The pedestrians halted and maintained clearance from the tug’s path.

4. No injuries or equipment damage were reported. However, the event represents a potential collision risk due to reduced separation distance between the tug and foot traffic during concurrent mission support activities.

5. Witness roster (short):

> John P. Ramirez, TSgt, USAF\
> Emily S. Turner, SSgt, USAF\
> Michael D. Brooks, A1C, USAF

6. Immediate actions taken: tug operator increased lookout/visibility checks, slowed to walking speed when traversing near pedestrian activity, and confirmed clearances prior to proceeding. Supervisors reminded flightline personnel to maintain marked pedestrian routes and to verify approaching vehicle movement.

7. Recommendations:

- Reinforce use of designated pedestrian routes and positive clearance before crossing or operating near active vehicle corridors.

- Consider temporary marking or elevated visibility controls during peak concurrency periods when both foot traffic and vehicle operations occur in the same area.

- Review vehicle routing and right-of-way expectations for AGE tug operators and ground support personnel.

8. This memorandum documents the near-miss for safety awareness and corrective action tracking within the 1st Fighter Wing safety program.

body: |  
  The purpose of this memorandum is to task the 88th Air Base Wing to provide personnel support for the upcoming Cyber Defense Exercise CYBER FLAG 26 conducted by the 26th Network Operations Squadron (26 NOS).
  
  1. Purpose.
  
     Col PATRICE N. OKONKWO, Commander, directs the wing to provide two network defenders to the 26 NOS for CYBER FLAG 26.
  
  2. Required Action.
  
     The 88 ABW is tasked with providing the following billets in support of CYBER FLAG 26, with a suspense date of 15 May 2026:
  
     a. One billet, AFSC 1N4X1A (Cyber Warfare Operations).
  
     b. One billet, AFSC 17S (Cyber Warfare Operator).
  
  Please ensure these requirements are met by the suspense date stated above.  
~~~

- F-35A, tail number 17-5265—power and thermal management system component.

The following memorandum documents a near-miss incident on the flightline at the 1st Fighter Wing involving an Aircraft Generation Equipment (AGE) tug during routine operations on 2 April 2026. Immediate actions were taken to secure the area, investigate root causes, and prevent recurrence. The safety office has prepared this memorandum for record purposes to capture facts, witnesses, and preliminary conclusions.

Witness roster:

> Lt Col Marcus A. Bennett, USAF Capt Sophia R. Kim, USAF SrA Daniel J. Flores, USAF

The incident involved an AGE tug moving on the flightline when another aircraft taxied nearby, creating a close proximity risk to personnel and equipment. There were no injuries or damage reported. Contributing conditions included limited visibility due to morning light glare and a momentary miscommunication between flightline personnel and tug operators. Corrective actions include mandatory pre-move confirmations, reinforcing ground crew signaling protocols, and a brief refresher on flightline safety procedures.

Recommendations:

- Reinforce standard operating procedures for AGE tugs on the flightline.

- Require spotter presence during tug movement near aircraft operations.

- Schedule a flightline safety refresher training within the next 30 days.

Signature: AVERY CHEN, Maj, USAF Chief of Safety

On 2 April 2026 at approximately 0935 local, the 1st Fighter Wing Safety Office was notified of a near-miss incident on the flightline involving an Aerospace Ground Equipment (AGE) tug. The incident occurred at the west end of Taxiway B near Parking Apron 3. No injuries or aircraft damage were reported.

Preliminary facts:

- The AGE tug was conducting routine repositioning of support equipment. The tug operator reported loss of situational awareness while maneuvering in confined ramp space adjacent to an aircraft parked with its engines powered down.

- The aircraft remained stationary and engines were not running. Wing safety and AGE maintenance were alerted and responded to the scene.

- The tug came within approximately two feet of striking the aircraft main landing gear before the operator stopped and applied brakes.

Immediate corrective actions taken:

- The tug operator was removed from operations pending a supervisory interview and local retraining on ramp maneuvering and tow procedures.

- Maintenance and safety personnel conducted an immediate ramp safety brief for on-shift AGE crews reviewing clearance standards, spotter usage, and applicable local procedures.

- A safety investigation was initiated to determine root causes and recommend further corrective actions as required.

Witnesses (names and ranks):

> MAJ AVERY CHEN, Maj, USAF\
> TSGT MICHAEL RAMOS, TSgt, USAF\
> SRA LILA NGUYEN, SrA, USAF

A safety investigation will document findings, causal factors, and recommendations. The Safety Office requests that any additional witnesses or individuals with knowledge of the event contact the 1st Fighter Wing Safety Office at the earliest opportunity.

Respectfully submitted,

```

```

$kind: main
memo_for:
  - 4 FW/CC
memo_from: []
subject: Additional SOF Manning

# The office symbol alone when every recipient is on this installation. The full mailing address as well when any recipient is elsewhere, so they can write back. Leave blank for a Memorandum for Record, which prints no FROM line.
memo_from: []
# Keep it brief. Capitalize the first letter of each word except articles, prepositions, and conjunctions. Put any suspense date in parentheses. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. Subject of the Memorandum
subject: "Additional SOF Manning"
date: "2026-10-08"
# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.
authority_line: ""
# Line 1: Name in UPPERCASE as signed, grade, and service. Line 2: Duty title.
signature_block: !must_fill
  - FIRST M. LAST, Rank, USAF
  - Duty Title
# Letterhead lines, top to bottom, all rendered in uppercase. The first is the department title, set larger than the rest. Change that line only for a Joint Command or a DoW agency. The lines below it are your unit's full organization name.
# e.g. [DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE, "HEADQUARTERS [UNIT NAME]"]
letterhead_title:
  - DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE
# Department of War (DoW) or Department of Defense (DoD) seal, shown at the top left of the letterhead. Leave blank for no seal.
letterhead_seal: dow
# Bold-caps line below the seal. Nothing prints when it is blank, or when there is no seal.
letterhead_seal_subtitle: ""
# Organizational motto, centered in the footer of every page. Supports Markdown emphasis: *italics*, **bold**.
tag_line: ""
# Classification marking, banner-printed at the top and bottom of every page. Leave blank for no banner, which is what an unclassified document normally carries. Mark per DAFI 16-1404, DoDM 5200.48 for CUI, and applicable DoD guidance.
classification:
  value: ""
# Suffix appended to the banner after a double slash, rendered in uppercase: 'NF' prints as CUI//NF. Leave blank for no suffix.
dissemination: ""
# Cite each reference by organization, type, date, and title. Two or more print as a References block lettered (a), (b), (c); a single one prints in parentheses after the subject, per AFH 33-337. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
references: []
# Offices or people receiving a courtesy copy, one per line.
cc: []
# Every recipient, listed here when 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' stands in the Memo For field.
# e.g. [ORG1/SYMBOL, ORG2/SYMBOL]
distribution: []
# Attachments in the order the memo mentions them. Describe each briefly; do not write 'as stated' or abbreviate. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
attachments: []
# USAF memorandum or DAF headquarters memorandum, per AFH 33-337. DAF dates as 'September 15, 2026' rather than '15 September 2026', and leaves top-level paragraphs unnumbered with a first-line indent.
memo_style: usaf
# Body text size in points; decimals allowed, such as 11.5. AFH 33-337 §5 specifies 12.
font_size: 12

The 4th Fighter Wing concurs with the proposed increase in SOF personnel and recommends approval.
Action: APPROVE.

This memo provides an update regarding the staffing requirements for the Special Operations Forces.
Please review the enclosed information and proceed accordingly.

This memorandum provides the Aircraft Availability Briefing for the 56th Maintenance Group to inform 56 FW/CC of current mission-impacting maintenance status and parts shortages affecting sortie generation. The Maintenance Group continues to prioritize safety, sortie requirements, and depot-directed inspections while coordinating with logistics and supply chain partners to expedite critical components. An itemized list of aircraft currently down awaiting parts is provided below for situational awareness and planning.

Maintenance is actively working deferred discrepancies and sourcing replacement parts through AFLCMC channels and exchange agreements with sister units; estimated return-to-service dates remain dependent on part delivery and inspection outcomes. Command-directed priorities will be accommodated as parts become available. Current aircraft down for parts:

- F-16, tail 86-1234

- F-16, tail 88-1357

- F-16, tail 90-1420

This memorandum implements the standards in AFH 33-337, *The Tongue and Quill*, and directs revision of local preparatory letter templates and guidance to comply with the handbook.

1. Background. AFH 33-337 prescribes official correspondence format, grammar, and style that the Department expects across Air Force and Space Force communications. Conformance improves clarity, reduces coordination friction, and ensures uniform presentation of official actions.

2. Action. The 88 ABW/JA staff will review and rewrite all local preparatory letters, templates, and administrative correspondence guidance to align with AFH 33-337 standards. Revisions will address formatting, subject-line conventions, date formatting, signature blocks, citation style, and plain-language requirements.

3. Coordination and Submission. Forward revised templates and a brief implementation plan to 88 ABW/CC (88abw.cc@us.af.mil) for legal review and final approval. Provide initial submissions no later than 30 days from the date of this memorandum.

4. Point of Contact. The 88 ABW/JA point of contact for this action is the Chief of Legal Services, DSN 312-XXX-XXXX or commercial (XXX) XXX-XXXX.

COL LENA M. BROOKS, USAF Commander

88 MDG/SG is conducting a privacy review of the proposed transfer of outpatient records to a civilian hospital for continuity of care. The transfer will be limited to records necessary to support the patient’s treatment, and the receiving hospital will be provided only the information authorized for the stated medical purpose. Before release, the responsible personnel will verify the patient’s identity, confirm the receiving hospital and authorized point of contact, and document the applicable authorization or other legal basis for disclosure.

The transfer team will use approved transmission methods and will maintain an accounting of the records released, the recipient, the date, and the purpose of the disclosure. Any discrepancy, suspected unauthorized disclosure, or transmission error will be reported promptly through established privacy and health information management channels. Questions regarding this review or the required documentation should be directed to Capt Nina Volkov at DSN 787-4410 or nina.volkov@us.af.mil.

This memorandum notifies recipients of an immediate budget lock on Fiscal Year (FY) 27 Communications funds and provides guidance for required actions.

1. Background. Due to program execution reviews and pending higher headquarters allocation guidance, 42 CS is instituting a temporary freeze on obligating and committing FY27 Communications funds to ensure execution aligns with final allocations and priority mission requirements.

2. Effective Date. The FY27 Communications budget lock is effective immediately on the date of this memorandum and will remain in place until released in writing by 42 CS/CC or higher authority.

3. Impacted Actions. During the budget lock, units and activities must not:

- Initiate new purchases, contracts, or tasking actions that obligate FY27 Communications funds.

- Execute planned expenditures against FY27 Communications budgets unless specifically authorized in writing by 42 CS/CC.

4. Exceptions. Requests for exceptions to the budget lock (emergency mission-essential requirements only) must be submitted with justification and cost estimates to 42 CS/FM for coordination. Exception requests will be adjudicated on a case-by-case basis and require written approval from 42 CS/CC.

5. Required Coordination. Unit budget custodians and procurement personnel must coordinate with 42 CS/FM and 42 CS/CC for any questions regarding current obligations, planned expenditures, or to submit exception requests.

6. Point of Contact. For clarification or to submit an exception request, contact 42 CS/FM.

7. Closeout. This action is necessary to ensure FY27 Communications execution remains within authorized allocations and supports prioritized mission requirements. Further guidance will be provided when available.

AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.
# e.g. FOR THE COMMANDER
authority_line: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>

  - ALAN P. MORRIS, SES
  - Director of Cyberspace Operations
# Letterhead lines, top to bottom, all rendered in uppercase. The first is the department title, set larger than the rest. Change that line only for a Joint Command or a DoW agency. The lines below it are your unit's full organization name.
# e.g. [DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE, "HEADQUARTERS [UNIT NAME]"]
letterhead_title:

# Department of War (DoW) or Department of Defense (DoD) seal, shown at the top left of the letterhead. Leave blank for no seal.

# Bold-caps line below the seal. Nothing prints when it is blank, or when there is no seal.
letterhead_seal_subtitle: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Organizational motto, centered in the footer of every page. Supports Markdown emphasis: *italics*, **bold**.
tag_line: "" # richtext(inline)<markdown>

# Suffix appended to the banner after a double slash, rendered in uppercase: 'NF' prints as CUI//NF. Leave blank for no suffix.
dissemination: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>

1. Purpose. This memorandum establishes CTI sharing procedures for coalition partners to support approved intelligence collaboration while ensuring compliance with applicable CUI and CTI handling requirements.

2. Scope. This guidance applies to all CTI created, received, stored, transmitted, or shared by 67 CW/IN personnel and to coalition partner dissemination actions performed on behalf of 16 AF/A2.

3. Requirements.

a. Access and authorization.

```
(1) Share CTI only with coalition partners who have an approved need-to-know and a current authorization for CTI handling.
(2) Verify and document the partner’s authorization and the specific CTI categories being shared before release.
```

b. Marking.

```
(1) Ensure each CTI item is marked consistent with CTI requirements prior to release.
(2) Preserve all control markings, including NOFORN handling constraints, throughout transmission and receipt.
```

c. Transmission methods.

```
(1) Use approved secure channels and systems for all CTI transmissions to coalition partners.
(2) Do not transmit CTI via non-approved email, consumer messaging platforms, or removable media unless explicitly authorized by 67 CW/IN.
```

d. Downstream dissemination.

```
(1) Release CTI only to designated coalition offices or personnel identified in the approved sharing record.
(2) Do not allow coalition partners to further disseminate CTI without prior coordination with 67 CW/IN.
```

e. Storage and retention.

```
(1) Maintain CTI in approved systems and locations with appropriate access controls.
(2) Retain, sanitize, and dispose of CTI in accordance with the applicable retention and CUI disposition requirements.
```

4. Coordination and point of contact. For questions, sharing requests, or to request authorization for a coalition partner, contact Maj Owen Blake, DSN 312-555-0199, owen.blake@us.af.mil.

5. Effective date. This memorandum is effective upon receipt.

1. Purpose. This memorandum establishes CTI sharing procedures for coalition partners to support approved intelligence collaboration while ensuring compliance with applicable CUI and CTI handling requirements.

2. Scope. This guidance applies to all CTI created, received, stored, transmitted, or shared by 67 CW/IN personnel and to coalition partner dissemination actions performed on behalf of 16 AF/A2.

3. Requirements.

a. Access and authorization.

```
(1) Share CTI only with coalition partners who have an approved need-to-know and a current authorization for CTI handling.
(2) Verify and document the partner’s authorization and the specific CTI categories being shared before release.
```

b. Marking.

```
(1) Ensure each CTI item is marked consistent with CTI requirements prior to release.
(2) Preserve all control markings, including NOFORN handling constraints, throughout transmission and receipt.
```

c. Transmission methods.

```
(1) Use approved secure channels and systems for all CTI transmissions to coalition partners.
(2) Do not transmit CTI via non-approved email, consumer messaging platforms, or removable media unless explicitly authorized by 67 CW/IN.
```

d. Downstream dissemination.

```
(1) Release CTI only to designated coalition offices or personnel identified in the approved sharing record.
(2) Do not allow coalition partners to further disseminate CTI without prior coordination with 67 CW/IN.
```

e. Storage and retention.

```
(1) Maintain CTI in approved systems and locations with appropriate access controls.
(2) Retain, sanitize, and dispose of CTI in accordance with the applicable retention and CUI disposition requirements.
```

4. Coordination and point of contact. For questions, sharing requests, or to request authorization for a coalition partner, contact Maj Owen Blake, DSN 312-555-0199, owen.blake@us.af.mil.

5. Effective date. This memorandum is effective upon receipt.

Coalition partners may receive cyber threat intelligence (CTI) only when the information is authorized for release, the recipient has a validated mission need to know, and the disclosure complies with applicable policy, releasability determinations, and bilateral or multilateral agreements.

Personnel sharing CTI with coalition partners will:

- Verify the recipient’s identity, organization, and authorized communication channel before transmission.

- Confirm that the CTI is marked and handled as controlled unclassified information (CUI) and that the specific CTI category and dissemination restriction are preserved.

- Ensure the recipient is authorized to receive the information under the applicable disclosure authority and agreement.

- Remove information that is not releasable to the recipient and document any redactions or sanitization performed.

- Use approved systems and transmission methods. Do not transmit CTI through personal accounts, unapproved collaboration tools, or other unauthorized channels.

- Include the applicable CUI markings and handling instructions with every shared product or message.

- Record the date, recipient, transmitting organization, product or subject, authority for release, and method of transmission.

Before sharing CTI, the originator will coordinate any unresolved releasability, classification, or disclosure questions with 67 CW/IN. When the information includes another organization’s reporting or source-sensitive material, the originator will obtain the required originator-control or source-owner approval before release.

Recipients will protect the CTI in accordance with the handling instructions provided by 67 CW/IN, will not further disseminate it without authorization, and will promptly report suspected unauthorized disclosure, loss, or compromise through established command and security-reporting channels.

Questions about these procedures or requests for release authorization should be directed to Maj Owen Blake, DSN 312-555-0199, or owen.blake@us.af.mil.

- Record the date, recipient, transmitting organization, product or subject, authority for release, and method of transmission.

Recipients will protect the CTI in accordance with the handling instructions provided by 67 CW/IN, will not further disseminate it without authorization, and will promptly report suspected unauthorized disclosure, loss, or compromise through established command and security-reporting channels.

This memorandum outlines the Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) procedures established by 67 CW/IN for sharing Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) with coalition partners. These procedures are designed to ensure secure, authorized handling and dissemination of CTI in accordance with applicable directives and security protocols.

1. Sharing of CTI shall occur only with coalition partners who have been appropriately vetted and authorized to receive such information under current security agreements.

2. All CTI sharing activities must adhere to the NOFORN dissemination limitation, preventing further dissemination to foreign nationals unauthorized by this memorandum.

3. Requests for CTI from coalition partners require validation by 67 CW/IN. The point of contact for validation and coordination is Maj Owen Blake, DSN 312-555-0199, owen.blake@us.af.mil.

4. All shared CTI must be marked with the appropriate CUI banner and include this memorandum’s classification markings to ensure proper handling.

5. Recipients of CTI are responsible for safeguarding the information in accordance with CUI requirements and reporting any unauthorized disclosures immediately.

Continued compliance with these procedures is essential to maintaining coalition trust and operational security.

If there are any questions regarding this memorandum or the sharing procedures, please contact 67 CW/IN directly.
